entries.definition: The gases surrounding the Earth or any astronomical body.
entries.example: We may smile now to hear witchcraft spoken seriously of; but we forget perhaps that a belief in it is like a belief in the after appearance of the dead among the blue waters, the green graves, the still starry atmosphere and the great shadowy woods of our earth; […]

entries.definition: All the liquid waters of the Earth or another astronomical body, as distinguished from the land and the gases of the atmosphere.
entries.example: The hydrosphere includes the water in lakes, rivers, and oceans.

entries.definition: The rigid, mechanically strong, outer layer of the Earth, which is divided into twelve major tectonic plates.
entries.example: Holonyms: Earth, earth

entries.definition: The chemical element (symbol O) with an atomic number of 8 and relative atomic mass of 15.9994. It is a colorless and odorless gas. Sometimes called elemental oxygen to distinguish it from molecular oxygen.
entries.example: Holonyms: dioxygen, O₂, oxygen (loose sense)

entries.definition: A binary chemical compound of oxygen with another chemical element.
entries.example: Most metals, when subjected to heat until they become melted, combine with oxygen of the atmosphere, and form what are called oxides.

entries.definition: The normal oxide of carbon, CO₂; a colorless, odorless gas formed during respiration and combustion and consumed by plants during photosynthesis.
entries.example: There were dozens of presentations in 2008, including: […

entries.definition: The lightest chemical element (symbol H), with an atomic number of 1 and atomic weight of 1.008.
entries.example: Our professor then reminded us that a hydrogen ion is merely a proton, and thus we should think about acid-base theory as we consider this problem further.

entries.definition: In general usage, an essential part of a thing surrounded by other essential things.
entries.example: the core of an apple or quince

entries.definition: A more solid, dense or hard layer on a surface or boundary.
entries.example: A hard crust formed on the soil after several hot days.

entries.definition: A piece of clothing somewhat like an open robe or cloak, especially that worn by Orthodox bishops.
entries.example: The people of the village all said, "It could be none but the good-natured Dwarfs, who come by night tripping along with their feet covered with long mantles, as light as birds, and industriously perform for mankind their daily work."

entries.definition: Angular distance measured west or east of the prime meridian.
entries.example: But was it responsible governance to pass the Longitude Act without other efforts to protect British seamen? Or might it have been subterfuge—a disingenuous attempt to shift attention away from the realities of their life at sea.

entries.definition: The angular distance north or south from a planet's equator, measured along the meridian of that particular point.
entries.example: The oat is hardier than wheat, and ripens in higher latitudes.

entries.definition: The visible horizontal line (in all directions) where the sky appears to meet the earth in the distance.
entries.example: A tall building was visible on the whole sweep of the horizon.

entries.definition: The absolute height of a location, usually measured from sea level.
entries.example: As the altitude increases, the temperature gets lower, so remember to bring warm clothes to the mountains.

entries.definition: An unexpected natural or man-made catastrophe of substantial extent causing significant physical damage or destruction, loss of life or sometimes permanent change to the natural environment.
entries.example: People would suffer disasters when society's morality degenerates.

entries.definition: An accident, mistake, or problem.
entries.example: Since the mishap with the banana peel, he watches his step.

entries.definition: Causing extremely serious damage or suffering.
entries.example: The earthquake caused catastrophic damage to the coastal town.

entries.definition: An event resulting in great loss.
entries.example: Romeo come forth / Come forth thou fearfull man, / Affliction is enamor’d of thy parts: / And thou art wedded to calamitie.

entries.definition: To put (someone or something) in danger; to risk causing harm to.
entries.example: I hold him but a fool that will endanger / His body [in a duel] for a girl that loves him not

entries.definition: Non-Oxford British English standard spelling of jeopardize.
entries.example: MIT professor behind influential letter says unchecked development is allowing a few AI firms to jeopardise society’s future.

entries.definition: Causing destruction; damaging.
entries.example: The pastures are filled with gay political drop-outs, persons of reasonable intent who found the scene personally destructive.

entries.definition: An irregular climate pattern involving unusually warm surface water in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean.
entries.example: El Nino can bring unusually wet weather to some regions.
entries.usage: Usually written El Niño; the source form omits the accent.

entries.definition: A building used to grow plants, particularly one with large glass windows or plastic sheeting to trap heat from sunlight even in intemperate seasons or climates.
entries.example: The royal party had dined in the greenhouse, the coup d'œil of which was as striking as it was new. Vast stands of the most costly exotics reached to the glass roof, which was partly covered by a luxuriant vine, or by a small scarlet creeper.

entries.definition: A thing or being, event or process, perceptible through senses; or a fact or occurrence thereof.
entries.example: The year 1866 was signalised by a remarkable incident, a mysterious and inexplicable phenomenon, which doubtless no one has yet forgotten.

entries.definition: A small stone, especially one rounded by the action of water.
entries.example:
Then let the pebbles on the hungry beach
Fillip the stars;

entries.definition: A piece of material that attracts some metals by magnetism.
entries.example: The magnet picked up the steel paper clips but left the plastic buttons behind.

entries.definition: Rock or other material that contains valuable or utilitarian materials; primarily a rock containing metals or gems for which it is typically mined and processed.
entries.example: They general­ly occur in the earth in what are called veins, and are seldom found in the pure metallic state, but generally in combination with some other substance, in which state they are call­ed ores.

entries.definition: Any naturally occurring solid material that has a (more or less) definite chemical composition and characteristic physical properties; especially, an inorganic and crystalline one.
entries.example: The physiology of matter in the abstract is dynamical, that of mineral species is both dynamical and chemical, while that of organized forms is at once dynamical, chemical, and biotical.

entries.definition: A metamorphic rock of crystalline limestone.
entries.example: Open thy marble jaws, O tomb / And hide me, earth, in thy dark womb.

entries.definition: The most abundant mineral on the earth's surface, of chemical composition silicon dioxide, SiO₂. It occurs in a variety of forms, both crystalline and amorphous. Found in every environment.
entries.example: The telescope and collimator have each an object-glass consisting of a single lens of quartz 1½ inch diameter and a focal length of 18½ inches for the sodium yellow light, but not more than 16 inches for the highest rays measured.

entries.definition: A group of igneous and plutonic rocks composed primarily of feldspar and quartz. Usually contains one or more dark minerals, which may be mica, pyroxene, or amphibole. Granite is quarried for building stone, road gravel, decorative stone, and tombstones. Common colors are gray, white, pink, and yellow-brown.
entries.example: Many monuments sold in the US are crafted from granite produced in China, India and elsewhere overseas, while a lot of stone-working equipment comes from Europe.

entries.definition: A strong, abrupt rush of wind.
entries.example: The maximum sustained winds recorded at Waglan Island, Tate’s Cairn and Cheung Chau Beach were 113, 101 and 97 kmh (70, 62, 60 mph) respectively, with maximum gusts 135, 154 and 130 kmh (84, 96, 81 mph)

entries.definition: A light, gentle wind.
entries.example: The breeze rustled the papers on her desk.

entries.definition: Any of a number of winds associated with regions where most rain falls during a particular season.
entries.example: The monsoon brings heavy rain to the region each summer.

entries.definition: A very strong wind, more than a breeze, less than a storm; number 7 through to 9 winds on the 12-step Beaufort scale.
entries.example: It's blowing a gale outside.

entries.definition: A severe tropical cyclone; an intense storm rotating around a central eye.
entries.example: Whole villages have been leveled by the hurricane coastal residents braced for.

entries.definition: A violent wind in the form of a mobile, rapidly rotating, funnel cloud that has contacted the ground.
entries.example: An extreme version of vorticity is a vortex. The vortex is a spinning, cyclonic mass of fluid, which can be observed in the rotation of water going down a drain, as well as in smoke rings, tornados and hurricanes.

entries.definition: A severe tropical cyclone; an intense, rotating storm.
entries.example: The typhoon damaged homes along the coast.

entries.definition: A vent or fissure on the surface of a planet (usually in a mountainous form) with a magma chamber attached to the mantle of a planet or moon, periodically erupting forth lava and volcanic gases onto the surface.
entries.example: Iceland's volcanoes are among the most active on Earth.

entries.definition: To eject something violently (such as lava or water, as from a volcano or geyser).
entries.example: The volcano erupted, spewing lava across a wide area.

entries.definition: A mixture of molten silicate rock, crystals, and gas within the earth, which may be erupted as lava or cool in place to form igneous intrusions.
entries.example: By the pathside, there are occasional large boulders that shown black crystals the size of a fingernail; these are pyroxene minerals that had time to crystallise out deep within the chamber of liquid rock – or magma – beneath the volcano.

entries.definition: Of, or relating to the conversion of heat into other forms of energy.
entries.example: The locomotive is designed to give a high and sustained tractive effort at moderate speed on steep gradients. To attain this result, M. Chapelon, in experiments dsting back to 1940, aimed at improving the thermodynamic efficiency.

entries.definition: A noxious mixture of particulates and gases that is the result of urban air pollution.
entries.example: A widow since 1967, she lives now in Honolulu because, she says, she can enjoy the Californialike climate without the smog.

entries.definition: A gas or vapour/vapor that is strong-smelling or dangerous to inhale.
entries.example: Don't stand around in there breathing the fumes while the adhesive cures.

entries.definition: Water or other liquid finely suspended in air. (Compare fog, haze.)
entries.example: It was difficult to see through the morning mist.

entries.definition: A very large and destructive wave, generally caused by a tremendous disturbance in the ocean, such as an undersea earthquake or volcanic eruption; often a series of waves (a wave train).
entries.example: A tsunami struck Japan recently.

entries.definition: A long period with little or no rain.
entries.example: The prolonged drought reduced crop yields across the region.
entries.usage: Typical combinations: severe drought, prolonged drought, drought conditions.

entries.definition: Covering or filling an area with water.
entries.example: Water is flooding the basement after the pipe burst.

entries.definition: A violent flow, as of water, lava, etc.; a stream suddenly raised and running rapidly, as down a precipice.
entries.example: Rain fell on the hills in torrents.

entries.definition: A shaking of the ground, caused by volcanic activity or movement around geologic faults.
entries.example: Her alablaster brest she soft did kis, / Which all that while shee felt to pant and quake, / As it an Earth-quake were: at last she thus bespake.

entries.definition: Related to, or caused by an earthquake or other vibration of the Earth.
entries.example: seismic activity

entries.definition: A large mass or body of snow and ice sliding swiftly down a mountain side, or falling down a precipice.
entries.example: They were drinking from a fountain / That was pouring like an avalanche / Coming down the mountain

entries.definition: An area of land or its physical features.
entries.example: The hikers crossed rough terrain before reaching the valley.

entries.definition: A portion of land or territory as defined by its landform, its geographical (and architectural) features.
entries.example: Piſcat[or]. [...] [T]heſe Hills though high, bleak, and craggy, breed and feed good Beef, and Mutton above ground, and afford good ſtore of Lead within. / Viat[or]. They had need of all thoſe commodities to make amends for the ill Land-ſchape: [...]

entries.definition: One of the main contiguous landmasses, separated by water or geological features, on the surface of a planet, sometimes including its continental shelves and the islands on them.
entries.example:
But I should turn mine ears and hear
The moanings of the homeless sea,
⁠The sound of streams that swift or slow
⁠Draw down Æonian hills, and sow
The dust of continents to be; […]

entries.definition: Impossible to avoid or prevent.

entries.definition: Incapable of being reversed or turned about or back; incapable of being made to run backwards.

entries.definition: In an irregular manner; without rule, method, or order.

entries.definition: Not appropriate; not suitable for the situation, time, or place.

entries.definition: Not conforming to rule or system; deviating from the usual or normal type.

entries.definition: A collection of small particles, particularly dirt, that precipitates from a river or other body of water.

entries.definition: Mud or fine earth deposited from running or standing water.

entries.definition: Covered or splashed with, or full of, mud (“wet soil”).

entries.definition: A mineral substance made up of small crystals of silica and alumina, that is ductile when moist; the material of pre-fired ceramics.

entries.definition: Soil or earth.

entries.definition: Connected with the countryside.
entries.example: The programme brings broadband services to rural communities.

entries.definition: The area surrounding a city or town; suburb.

entries.definition: At a distance; disconnected.

entries.definition: Deserted and devoid of inhabitants.

entries.definition: Far off (physically, logically or mentally).

entries.definition: Lying next to, close, or contiguous; neighboring; bordering on.

entries.definition: Having a chemical nature that is harmful to health or lethal if consumed or otherwise entering into the body in sufficient quantities.

entries.definition: Physical contamination, now especially the contamination of the environment by harmful substances, or by disruptive levels of noise, light etc.

entries.definition: A substance that makes air, water or land dirty or harmful.

entries.definition: To make something dangerous or toxic by introducing impurities or foreign matter.

entries.definition: The science that studies the structure of the Earth (or other planets), together with its origin and development, especially by examination of its rocks.
entries.example: She studies geology to understand how mountains and rocks form.

entries.definition: The line or frontier area separating political or geographical regions.

entries.definition: The edge of the paper, typically left blank when printing but sometimes used for annotations etc.

entries.definition: A decorative border.

entries.definition: A slightly curved but almost flat dish from which food is served or eaten.

entries.definition: Rubble, wreckage, scattered remains of something destroyed.

entries.definition: To form cracks.

entries.definition: An opening in anything, made by breaking or parting.

entries.definition: Possessing or displaying splendor; shining; very bright.

entries.definition: Large, senior (high-ranking), intense, extreme, or exceptional

entries.definition: Grand, elegant or splendid in appearance.

entries.definition: Of excellent quality, superfine.

entries.definition: Arousing or holding the attention or interest of someone.

entries.definition: Of or relating to the drama.

entries.definition: Uncultivated and unsettled land in its natural state inhabited by wild animals and with vegetation growing wild; (countable) a tract of such land; a waste or wild.

 VVearie your ſelues in vvandring deſert vvayes […]

entries.definition: Not bearing children, childless; hence also unable to bear children, sterile.

entries.definition: Of land, etc.: capable of growing abundant crops; productive.

entries.definition: To add nutrients to soil or plants to support growth.

entries.definition: Of or pertaining to the sun; proceeding from the sun.

entries.definition: Of, pertaining to, or resembling the Moon (that is, Luna, the Earth's moon).

entries.definition: Any system by which time is divided into days, weeks, months, and years.

entries.definition: The time of day when the sun appears above the eastern horizon.
entries.example: I'll meet you at the docks at sunrise.

entries.definition: The moment each evening when the sun disappears below the western horizon.

entries.definition: An alignment of astronomical objects whereby one object comes between the observer (or notional observer) and another object, thus obscuring the latter.
entries.example: Special glasses protected our eyes during the solar eclipse.

entries.definition: Tending to darkness or blackness; moderately dark or black; dusky.

entries.definition: The sky, especially when described poetically as the heavens.

entries.definition: The place where sanctified souls are believed to live after death.

entries.definition: A large, naturally-occurring cavity formed underground or in the face of a cliff or a hillside.

entries.definition: A vertical (or nearly vertical) rock face.
entries.example: , scar

entries.definition: A large body of ice which flows under its own mass, usually downhill.

entries.definition: An area of wet (water-saturated), spongy (soft) land, often with trees, generally a rich ecosystem for certain plants and animals but ill-suited for many agricultural purposes. (A type of wetland. Compare marsh, bog, fen.)

entries.definition: Land formed from sediment deposited where a river enters a sea or lake.
entries.example: The river divides into several channels across its delta.

entries.definition: Simple, unaltered.

entries.definition: A period or level at which change stops after a rise.

entries.definition: A spring of fresh water, surrounded by a fertile region of vegetation, in a desert.

entries.definition: Any spherical (or nearly spherical) object.

entries.definition: One half of Earth, such as the Northern or Southern Hemisphere.

entries.definition: An imaginary great circle around Earth, equidistant from the two poles, and dividing earth's surface into the northern and southern hemispheres.

entries.definition: Relating to Antarctica or its surrounding region.

entries.definition: Originally, a stick; now specifically, a long and slender piece of metal or (especially) wood, used for various construction or support purposes.

entries.definition: Of or relating to the North Pole or the South Pole.

entries.definition: An imaginary line around which an object spins (an axis of rotation) or is symmetrically arranged (an axis of symmetry).
entries.example: A doorknob of whatever roundish shape is effectively a continuum of levers, with the axis of the latching mechanism—known as the spindle—being the fulcrum about which the turning takes place.

entries.definition: To make worse; to make inferior in quality or value; to impair.

entries.definition: To make (an offence) worse or more severe; to increase in offensiveness or heinousness.

entries.definition: To lower in value or social position.

entries.definition: An upward grade or slope.

entries.definition: To wear away by abrasion, corrosion, or chemical reaction.
entries.example: The cliff is gradually being eroded by the waves.

entries.definition: Of or pertaining to the Mediterranean Sea and its surrounding region.

entries.definition: The Atlantic Ocean.

entries.definition: Calm, peaceful.

entries.definition: One of the large bodies of water separating the continents.
entries.example: The ship crossed the ocean in twelve days.

entries.definition: Belonging to or characteristic of the sea; existing or found in the sea; formed or produced by the sea.

Terrestrial bacteria and fungi which can manage this trick are already familiar to experts in the field. Dr Mincer and Dr Amaral-Zettler found evidence of them on their marine plastic, too.

entries.definition: The theory, practice and technology of charting a course for a road vehicle, ship, aircraft, or spaceship.
entries.example: An ocean-going yachtsman must be competent at night navigation

entries.definition: A hollow place in the earth; an abyss; a deep chasm or basin.

entries.definition: The shore of a body of water, especially when sandy or pebbly.

And, back of the lawn, was a big, old-fashioned house, with piazzas stretching in front of it, and all blazing with lights. 'Twas the house I'd seen the roof of from the beach.

entries.definition: The edge of the land where it meets an ocean, sea, gulf, bay, or large lake.

entries.definition: Land adjoining a non-flowing body of water, such as an ocean, lake or pond.

entries.definition: The daily fluctuation in the level of the sea caused by the gravitational influence of the moon and the sun.

entries.definition: The generally unidirectional movement of a gas or fluid.

entries.definition: To bear; endure; support; put up with; tolerate.

entries.definition: Having little depth; significantly less deep than wide.

entries.definition: Existing, occurring, or located on the surface.

entries.definition: Having no variations in height.

entries.definition: Covered with sand.

entries.definition: As hard as stone.

entries.definition: Standing, pointing, or moving straight up or down; parallel to the local direction of gravity; along the direction of a plumb line; perpendicular to something horizontal.

entries.definition: Of a near-vertical gradient; of a slope, surface, curve, etc. that proceeds upward or downward at an angle approaching vertical.

entries.definition: Equally distant from one another at all points.

entries.definition: Having a small width; not wide; having opposite edges or sides that are close, especially by comparison to length or depth.
entries.example: a narrow hallway

entries.definition: A continental region composed of the islands of the central and southern Pacific Ocean, principally divided into Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia.

entries.definition: The continent; the principal land, as distinguished from islands or a peninsula.
