entries.definition: To raise or rise.
entries.example: The fog eventually lifted, leaving the streets clear.

entries.definition: A seat, especially for one person and without armrests.
entries.example: She sat on a stool beside the kitchen counter.

entries.definition: An open-topped box that can be slid in and out of the cabinet that contains it, used for storing clothing or other articles.
entries.example: He knelt down and began shoving the drawer into the slot; the rail was misaligned so he banged it with the heel of his hand. It stuck.

entries.definition: A cloth-covered frame used for protection against rain or sun.
entries.example: Quick, grab that umbrella before you get rained on!

entries.definition: A waterproof coat to be worn in the rain; (loosely) any coat or jacket with this purpose.
entries.example: After standing around in talk for a while, during which time Doris arrived with my hat and raincoat (left with her at the site) we made our way some two hundred strong, up the gracious stone stairway to the Hall of Christ Church, loaned by that College for the celebrationary lunch.

entries.definition: An instrument used to remove mud or other material from the bottom of water.
entries.example: The dredge removed sediment from the harbour.

entries.definition: To know how to.
entries.example: She can speak English, French, and German.

entries.definition: A grinding apparatus for substances such as grains, seeds, etc. (Some are small and simple, and some are large and complex.)
entries.example: Pepper has a stronger flavor when it is ground straight from a mill.

entries.definition: A furnace or hearth where metals are heated prior to hammering them into shape.
entries.example: Close to the hump-backed bridge on the lane leading into the Hambleden Valley is a mid-19th-century smithy, its inside walls hung with tools of the blacksmith's trade, though decorative wrought-ironwork is now the main product from its glowing forge.

entries.definition: A metal that is a combination of two or more elements, at least one of which is a metal, a base metal.
entries.example: Brass is an alloy containing copper and zinc.

entries.definition: Chemical elements or alloys, their ores, and the mines where their ores come from.
entries.example: Manganism has been known about since the 19th century, when miners exposed to ores containing manganese, a silvery metal, began to totter, slur their speech and behave like someone inebriated.

entries.definition: A common, inexpensive metal, silvery grey when untarnished, that rusts, is attracted by magnets, and is used in making steel: a chemical element having atomic number 26 and symbol Fe.
entries.example: Today we studied about metals — including iron — at school.

entries.definition: A heavy, pliable, inelastic metal element, having a bright, bluish color, but easily tarnished; both malleable and ductile, though with little tenacity. It is easily fusible, forms alloys with other metals, and is an ingredient of solder and type metal. Atomic number 82.
entries.example: The old pipe was made of lead.

entries.definition: A metallic alloy of copper and zinc used in many industrial and plumbing applications.
entries.example: The door handle is made of polished brass.

entries.definition: A naturally occurring or man-made alloy of copper, usually in combination with tin, but also with one or more other metals.
entries.example: How little gives thee joy or pain; A print, a bronze, a flower, a root.

entries.definition: A powdered substance produced by firing (calcining) calcium carbonate (limestone) and clay that develops strong cohesive properties when mixed with water. The main ingredient of concrete.
entries.example: In the autumn there was a row at some cement works about the unskilled labour men. A union had just been started for them and all but a few joined. One of these blacklegs was laid for by a picket and knocked out of time.

entries.definition: Any inorganic material containing calcium, usually calcium oxide (quicklime) or calcium hydroxide (slaked lime).
entries.example: Lime, which is the product of the burning of chalk or limestone, might be bought ready burnt, or it could be burnt in kilns specially constructed in the neighbourhood of the building operations.

entries.definition: A paste applied to the skin for healing or cosmetic purposes.
entries.example:
Then Jill came in,
And she did grin,
To see Jack's paper plaster;
Her mother whipt her,
Across her knee,
For laughing at Jack's disaster.

entries.definition: A tough material produced from the skin of animals, by tanning or similar process, used e.g. for clothing; often denotes leather from cattle when no qualifier specifies otherwise.
entries.example: The bag is made of soft brown leather.

entries.definition: A synthetic, solid, hydrocarbon-based polymer, whether thermoplastic or thermosetting.
entries.example: Plastics are energy-rich substances, which is why many of them burn so readily. Any organism that could unlock and use that energy would do well in the Anthropocene. Terrestrial bacteria and fungi which can manage this trick are already familiar to experts in the field. Dr Mincer and Dr Amaral-Zettler found evidence of them on their marine plastic, too.

entries.definition: A single piece of a given material, elongated and roughly round in cross-section, often twisted with other fibres to form thread.
entries.example: The microscope showed several different fibres stuck to the sole of the shoe.

entries.definition: The physical material of a building.
entries.example: This church dates back to the 11th century, though the great majority of its fabric is fifteenth century or later.

entries.definition: To turn thread or yarn into a piece of fabric by forming loops that are pulled through each other. This can be done by hand with needles or by machine.
entries.example: to knit a stocking

entries.definition: To form something by passing lengths or strands of material over and under one another.
entries.example: This loom weaves yarn into cloth.

entries.definition: A type of coarse cloth, woven from hemp (traditionally) or from cotton and polyesters, useful for making sails, tents, and overcoats or as a surface for paintings.
entries.example: The term canvas is very widely used, as well to denote the coarse fabrics employed for kitchen use, as for strainers, and wraps for meat, as for the best quality of ordinary table and shirting linen.

entries.definition: Thread or cloth made from flax fiber.
entries.example: Here, in the transept and choir, where the service was being held, one was conscious every moment of an increasing brightness; colours glowing vividly beneath the circular chandeliers, and the rows of small lights on the choristers' desks flashed and sparkled in front of the boys' faces, deep linen collars, and red neckbands.

entries.definition: Soft fibres from the cotton plant, used to make thread and cloth.
entries.example: This shirt is made from cotton.

entries.definition: A strong synthetic polymer used to make fibres, fabric, and other products.
entries.example: The nylon rope resisted water and dried quickly.

entries.definition: Wood sawn into planks or otherwise prepared for sale or use, especially as a building material.
entries.example: Here they live by fishing on the most plentiful coasts in the world; there they fell trees, by the sides of large rivers, for masts and lumber […].

entries.definition: Made of wood.
entries.example: a wooden boat

entries.definition: That or those belonging to me.
entries.example: The house itself is mine, but the land is not.

entries.definition: A hole in the ground.
entries.example: The meadow around the town is full of old pits.

entries.definition: Substance consumed to provide energy through combustion, or through chemical or nuclear reaction.
entries.example: More than a mere source of Promethean sustenance to thwart the cold and cook one's meat, wood was quite simply mankind's first industrial and manufacturing fuel.

entries.definition: To make slippery or smooth (normally to minimize friction) by applying a lubricant.
entries.example: If your bicycle chain is squeaking you should lubricate it.

entries.definition: A glimmering glass-like mineral that is an allotrope of carbon in which each atom is surrounded by four others in the form of a tetrahedron.
entries.example: The saw is coated with diamond.

entries.definition: A solid composed of an array of atoms or molecules possessing long-range order and arranged in a pattern which is periodic in three dimensions.
entries.example: A salt crystal has an orderly arrangement of atoms.

entries.definition: Lower in rank, status, or quality.
entries.example: Anna had always felt inferior to her brother due to poor school grades.

entries.definition: False, especially of money; intended to deceive or carry appearance of being genuine.
entries.example: This counterfeit watch looks like the real thing, but it broke a week after I bought it.

entries.definition: Not real; false, fraudulent.
entries.example: Which fur coat looks fake?

entries.definition: Greatly diminished size or form; reduced scale.
entries.example: The exhibition recreates the village in miniature.

entries.definition: Easily broken, not sturdy; of delicate material.
entries.example: She caught the fragile vase before it could shatter on the floor.

entries.definition: Able to resist wear or decay; lasting; enduring.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: persistent, long-lasting, lasting, hard-wearing; see also Thesaurus:lasting

entries.definition: Such as one may avail oneself of; capable of being used for the accomplishment of a purpose.
entries.example: We have an available candidate.

entries.definition: Fitting its definition precisely.
entries.example: a perfect circle

entries.definition: Exceeding the bounds of something; roving; hence, foreign.
entries.example: The extravagant and erring spirit hies / To his confine.

entries.definition: A current (constantly changing) trend, favored for frivolous rather than practical, logical, or intellectual reasons.
entries.example: The huge square box, parquet-floored and high-ceilinged, had been arranged to display a suite of bedroom furniture designed and made in the halcyon days of the last quarter of the nineteenth century, when modish taste was just due to go clean out of fashion for the best part of the next hundred years.

entries.definition: A particular manner of expression in writing or speech, especially one regarded as good.
entries.example: May I not vvrite in such a ſtile as this? / In ſuch a method too, and yet not miſs / Mine end, thy good? vvhy may it not be done?

entries.definition: An inclination in a particular direction.
entries.example: Her trend is to dump boyfriends when it gets serious.

entries.definition: A likelihood of behaving in a particular way or going in a particular direction; a tending toward.
entries.example: Denim has a tendency to fade.

entries.definition: The quality or state of being popular; especially, the state of being widely liked or in favor with the people at large.
entries.example: This destination has increased in popularity after great reviews in the guide books.

entries.definition: The prevailing fashion or style.
entries.example: Miniskirts were the vogue in the '60s.

entries.definition: To be superior in strength, dominance, influence, or frequency; to have or gain the advantage over others; to have the upper hand; to outnumber others.
entries.example: Red colour prevails in the Canadian flag.

entries.definition: A person who poses as a subject or visual reference for an artist.
entries.example: Leonardo da Vinci chose a 15th century criminal as a model for Judas in his painting The Last Supper.

entries.definition: An image, symbol, picture, portrait, or other representation, usually as an object of religious devotion.
entries.example: The chapel contains a painted icon of a saint.

entries.definition: A graven image or representation of anything that is revered, or believed to convey spiritual power.
entries.example:
20 And the rest of the men which were not killed by these plagues, yet repented not of the works of their hands, that they should not worship deuils, and idoles of golde, and siluer, and brasse, and stone, and of wood, which neither can see, nor heare, nor walke:
21 Neither repented they of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts.

entries.definition: Very wealthy and comfortable surroundings; the state of being that they create.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: splendor, grandeur, grandness, decadence

entries.definition: Collectively, personal ornamentation such as rings, necklaces, brooches and bracelets, made of precious metals and sometimes set with gemstones.
entries.example: The jewellery was very expensive in that shop.

entries.definition: A precious or semi-precious stone; gem, gemstone.
entries.example: A green jewel was set in the centre of the pendant.

entries.definition: A precious stone, usually of substantial monetary value or prized for its beauty or shine.
A semiprecious stone, either nephrite or jadeite, generally green or white in color, often used for carving figurines.
entries.example: Although there are dozens of different types of gems, among the best known and most important are diamond, ruby and sapphire, emerald and other gem forms of the mineral beryl, chrysoberyl, tanzanite, tsavorite, topaz and jade.

entries.definition: To make more beautiful and attractive; to decorate.
entries.example: a man adorned with noble statuary and columns

entries.definition: An element of decoration; that which embellishes or adorns.
entries.example: Dust are our frames; and, gilded dust, our pride / Looks only for a moment whole and sound; / Like that long-buried body of the king / Found lying with his urns and ornaments, / Which at a touch of light, an air of heaven, / Slipt into ashes and was found no more.

entries.definition: To make more beautiful and attractive by adding ornamentation; to decorate.
entries.example: The old book cover was embellished with golden letters

entries.definition: To stitch a decorative design on fabric with needle and thread of various colours.
entries.example: She will embroider flowers around the edge of the cloth.

entries.definition: The washing, colouring, cutting and styling of the hair; the art or trade of a hairdresser.
entries.example: There was also hairdressing: hairdressing, too, really was hairdressing in those times — no running a comb through it and that was that. It was curled, frizzed, waved, put in curlers overnight, waved with hot tongs;[…].

entries.definition: Any color in plant or animal cells.
entries.example: Chlorophyll is the pigment responsible for most plants' green colouring.

entries.definition: A colorant, especially one that has an affinity to the substrate to which it is applied.
entries.example: While the yarn is soaking in its water and vinegar bath, I prepare a selection of dyes for my preferred colorway. Isolate each dye in its own jar and place it in the larger dyepot.

entries.definition: An assembly or party of people wearing (usually elaborate or fanciful) masks and costumes, and amusing themselves with dancing, conversation, or other diversions.
entries.example: Near-synonym: costume party

entries.definition: Something hung up or spread out to hide or protect the face, or hide an object from view; usually of gauze, crepe, or similar diaphanous material.
entries.example: The veil of the temple was rent in twain.

entries.definition: A style of dress, including garments, accessories and hairstyle, especially as characteristic of a particular country, period or people.
entries.example: the sight of thousands of people gathered to watch men walk the streets openly in female costume

entries.definition: To evoke an intense interest or attraction in someone.
entries.example: The flickering TV fascinated the cat.

entries.definition: Appropriate; suitable for the circumstances.
entries.example: The hotel provided decent accommodation at a reasonable price.

entries.definition: Especially or extraordinarily fine or pleasing; exceptional.
entries.example: They sell good coffee and pastries, but their chocolate is exquisite.

entries.definition: Charming, pleasing qualities.
entries.example: The Princess brought grace to an otherwise dull and boring party.

entries.definition: Grace, refinement, and beauty in movement, appearance, or manners.
entries.example: The bride was elegance personified.

entries.definition: The act of appearing or coming into sight; the act of becoming visible to the eye.
entries.example: His sudden appearance surprised me.

entries.definition: Preparations applied externally to change or enhance the beauty of skin, hair, nails, lips, and eyes.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: makeup, make-up; beauty products

entries.definition: Alternative spelling of makeup. See usage notes there.
entries.example: From Whitemoor, left at 6.45 p.m., the train's make-up usually includes also some Continental ferry wagons, originating from Harwich.

entries.definition: Having a pleasing appearance, good-looking, attractive, particularly
entries.example: That is one handsome tree you've got there.

entries.definition: Pleasant, charismatic.
entries.example: "What a charming amusement for young people this is, Mr. Darcy! There is nothing like dancing after all. I consider it as one of the first refinements of polished society."

entries.definition: Pleasant to the sight or other senses; attractive, especially of women or children.
entries.example: Having brought it to a close, he took his way to the Kursaal. The great German watering-place is one of the prettiest nooks in Europe, and of a summer evening in the gaming days, five-and-twenty years ago, it was one of the most brilliant scenes.

entries.definition: Possessing beauty, impressing the eye; attractive.
entries.example: Anyone who has ever met her thought she was absolutely beautiful.

entries.definition: Displeasing to the eye; aesthetically unpleasing.
entries.example: the ugly view of his deformed crimes

entries.definition: To put clothes (or, formerly, armour) on (oneself or someone, a doll, a mannequin, etc.); to clothe.
entries.example: He was dressed in the latest fashions.

entries.definition: To adorn or cover with clothing; to dress; to supply clothes or clothing.
entries.example: to feed and clothe a family; to clothe oneself extravagantly

entries.definition: Unvarying; all the same.
entries.example: "Chocolate and cream," the standard colours of G.W.R. rolling stock for 21 years, are now being replaced by an all-over utility coating of reddish-brown. This is the third time that a uniform brown has been adopted as the standard livery of G.W.R. carriages.

entries.definition: A single article of clothing.
entries.example: The woman ſhall not weare that which pertaineth vnto a man, neither ſhall a man put on a womans garment: foꝛ all that doe ſo, are abomination vnto the Lord thy God.

entries.definition: A laundering; a washing.
entries.example: In our family of five, we have to do the laundry every other day.

entries.definition: A large cupboard or cabinet used to store clothes.
entries.example: She hung her coat in the wardrobe beside the bed.
entries.usage: Selected household furniture rather than a historical royal office.

entries.definition: All-encompassing, all around.
entries.example: We believe also that a controlled economy cannot be understood without some overall view of the controlling institutions: hence our short studies — shorter by far than the original drafts — of the central administration.

entries.definition: A heavy garment worn over other clothes, for protection from cold or weather.
entries.example: Men that I knew around Wapatomac didn't wear high, shiny plug hats, nor yeller spring overcoats, nor carry canes with ivory heads as big as a catboat's anchor, as you might say.

entries.definition: A long loose outer garment, often signifying honorary stature.
entries.example: Through tattered clothes small vices do appear; / Robes and furred gowns hide all.

entries.definition: A loose, flowing upper garment.
entries.example: The patient changed into a loose hospital gown.

entries.definition: A knitted garment worn on the upper body.
entries.example: She put on a sweater when the room became cold.

entries.definition: Any of certain types of outerwear.
entries.example: Take a jacket because it may be cold tonight.

entries.definition: A separate article of clothing, usually worn by women and girls, that hangs from the waist and covers the lower torso and part of the legs.
entries.example: "I like purple best," said Maida. "And old Schlegel has promised to make it for $8. It's going to be lovely. I'm going to have a plaited skirt and a blouse coat trimmed with a band of galloon under a white cloth collar with two rows of—"

entries.definition: A pair of trousers made from denim cotton.
entries.example: Traditionally most jeans are dyed dark blue.

entries.definition: An article of clothing that covers the part of the body between the waist and the ankles or knees, and is divided into a separate part for each leg.
entries.example: The trousers need to be shortened.

entries.definition: A device with interlocking parts used for fastening things together, such as a fastener or a holder.
entries.example: I always have a hard time working the clasp on this necklace!

entries.definition: A knob or disc that is passed through a loop or (buttonhole), serving as a fastener.
entries.example: I liked the man for his own sake, and even had he promised to turn out a celebrity it would have had no weight with me. I look upon notoriety with the same indifference as on the buttons on a man's shirt-front, or the crest on his note-paper.

entries.definition: To enclose (an object) completely in any flexible, thin material such as fabric or paper.
entries.example: Christmas gifts are commonly known to be wrapped in paper.

entries.definition: A series of interconnected rings or links usually made of metal.
entries.example: He wore a gold chain around the neck.

entries.definition: An item of clothing, covering all or part of the hand and fingers, but usually allowing independent movement of the fingers.
entries.example: I wore gloves to keep my hands warm.

entries.definition: A covering for the head, often in the approximate form of a cone, dome or cylinder closed at its top end, and sometimes having a brim and other decoration.
entries.example: There was a neat hat-and-umbrella stand, and the stranger's weary feet fell soft on a good, serviceable dark-red drugget, which matched in colour the flock-paper on the walls.

entries.definition: A close-fitting hat, either brimless or peaked.
entries.example: The children were all wearing caps to protect them from the sun.

entries.definition: Originally, a border or edge of a sea, a river, or other body of water; now, any border or edge.
entries.example: Yet ſtill that direful ſtroke kept on his vvay, / And falling heauie on Cambellos creſt, / Strooke him ſo hugely, that in ſvvovvne he lay, / And in his head an hideous vvound impreſt: / And ſure had it not happily found reſt / Vpon the brim of his brode plated ſhield, / It vvould haue cleft his braine dovvne to his breſt.

entries.definition: A long, often knitted, garment worn around the neck.
entries.example: Now that she had rested and had fed from the luncheon tray Mrs. Broome had just removed, she had reverted to her normal gaiety. She looked cool in a grey tailored cotton dress with a terracotta scarf and shoes and her hair a black silk helmet.

entries.definition: A piece of cloth, usually square and often fine and elegant, carried for wiping the face, eyes, nose or hands.
entries.example: He sneezed into his handkerchief during the meeting.

entries.definition: A small bag for carrying money.
entries.example: And then muſt many a man occupie as farre as his purſe would reache, and ſtretche out his legges accordynge to the length of his couerlet.

entries.definition: A small case, often flat and often made of leather, for keeping money (especially paper money), credit cards, etc.
entries.example: The thief stole all the money and credit cards out of the old man's wallet.

entries.definition: A sleeveless garment that buttons down the front, worn over a shirt, and often as part of a suit; a waistcoat.
entries.example: The Jones man was looking at her hard. Now he reached into the hatch of his vest and fetched out a couple of cigars, everlasting big ones, with gilt bands on them.

entries.definition: A long outer garment worn over the shoulders covering the back; a cape, often with a hood.
entries.example: ‘It's rather like a beautiful Inverness cloak one has inherited. Much too good to hide away, so one wears it instead of an overcoat and pretends it's an amusing new fashion.’

entries.definition: Clothes that encircle the neck.
entries.example: It was April 22, 1831, and a young man was walking down Whitehall in the direction of Parliament Street. He wore shepherd's plaid trousers and the swallow-tail coat of the day, with a figured muslin cravat wound about his wide-spread collar.

entries.definition: The part of a garment that covers the arm.
entries.example: The sleeves on my coat are too long.

entries.definition: A knitted or woven covering for the foot.
entries.example: One sock was missing after I emptied the washing machine.

entries.definition: A soft garment, usually knit or woven, worn on the foot and lower leg under shoes or other footwear.
entries.example: a pair of stockings

entries.definition: A low soft shoe that can be slipped on and off easily.
entries.example: He slipped a slipper onto each foot before leaving the bedroom.

entries.definition: A heavy shoe that covers part of the leg.
entries.example: The boot protects her ankle while she walks on rough ground.

entries.definition: A light fabric containing patterns of holes, usually built up from a single thread.
entries.example:
c. 1620, Francis Bacon, letter of advice to Sir George Villiers
Our English dames are much given to the wearing of very fine and costly laces.

entries.definition: A person who makes, repairs, or alters clothes professionally, especially suits and men's clothing.
entries.example: He works as a tailor on Swanston Street.

entries.definition: To use a needle to pass thread repeatedly through (pieces of fabric) in order to join them together.
entries.example: I sewed a button on.

entries.definition: To rotate, revolve, gyrate (usually quickly); to partially or completely rotate to face another direction.
entries.example: I spun myself around a few times.

entries.definition: A single pass of a needle in sewing; the loop or turn of the thread thus made.
entries.example: A loose stitch caused the seam to come apart.

entries.definition: A long, thin, sharp implement usually for piercing as in sewing, embroidery, acupuncture, tattooing, body piercing, medical injections, sutures, etc; or a blunt but otherwise similar implement used for forming loops or knots in crafts such as darning, knitting, tatting, etc.
entries.example: The seamstress threaded the needle to sew on a button.

entries.definition: A needle without an eye (usually) made of drawn-out steel wire with one end sharpened and the other flattened or rounded into a head, used for fastening.
entries.example: With pins of adamant / And chains they made all fast.

entries.definition: A long, thin and flexible structure made from threads twisted together.
entries.example: She bought cotton thread to use to make string.

entries.definition: A cord formed by spinning or twisting together textile fibers or filaments into one or more continuous strands, typically used in needlework.
entries.example: Woolen threads were an occult means, according to the Roman poet Horace, of depriving a person of virility.

entries.definition: A long, narrow, pliable strip of leather, cloth, or the like.
entries.example: The patter of feet, and clatter of strap and swivel, seemed to swell into a bewildering din, but they were almost upon the fielato offices, where the carretera entered the town, before a rifle flashed.

entries.definition: A long region of a single colour in a repeating pattern of similar regions.
entries.example: zebra stripes

entries.definition: A long, narrow strip of material used for decoration of clothing or the hair or gift wrapping.
entries.example: A Svveet diſorder in the dreſſe / Kindles in cloathes a vvantonneſſe: / […] / A Cuffe neglectfull, and thereby / Ribbands to flovv confuſedly: / […] / Do more bevvitch me, than vvhen Art / Is too preciſe in every part.

entries.definition: A band worn around the waist to hold clothing to one's body (usually pants), hold weapons (such as a gun or sword), or serve as a decorative piece of clothing.
entries.example: As part of the act, the fat clown's belt broke, causing his pants to fall down.

entries.definition: A band or chain worn around the wrist as jewelry/jewellery or an ornament.
entries.example: Pliny the Elder states that, to increase sexual potency, the right testis of an ass should be worn in a bracelet.

entries.definition: An article of jewelry that is worn around the neck, most often made of a string of precious metal, pearls, gems, beads or shells, and sometimes having a pendant attached.
entries.example: Her necklace had a small silver pendant.

entries.definition: Each in a string of small balls making up the rosary or paternoster.
entries.example: Holonym: prayer beads

entries.definition: Any material made of interlacing or matted fibres, including carpeting and geotextiles, woven or nonwoven.
entries.example: Near-synonym: cloth (not always differentiated)

entries.definition: A closely woven fabric (originally of silk, now also of cotton or man-made fibres) with a thick short pile on one side.
entries.example: For the first time since her husband's death, she had thrown off her weeds, and put on attire more suited to the occasion. She was richly, yet plainly dressed, in a purple velvet, with a hood of white point lace. Even her silent handmaids were surprised out of their ordinary propriety by her appearance.

entries.definition: The hair of the sheep, llama and some other ruminants.
entries.example: The sheep were caught and plucked, because shears had not yet been invented to cut the wool from the sheep's back.

entries.definition: A piece of cloth, or other suitable material, sewed or otherwise fixed upon a garment to repair or strengthen it, especially upon an old garment to cover a hole.
entries.example: His sleeves had patches on the elbows where different fabric had been sewn on to replace material that had worn away.

entries.definition: Tattered clothes (clothing).
entries.example: —What a pretty dress! —What, this old rag?

entries.definition: Of clothing, a place, etc.: unkempt and worn or otherwise in poor condition due to age or neglect; scruffy.
entries.example: They lived in a tiny apartment, with some old, shabby furniture.

entries.definition: Firmly held together; compact; not loose or open.
entries.example: a tight sponge; a tight knot

entries.definition: Commonwealth and Ireland standard spelling of color.
entries.example: Substances float around each other until you crush them all with a blender. Add a bit of white miso, lemon juice, truffle oil, chives: survey your wreckage, which will be the wrong colour (cream with a hint of grey) and the wrong consistency (gluey).

entries.definition: Bright and colourless; reflecting equal quantities of all frequencies of visible light.
entries.example: Write in black ink on white paper.

entries.definition: The color of sunflower petals and lemons; the color obtained by mixing green and red light, or by subtracting blue from white light; the color evoked by light of wavelength around 580 nm; one of the three primary colors in subtractive color systems.
entries.example: It is the strangest yellow, that wall-paper! It makes me think of all the yellow things I ever saw—not beautiful ones like buttercups, but old foul, bad yellow things.

entries.definition: A colour like that of chocolate or coffee.
entries.example: The browns and greens in this painting give it a nice woodsy feel.

entries.definition: Commonwealth standard spelling of gray.
entries.example: These grey and dun colors may be also produced by mixing whites and blacks.

entries.definition: A color reminiscent of pinks, the flowers.
entries.example: My new dress is a wonderful shade of pink.

entries.definition: A colour between red and blue; violet, though often closer to magenta.
entries.example: Arraying with reflected Purple and Gold / The Clouds that on his Weſtern Throne attend.

entries.definition: A light, brown-like colour.
entries.example: The walls were painted a warm tan rather than bright yellow.

entries.definition: A golf shot that curves intentionally to the player's right (if they are right-handed) or to the left (if left-handed).
entries.example: If you confine yourself to hitting straight shots while you are developing your golf swing, you are less likely to develop a preference for hitting a fade or a draw.

entries.definition: A discolored spot or area caused by spillage or other contact with certain fluids or substances.
entries.example: The coffee left a dark stain on the tablecloth.

entries.definition: A blemish, spot or stain made by a coloured substance.
entries.example: England bound in with the triumphant ſea, / Whoſe rocky ſhore beates backe the enuious ſiedge / Of watery Neptune, is now bound in with ſhame, / With Inky blottes, and rotten Parchment bonds.

entries.definition: A drawing or diagram conveying information.
entries.example: For example, while Figure 1 shows information for 516 visitor groups, Figure 3 presents data for 1,625 individuals. A note above each graph or table specifies the information illustrated. ... For example, although Joshua Tree NP visitors returned 525 questionnaires, Figure 1 shows data for only 516 respondents.

entries.definition: Thin; slim.
entries.example: A rod is a long slender pole used for angling.

entries.definition: Minor; small in amount
entries.example: The forecast calls for a slight warming trend in the coming days, with sunny skies and daytime temperatures reaching the midteens on Sunday and Monday, when the men will hit the snowboard course.

entries.definition: Arrangement, disposition, or sequence.
entries.example: put the children in age order

entries.definition: Any solid substance that can be consumed by living organisms, especially by eating, in order to sustain life.
entries.example: The innkeeper brought them food and drink.

entries.definition: The food and beverage a person or animal consumes.
entries.example: The diet of the giant panda consists mainly of bamboo.

entries.definition: A desire to eat food or consume drinks.
entries.example: And I return with an excellent appetite. There can be no question, my dear Watson, of the value of exercise before breakfast.

entries.definition: To care for medicinally or surgically; to apply medical care to.
entries.example: They treated me for malaria.

entries.definition: To provide, particularly
entries.example: Noe widdowes curse caters a dish of mine.

entries.definition: An item of goods or supplies, especially food, obtained for future use.
entries.example: [H]e hath preſerued all points of Humanity, in taking Order, and making Proviſion for the Releefe of Strangers diſtreſſed; whereof you have taſted.

entries.definition: Capable of being eaten without harm; suitable for consumption; innocuous to humans.
entries.example: edible fruit

entries.definition: Now especially, a set of instructions for making or preparing food dishes.
entries.example: Follow the recipe carefully when baking the cake.

entries.definition: An eating establishment in which diners are served food, usually by waiters at their tables but sometimes (as in a fast food restaurant) at a counter.
entries.example: That Italian restaurant serves some of the best food I've ever had in my life.

entries.definition: A dining hall, especially in an institution such as a college or monastery.
entries.example: t was like a train going in and out of tunnels and that was like the noise of the boys eating in the refectory when you opened and closed the flaps of the ears.

entries.definition: A restaurant in which customers select their food at a counter then carry it on a tray to a table to eat.
entries.example: Choose your lunch at the cafeteria counter, then take your tray to a table.

entries.definition: A counter or sideboard from which food and drinks are served or may be bought.
entries.example: They stayed together during three dances, went out on to the terrace, explored wherever they were permitted to explore, paid two visits to the buffet, and enjoyed themselves much in the same way as if they had been school-children surreptitiously breaking loose from an assembly of grown-ups.

entries.definition: A fireplace or pit for grilling food, typically used outdoors and traditionally employing hot charcoal as the heating medium.
entries.example: We cooked our food on the barbecue.

entries.definition: An optional light meal consumed shortly before going to bed.
entries.example: There he stood, with admirable patience, […] longing to go to rest for hours past; aware that suppers disagreed with him […] so tired and longing for bed!

entries.definition: A large celebratory meal; a feast.
entries.example:
True, worthy Banquo; he is full so valiant,
And in his commendations I am fed; / It is a banquet to me.

entries.definition: Food or drink that helps restore energy.
entries.example: A cold drink provided welcome refreshment after the climb.

entries.definition: A light meal.
entries.example: I ate a small snack before the afternoon class.

entries.definition: A small dish served before a meal to stimulate the appetite.
entries.example: We ordered a small appetiser before the main course.

entries.definition: A characteristic manner or style of preparing food, often associated with a place of origin.
entries.example: French cuisine is considered to be one of the world's most refined and elegant styles of cooking.

entries.definition: The details of the food to be served at a banquet; a bill of fare.
entries.example: After the wedding celebration was over the menu was displayed for dinner.

entries.definition: (Of food) intended to be eaten off the premises from which it was bought.
entries.example: I couldn't be bothered to cook, so I bought a takeaway curry.
entries.usage: Commonwealth, Hong-Kong, Ireland, Philippines, UK, not-comparable, sometimes

entries.definition: The presiding cook in the kitchen of a large household.
entries.example: The Chef's peace of mind was restor'd, And in due time a banquet was placed on the board.

entries.definition: Fine; of superior quality.
entries.example: We need to go to the gourmet grocery store to get the exotic ingredients for this recipe.

entries.definition: A person who does not eat animal flesh, or, in some cases, use any animal products.
entries.example: "The sight and smell of raw meat are especially odious to me, and I have often thought that if I had had to be my own cook, I should inevitably become a vegetarian, probably, indeed, return entirely to my green and salad days."

entries.definition: Sharp cutting utensils.
entries.example: Proper maintenance of your cutlery will keep the blades from dulling.

entries.definition: A lustrous, white, metallic element, atomic number 47, atomic weight 107.87, symbol Ag.
entries.example: The ring is made of silver.

entries.definition: Made of material produced by the high-temperature firing of inorganic, nonmetallic rocks and minerals.
entries.example: A ceramic vase stood on the table.

entries.definition: A hard white translucent ceramic, originally made by firing kaolin, quartz, and feldspar at high temperatures but now also inclusive of similar artificial materials; also often (figurative) such a material as a symbol of the fragility, elegance, etc. traditionally associated with porcelain goods.
entries.example: Tableware and toilets are both made of porcelain.

entries.definition: A roughly hemispherical container used to hold, mix, prepare or present food, such as salad, fruit or soup, or other items.
entries.example: You can’t have any more soup – you’ve had three bowls already.

entries.definition: A vessel such as a plate for holding or serving food, often flat with a depressed region in the middle.
entries.example: She brought forth butter in a lordly dish.

entries.definition: A small shallow dish to hold a cup and catch drips.
entries.example: Place the cup on its saucer to catch any drips.

entries.definition: A small, typically rectangular or round, flat, and rigid object upon which things are carried.
entries.example: I carefully arranged the dishes on the tray and brought it upstairs.

entries.definition: A tool with several pointed prongs, used for eating or lifting food.
entries.example: She picked up the salad with a fork.

entries.definition: A utensil or a tool designed for cutting, consisting of a flat piece of hard material, usually steel or other metal (the blade), usually sharpened on one edge, attached to a handle. The blade may be pointed for piercing.
entries.example: He was looking for a knife to chop some steak.

entries.definition: An implement for eating or serving; a scooped utensil whose long handle is straight, in contrast to a ladle.
entries.example: He must have a long spoon that must eat with the devil.

entries.definition: An amorphous solid, often transparent substance, usually made by melting silica sand with various additives (for most purposes, a mixture of soda, potash and lime is added).
entries.example: This tabletop is made of glass.

entries.definition: A large cup for beverages, usually having a handle and used without a saucer.
entries.example: He poured the tea into a large mug.

entries.definition: A vessel for boiling a liquid or cooking food, usually metal and equipped with a lid.
entries.example: To cook pasta, you first need to put the kettle on.

entries.definition: Greek god of nature, often visualized as half goat and half man playing pipes.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: Faunus, Pales (Roman counterparts, not identical)

entries.definition: A flat-bottomed vessel (usually metal) used for cooking food, possibly excluding saucepans (see usage notes).
entries.example: The soup simmered in a large pot.

entries.definition: A heater, a closed apparatus to burn fuel for the warming of a room.
entries.example:
1815 Robertson Buchanan, Appendix to A Treatise on the Economy of Fuel, and Management of Heat, Especially as it Relates to Heating and Drying by Means of Steam. p. 309.
[I]n the countries of modern Europe, the use of stoves prevail throughout the north; while in France and Great Britain, open fires are used. In the warm countries of Italy and Spain, there are very few chimneys, and the only method usually practised of tempering the cold... is to burn charcoal in portable brasiers.

entries.definition: An industrial heating device, such as for smelting metal or firing ceramics.
entries.example: Plans for the next phase include furnaces capable of inert atmospheres and partial vacuums.

entries.definition: A chamber used for baking or heating.
entries.example: Baby I'm hot just like an oven / I need some lovin'

entries.definition: A malleable, ductile, metallic element, resistant to corrosion, with atomic number 50 and symbol Sn.
entries.example: Tin is used in alloys and as a coating to protect other metals.

entries.definition: The top or cover of a container.
entries.example: Put the lid on the jar tightly.

entries.definition: To consume (a liquid) through the mouth.
entries.example: He drank the water I gave him.

entries.definition: A liquid to consume; a drink, such as tea, coffee, liquor, beer, milk, juice, or a soft drink, often excluding water.
entries.example: carbonated beverage

entries.definition: A liquid made from plant, especially fruit.
entries.example: Squeeze the orange and some juice will come out.

entries.definition: Sodium bicarbonate.
entries.example: Add a teaspoon of baking soda to the flour.

entries.definition: A beverage made by infusing the beans of the coffee plant in hot water.
entries.example: He and his friends used to order coffee whenever they went out.

entries.definition: Any of a class of organic compounds (such as ethanol) containing a hydroxyl functional group (-OH).
entries.example: Our stomachs and livers have an enzyme known as alcohol dehydrogenase that breaks down ethanol to make it less toxic for our bodies, said Atlanta gastroenterologist Dr. Preston Stewart.

entries.definition: A strong alcoholic drink produced by distillation.
entries.example: The shop sells wine and liquor behind the counter.
entries.usage: Selected the ordinary alcoholic-drink sense rather than cooking liquid.

entries.definition: Alternative form of whiskey, an alcoholic liquor distilled from fermented grain, usually aged in oak barrels, (particularly) Scotch; a drink of this liquor.
entries.example: That the young Mr. Churchills liked—but they did not like him coming round of an evening and drinking weak whisky-and-water while he held forth on railway debentures and corporation loans. Mr. Barrett, however, by fawning and flattery, seemed to be able to make not only Mrs. Churchill but everyone else do what he desired.
entries.usage: Australia, Canada, New-Zealand, Scotland, alt-of, alternative

entries.definition: An alcoholic liquor distilled from wine or fermented fruit juice.
entries.example: The recipe calls for a tablespoon of brandy.

entries.definition: Intoxicated as a result of excessive alcohol consumption, usually by drinking alcoholic beverages.
entries.example: So I took a great dry gourd and, cutting open the head, scooped out the inside and cleaned it; after which I gathered grapes from a vine which grew hard by and squeezed them into the gourd, till it was full of the juice. Then I stopped up the mouth and set in the sun, where I left it for some days, until it became strong wine; and every day I used to drink of it, to comfort and sustain me under my fatigues with that from froward and obstinate fiend; and as often as I drank myself drunk, I forgot my troubles and took new heart.

entries.definition: To remove the skin or outer covering of.
entries.example: I sat by my sister's bed, peeling oranges for her.

entries.definition: Any plant of the genus Nicotiana.
entries.example: The farmer planted tobacco in the southern field.

entries.definition: A small cigar consisting of tobacco or another substance, wrapped up in a thin roll with paper, intended for smoking.
entries.example: No matter how early I came down, I would find him on the veranda, smoking cigarettes, or otherwise his man would be there with a message to say that his master would shortly join me if I would kindly wait.

entries.definition: Not drunk; not intoxicated.
entries.example: The driver remained sober and drank only water all evening.

entries.definition: A plant or part of a plant eaten as food, such as a carrot or cabbage.
entries.example: Serve a fresh vegetable with every meal.

entries.definition: The edible fruit of the tomato plant, usually red when ripe and used as a vegetable in cooking.
entries.example: Slice the tomato and add it to the salad.

entries.definition: The edible starchy tuber of the plant species Solanum tuberosum.
entries.example: Do not let your child have potato for another year; he will probably take milk well enough after he is weaned.

entries.definition: Any of certain plants of the family Fabaceae: Pisum sativum and others.
entries.example: The pea plant climbed the garden support.

entries.definition: Any plant of several genera of the taxonomic family Fabaceae that produces large edible seeds or edible seedpods.
entries.example:
2004, T. N. Shivenanda, B. R. V. Iyengar, Phosphorus Management in French Bean (Phaseolus Vulgaris L.), Ramdane Dris, S. Mohan Jain (editors), Production Practices and Quality Assessment of Food Crops, Volume 2: Plant Mineral Nutrition and Pesticide Management, page 79,
Beans are a large group of leguminous vegetables that serve as a main source of proteins in human diet. This group comprises several species and some of them are Adzuki bean (Vigna angularis); Broad bean (Vicia faba); Cluster bean (Cyamposis tetragonoloba); French bean (Phaseolus vulgaris); […] .

entries.definition: A vine in the gourd family, Cucumis sativus.
entries.example: ASPARAGUS, cauliflowers, imperial Sileſia, royal and cabbage lettuces, burnet, purſlain, cucumbers, naſturtian flowers, peaſe and beans ſown in October, artichokes, ſcarlet ſtrawberries, and kidney beans.

entries.definition: An edible plant (Brassica oleracea var. capitata) having a head of green leaves.
entries.example: In aphrodisiac preparation, wild cabbage was frequently an ingredient.

entries.definition: A monocotyledonous plant (Allium cepa), allied to garlic, used as vegetable and spice.
entries.example: Some of the weeds that cause an undesirable flavor in milk are: onion, tarweed, scaleweed, garlic, mustard, pepper grass.

entries.definition: Any of the fleshy fruiting bodies of fungi typically produced above ground on soil or on their food sources (such as decaying wood).
entries.example: Some mushrooms are edible whereas others are poisonous, and sometimes they are difficult to tell apart.

entries.definition: The plant Solanum melongena or its edible fruit; an aubergine.
entries.example: Some fun meatless recipes include jackfruit sandwiches in place of pulled pork; black bean meatless balls or eggplant and shiitake “meatballs.”

entries.definition: A vegetable with a nutritious, juicy, sweet root that is often orange in colour, Daucus carota, family Apiaceae, especially the subspecies sativus.
entries.example: In general, beets, carrots, and turnips are all of aphrodisiac value in erotic dietary.

entries.definition: The white root of a yellow-flowered plant, Brassica rapa, grown as a vegetable and as fodder for cattle.
entries.example: The ancient Roman gastronomists considered the turnip, when prepared in the following manner, a dish fit for epicures: "After boiling, extract the water from them, and season with cummin, rue, or benzoin, pounded in a mortar; afterward add honey, vinegar, gravy, and boiled grapes. Allow the whole to simmer, and serve."

entries.definition: A plant of the Brassicaceae family, Raphanus sativus or Raphanus raphanistrum subsp. sativus, having an edible root.
entries.example: Many times they ſow divers ſeeds in a Bed together, as Radiſhes and Carrots, that by ſuch time as the Carrots come up, the Radiſhes may be gone. Upon beds newly ſet with Licorice they ſow Onions or Radiſh, or Lettice if their Licorice plants or ground be but weak, ſo as not quickly to cauſe a ſhadow with their leaves.

entries.definition: A long, thin piece of land; any long, thin area.
entries.example: The countries were in dispute over the ownership of a strip of desert about 100 metres wide.

entries.definition: The outer covering of a fruit or seed.
entries.example: Remove the hull from the seed before grinding it.

entries.definition: A small fruit, usually red, black or yellow, with a smooth hard seed and a short hard stem.
entries.example: She removed the stone from each cherry.

entries.definition: A small succulent fruit, of any one of many varieties.
entries.example: A single ripe berry hung from the branch.

entries.definition: A small, round, smooth-skinned edible fruit, usually purple, red, or green, that grows in bunches on female vines of most species of genus Vitis and the self-fertile plants of species Vitis vinifera.
entries.example: Grapes give us whole-fruit snacks, grape juice, raisins, wine, and more.

entries.definition: The large edible fruit of the papaya plant.
entries.example: She cut a ripe papaya into slices for breakfast.
entries.usage: Selected the edible fruit rather than the tree.

entries.definition: Any tree of species Prunus persica, native to China and now widely cultivated throughout temperate regions, having pink flowers and edible fruit.
entries.example: I think it the best way to plant the fifteen sorts, and the hard Peaches I have mentioned, in the same order as they stand in the list.

entries.definition: An edible fruit produced by the pear tree, similar to an apple but typically elongated towards the stem.
entries.example: The pear was ripe and sweet.

entries.definition: The fruit and its tree.
entries.example: She picked a plum from the tree and washed it.

entries.definition: A round citrus fruit with a thick peel and sweet or sour juice.
entries.example: She peeled an orange and shared the segments with her brother.
entries.usage: Selected the fruit rather than the tree.

entries.definition: A large fruit with a firm rind and soft, juicy flesh.
entries.example: She cut the melon into wedges for breakfast.

entries.definition: A yellowish citrus fruit.
entries.example: The juice of Lemmons killeth Warts, but better the water of the ſame juice, diſtilled through a glaſs.

entries.definition: A flightless bird of the order Apterygiformes native to New Zealand.
entries.example: The kiwi searched for insects on the forest floor.

entries.definition: A plant, grown for it, or its fruits or seeds, to be harvested as food, livestock fodder, or fuel or for any other economic purpose.
entries.example: The farmer had to decide which crop to grow as his main bet for the coming year. Would it be barley, oats, or something else?

entries.definition: Any cereal plant (or its grain) that is the main crop or staple of a country or region.
entries.example: And hee ſaid, Beholde, I haue heard that there is corne in Egypt: get you downe thither and buy for vs from thence, that we may liue, and not die.

entries.definition: The harvested seeds of various grass food crops, especially wheat, maize, rye, barley, and rice.
entries.example: Near-synonym: corn (broad sense, maize and others)

entries.definition: Any of the several cereal grains, of the genus Triticum, that yields flour as used in bakery.
entries.example: They bought a sack of wheat and a sack of rye with the intent to try their hand at milling and baking.

entries.definition: To cut (for example a grain) with a sickle, scythe, or reaping machine.
entries.example: The farmers reap the wheat when the grain is ready.

entries.definition: Powder obtained by grinding or milling cereal grains, especially wheat, or other foodstuffs such as soybeans and potatoes, and used to bake bread, cakes, and pastry.
entries.example: Everything a living animal could do to destroy and to desecrate bed and walls had been done. […] A canister of flour from the kitchen had been thrown at the looking-glass and lay like trampled snow over the remains of a decent blue suit with the lining ripped out which lay on top of the ruin of a plastic wardrobe.

entries.definition: A dish made of grain or legumes, milk or water, heated and stirred until thick and typically eaten for breakfast.
entries.example: Eat your porridge while it's hot!

entries.definition: A thick, soft mixture of a solid material and liquid.
entries.example: Mix the flour and water into a smooth paste.

entries.definition: Farm animals; animals domesticated for cultivation.
entries.example: Meronym: stock animal

entries.definition: A domesticated subspecies of red junglefowl (Gallus gallus domesticus).
entries.example: backyard chickens

entries.definition: A bird in the genus Meleagris, usually with a fan-shaped tail and wattled neck.
entries.example: A turkey wandered across the farmyard.

entries.definition: The meat from cattle or other bovines; especially, that from adults.
entries.example: I love eating beef.

entries.definition: The meat of a pig.
entries.example: The cafeteria serves pork on Tuesdays.

entries.definition: The meat of sheep used as food; especially, that of adults.
entries.example: Mutton, eaten with caraway seed, is eaten as an aphrodisiac among Arabs.

entries.definition: A food made of ground meat (or meat substitute) and seasoning, packed in a section of the animal's intestine, or in a similarly cylindrical shaped synthetic casing.
entries.example: He grilled a sausage for his lunch.

entries.definition: A typically cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water, moving with the help of fins and breathing with gills; any vertebrate that is not a tetrapod.
entries.example: Salmon is a fish.

entries.definition: An inland body of standing water, either natural or man-made, that is smaller than a lake.
entries.example: But when the moon rose and the breeze awakened, and the sedges stirred, and the cat's-paws raced across the moonlit ponds, and the far surf off Wonder Head intoned the hymn of the four winds, the trinity, earth and sky and water, became one thunderous symphony—a harmony of sound and colour silvered to a monochrome by the moon.

entries.definition: A straight, round stick, shaft, bar, cane, or staff.
entries.example: The circus strong man proved his strength by bending an iron rod, and then straightening it.

entries.definition: (also dairy products or dairy produce) Products produced from milk.
entries.example: My routine changed in February because I stopped alcohol, caffeine and dairy. Normally, I would have drunk a strong beer before I went to bed and made an espresso in the morning. It’s boring now but healthier.

entries.definition: A white liquid produced by the mammary glands of female mammals to nourish their young. From certain animals, especially cows, it is also called dairy milk and is a common food for humans as a beverage or used to produce various dairy products such as butter, cheese, and yogurt.
entries.example: Skyr is a product made of curdled milk.

entries.definition: A milk-based product stiffened by a bacterium-aided curdling process, and sometimes mixed with fruit or other flavoring.
entries.example: Moroccan curried crab and streaks of minty, lemony yogurt add luxury to a supersimple zucchini soup ($14).

entries.definition: The butterfat or milkfat part of milk which rises to the top; this part when separated from the remainder.
entries.example: Take 100 ml of cream and 50 grams of sugar…

entries.definition: A dairy product made from curdled or cultured milk.
entries.example: Add grated cheese to the pasta before serving.

entries.definition: Something added; especially, such an addition added to make up for a deficiency.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: see Thesaurus:adjunct

entries.definition: A soft, fatty foodstuff made by churning the cream of milk (generally cow's milk).
entries.example: Melt the butter before adding the flour.

entries.definition: A food consisting principally of raw vegetables (especially greens, e.g. lettuce), other savoury ingredients (typically cooked), fruit, or confectionary; often involving two or more such ingredients mixed together, with larger items cut or torn into small pieces, and usually with a dressing or binding; usually served cold or at room temperature, as a dish or savoury sandwich filling.
entries.example:
Lafeu. ’Twas a good lady, ’twas a good lady: we may pick a thousand salads ere we light on such another herb.
Clown. Indeed, sir, she was the sweet marjoram of the salad, or rather, the herb of grace.

entries.definition: A dish or foodstuff where at least one piece, but typically two or more pieces, of bread serves as the wrapper or container of some other food.
entries.example: The most famous place in Copenhagen, Ida Davidsen, has a menu of 190 different kinds of open sandwich.

entries.definition: A hot sandwich consisting of a patty of cooked ground beef or a meat substitute, in a sliced bun, usually also containing salad vegetables, condiments, or both.
entries.example: She ordered a hamburger with lettuce and tomato.

entries.definition: A block of bread after baking.
entries.example: Philander went into the next room[…]and came back with a salt mackerel that dripped brine like a rainstorm. Then he put the coffee pot on the stove and rummaged out a loaf of dry bread and some hardtack.

entries.definition: A type of pastry that consists of an outer crust and a filling. (Savory pies are more popular in the UK and sweet pies are more popular in the US, so "pie" without qualification has different connotations in these dialects.)
entries.example: The family had steak and kidney pie for dinner and cherry pie for dessert.

entries.definition: A baked Italian dish of a thinly rolled bread crust typically topped before baking with tomato sauce, cheese, and other ingredients such as meat or vegetables.
entries.example: a slice of pizza

entries.definition: Dough made from wheat and water and sometimes mixed with egg and formed into various shapes; often sold in dried form and typically boiled for eating.
entries.example: We cooked the pasta in a large pan of boiling water.

entries.definition: A type of pasta made in the shape of long thin strings.
entries.example: Her mother was cooking spaghetti for dinner.

entries.definition: Any of various dishes commonly made by combining liquids, such as water or stock, with other ingredients, such as meat and vegetables, that contribute the food value, flavor, and texture.
entries.example: Pho is a traditional Vietnamese soup.

entries.definition: Any of various dishes, sweet or savoury, prepared by boiling or steaming or from batter.
entries.example: The dishes in this chapter represent a range of multiethnic savory custards and steamed puddings, including a few surprises like a chèvre popover pudding and a bread pudding with lettuce and cheese.

entries.definition: A small, flat, baked good which is either hard and crisp or else soft but firm; a cookie.
entries.example: Weighed myself at the gym and have hit 10st 8lb, a sure sign of things getting out of control—so I can’t even console myself with a chocolate biscuit.
entries.usage: Australia, Canada, India, Ireland, New-Zealand, UK, sometimes, uncommon

entries.definition: A sweet mixture of fruit boiled with sugar and allowed to congeal. Often spread on bread or toast or used in jam tarts
entries.example: He is allergic to jam.

entries.definition: Any of various hard-shelled seeds or hard, dry fruits from various families of plants.
entries.example: There are many sorts of nuts: peanuts, cashews, pistachios, Brazil nuts and more.

entries.definition: A food made from ground roasted cocoa beans.
entries.example: Chocolate is a very popular treat.

entries.definition: A dessert made from frozen sweetened cream or a similar substance, usually flavoured.
entries.example: Strawberries are particularly delicious with ice cream.

entries.definition: Any tropical climbing orchid of the genus Vanilla (especially Vanilla planifolia), bearing podlike fruit yielding an extract used in flavoring food or in perfumes.
entries.example: Vanilla itself was transplanted from Madagascar, the main source of the spice, to Polynesia a century ago.

entries.definition: A strong-tasting paste or powder made from mustard seeds and used to flavour food.
entries.example: He added a little mustard to the sandwich.

entries.definition: A plant of the species Eutrema japonicum, cultivated for its edible root.
entries.example: The farmer grows wasabi in a shaded stream bed.

entries.definition: A pungent spice made from dried berries of the pepper plant.
entries.example: Add a little black pepper to the soup.
entries.usage: Selected the spice rather than the botanical plant category.

entries.definition: The pungent aromatic rhizome of a tropical Asian herb, Zingiber officinale, used as a spice and as a stimulant and acarminative.
entries.example: Fresh ginger adds a sharp flavour to the soup.

entries.definition: A plant, Allium sativum, related to the onion, having a pungent bulb much used in cooking.
entries.example: Athletes' use of herbal supplements has skyrocketed in the past two decades. At the top of the list of popular herbs are echinacea and ginseng, whereas garlic, St. John's wort, soybean, ephedra and others are also surging in popularity or have been historically prevalent.

entries.definition: A spring onion, Allium fistulosum.
entries.example: Slice a scallion over the noodles before serving.

entries.definition: A sour liquid formed by the fermentation of alcohol used as a condiment or preservative; a dilute solution of acetic acid.
entries.example: In Persia, newly married couples were presented with sheep's trotters steeped in vinegar as a love enticement.

entries.definition: A common substance, chemically consisting mainly of sodium chloride (NaCl), used extensively as a food ingredient, seasoning, condiment, and preservative.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: table salt, rock salt, road salt

entries.definition: A food consisting of small, sweet crystals, principally of sucrose, obtained from sugar cane or sugar beet and used as sweetener and preservative.
entries.example: To a pound of gooseberries take a pound and a half of double-refined sugar. Clarify the sugar with water, a pint to a pound of sugar, and when the syrup is cold, put the gooseberries single in your preserving pan, put the syrup to them, and set them on a gentle fire.

entries.definition: Sweet food made mainly with sugar or other sweeteners.
entries.example: The children shared a bag of candy after lunch.
entries.usage: Selected ordinary confectionery rather than crystallized sugar alone.

entries.definition: A sweet, viscous, gold-colored fluid produced from plant nectar by bees, and often consumed by humans.
entries.example: The honey in the pot should last for years.

entries.definition: British standard spelling of flavor.

entries.definition: Tasting of acidity.

entries.definition: Having an acrid taste (usually from a basic substance).

Never had he quite accustomed himself to the ruined flesh that civilized men had served him, and in the bottom of his savage heart there had constantly been the craving for the warm meat of the fresh kill, and the rich, red blood.

entries.definition: Delicious.

entries.definition: Having a pleasant or satisfying flavor.

entries.definition: A need or compelling desire for food.

entries.definition: Needing to drink water or any liquid that can supply water.

entries.definition: Aromatic or pungent plant matter (usually dried) used to season or flavor food.

entries.definition: A pleasant smell; the scent, odor, or odoriferous particles emitted from a sweet-smelling substance; a pleasant odor.
entries.example: Breezes blowing from beds of iris quickened her breath with their perfume; she saw the tufted lilacs sway in the wind, and the streamers of mauve-tinted wistaria swinging, all a-glisten with golden bees; she saw a crimson cardinal winging through the foliage, and amorous tanagers flashing like scarlet flames athwart the pines.

entries.definition: One of the substances present in a mixture, especially food.

entries.definition: To distribute or arrange methodically; to work over and classify; to reduce to portions for ready use or application.

entries.definition: A person who prepares food.

entries.definition: To cook using an oven, especially baked goods.

entries.definition: A method of cooking food.

entries.definition: Bread that has been toasted (cooked lightly by browning).

entries.definition: To stroke with the tongue.

entries.definition: To crush with the teeth by repeated closing and opening of the jaws; done to food to soften it and break it down by the action of saliva before it is swallowed.

entries.definition: The flesh around the teeth.

entries.definition: To be saturated with liquid by being immersed in it.

entries.definition: A lower section of a road or geological feature.

entries.definition: To apply pressure (to something) from two or more sides at once.

entries.definition: To disturb the relative position of the particles (of a liquid or similar) by passing an object through it.
entries.example: She stirred the pudding with a spoon.

entries.definition: To reduce to smaller pieces by crushing with lateral motion.
entries.example: Grind the coffee beans just before brewing.

entries.definition: That which is thin and broad.
entries.example: I pulled in hand over hand on the cord, and when I judged myself near enough, rose at infinite risk to about half my height and thus commanded the roof and a slice of the interior of the cabin.

entries.definition: To part with, separate from, leave off; cast off, cast, let fall, be divested of.

entries.definition: The art and science of designing and managing the construction of buildings and other structures, particularly if they are well proportioned and decorated.
entries.example: The architecture throughout NYC is amazing.

entries.definition: The act of building or putting up or together of something.

entries.definition: A cohesive whole built up of distinct parts.

entries.definition: To build something.
entries.example: Workers will construct a new bridge.

entries.definition: To block or fill (a passage) with obstacles or an obstacle.
entries.example: Do not leave boxes where they obstruct the emergency exit.

entries.definition: To create or start an organisation.
entries.example: The university plans to establish a research centre.

entries.definition: To form (something) by combining materials or parts.
entries.example: I built a shed in my backyard.

entries.definition: Located or discovered something; the past form of find.
entries.example: She found her keys under the sofa.

entries.definition: Real, actual, tangible.

entries.definition: An artificial metal produced from iron, harder and more elastic than elemental iron; used figuratively as a symbol of hardness.
entries.example: Ocearium stæli.

entries.definition: The condition of being stable or in equilibrium, and thus resistant to change.
entries.example: This platform offers good stability

entries.definition: The place where anything is fixed; situation; local position
entries.example: the site of a city or of a house

entries.definition: A theater, auditorium, arena, or other area designated for sporting or entertainment events.
entries.example: The concert venue can hold five hundred people.

entries.definition: A recognizable natural or man-made feature used for navigation.
entries.example: Anyone have any weird landmarks they often remember seeing along roads in the olden days?

entries.definition: Located in a specific place.
entries.example: The Pan-la-mên coal-field is situated about 16 km. south of Ssŭ-pʻing-chieh station on the railway between Chʻang-tʻu and Chʻang-chʻun.

entries.definition: To place; to set in a particular spot or position.
entries.example: The captives and emigrants whom he brought with him were located in the trans-Tiberine quarter.

entries.definition: To dwell permanently or for a considerable time; to have a settled abode for a time; to remain for a long time.
entries.example: […] And the delighted ſpirit / To die in fierie floods, or to recide / In thrilling Region of thicke-ribbed Ice […]

entries.definition: To live or reside in.
entries.example: The Inuit inhabit the Arctic.

entries.definition: To relocate periodically from one region to another, usually according to the seasons.
entries.example: Twice a year the geese migrate — from Florida to Canada and back again.

entries.definition: To resolve a disagreement or decide a matter.
entries.example: Both sides agreed to settle the dispute through negotiation.

entries.definition: A house or place in which a person lives; a habitation, a home.
entries.example: The old house served as a dwelling for Albert.

entries.definition: A very tall building with a large number of floors.
entries.example: The fact that land is a commodity of unlimited extent in America, together with the now appreciated fact that most high buildings have been economic failures, spell the doom of the skyscraper concept.

entries.definition: A house, often larger and more expensive than average, in the countryside or on the coast, often used as a retreat.
entries.example: What I commissioned you to get for me, and anything you see suitable to my Tusculan villa, I should be glad if you will, as you say in your letter, procure for me, only don't put yourself to any inconvenience. The truth is, there is no other place that gives me complete rest after all my worries and hard work.

entries.definition: A large luxurious house or building, usually built for the wealthy.
entries.example: The old mansion has twelve bedrooms and a large garden.

entries.definition: A complete domicile occupying only part of a building, especially one for rent; a flat.
entries.example: apartment dwellers

entries.definition: An overnight lodging place for travelers, with dormitory accommodation and shared facilities, especially a youth hostel.
entries.example: a rundown hostel

entries.definition: A building for recreational use such as a hunting lodge or a summer cabin.
entries.example: We stayed in a mountain lodge near the forest.

entries.definition: A small, simple one-storey dwelling or shelter, often with just one room, and generally built of readily available local materials.
entries.example: a thatched hut; a mud hut; a shepherd’s hut

entries.definition: A small dwelling characteristic of the frontier, especially when built from logs with simple tools and not constructed by professional builders, but by those who meant to live in it.
entries.example: Abraham Lincoln was born in a log cabin.

entries.definition: An enclosed underground space, often under a building, used for storage or shelter.
entries.example: The farmhouse has several additions, added over many decades; it has three cellars, and one of them is older than the other two.

entries.definition: A small house.
entries.example: So when four years were wholly finished, / She threw her royal robes away. / “Make me a cottage in the vale,” she said, / “Where I may mourn and pray.

entries.definition: A place where nursing (“breastfeeding”) or the raising of children is carried on.
entries.example: As soon as she was alone and the carriage had been driven well away from the door, Mrs. Trevelyan left the drawing-room and went up to the nursery. As she entered she clothed her face with her sweetest smile. "How is his own mother's dearest, dearest, darling duck?" she said, putting out her arms and taking the boy from the nurse.

entries.definition: A bed or cot for a baby, oscillating on rockers or swinging on pivots.
entries.example: No sooner was I crept out of my cradle / But I was made a king, at nine months old.

entries.definition: Somewhere one can find protection.
entries.example: The band of explorers found a shelter behind the waterfall, which they rested at for three days.

entries.definition: A substantial, often approximately cuboid, piece of any substance.
entries.example: a block of ice; a block of stone

entries.definition: A rectangular array of squares or rectangles of equal size, such as in a crossword puzzle.
entries.example: Draw a grid of equal squares on the paper.

entries.definition: A wing of a building, notably in a church separated from the nave proper by piers.
entries.example: Hester Earle and Violet Wayne were moving about the aisle with bundles of wheat-ears and streamers of ivy, for the harvest thanksgiving was shortly to be celebrated, while the vicar stood waiting for their directions on the chancel steps with a great handful of crimson gladioli.

entries.definition: A covered entrance to a building, whether taken from the interior, and forming a sort of vestibule within the main wall, or projecting without and with a separate roof. A porch often has chair(s), table(s) and swings.
entries.example: He sat on his porch, waiting for his friend to come over.

entries.definition: A narrow hall or passage with rooms leading off it, as in a building or in a railway carriage.
entries.example: There is an hour or two, after the passengers have embarked, which is disquieting and fussy.[…]Stewards, carrying cabin trunks, swarm in the corridors. Passengers wander restlessly about or hurry, with futile energy, from place to place.

entries.definition: A single step in a staircase.

entries.definition: A flight of stairs; a stairway.

entries.definition: A floor or level of a building or ship.

entries.definition: A single thickness of some material covering a surface.

entries.definition: Anything that escalates.

entries.definition: A solid upright structure designed usually to support a larger structure above it, such as a roof or horizontal beam, but sometimes for decoration.

entries.definition: The desk or area where visitors are greeted and assisted.

Whon he haþ vsed he walkeþ riht

entries.definition: To connect, set up or prepare something for use

entries.definition: Material used to create an engineered product.

entries.definition: The act of placing or putting in place; the act of locating or positioning; the state of being placed.

entries.definition: A structured arrangement of items within certain limits.

entries.definition: A specification of an object or process, referring to requirements to be satisfied and thus conditions to be met for them to solve a problem.

entries.definition: To go or come into an enclosed or partially enclosed space.

entries.definition: An act of going out or going away, or leaving; a departure.

entries.definition: The part of something that faces out; the outer surface.

entries.definition: A trip into any undeveloped area to see, photograph or to hunt wild animals in their own environment.

entries.definition: An organized display of a group of people, particularly

entries.definition: To inhabit or to visit frequently (most often used in reference to ghosts).
