entries.definition: The tendency to attract.
entries.example: The Moon is held in its orbit by the attraction of the Earth's gravity.

entries.definition: Something, such as a monument, by which someone or something is remembered.
entries.example: These mementoes or memorials [sculptural national monuments], though in the present age the unphilosophical and sciolistic spirit of some have led them to regard with contempt this method of honouring the illustrious great, excite a laudable admiration for the service or benefit to which they testify, and are living realities to perpetuate at once the respect entertained by the nation, both for the individual himself and the performance that has entitled him to their gratitude.

entries.definition: An ancient massive construction with a square or rectangular base and four triangular sides meeting in an apex, such as those built as tombs in Egypt or as bases for temples in Mesoamerica.
entries.example: The ancient pyramid rises above the surrounding desert.

entries.definition: A place on the coast at which ships can shelter, or dock to load and unload cargo or passengers.
entries.example: peering in maps for ports and piers and roads

entries.definition: A permit to enter and leave a country, normally issued by the authorities of the country to be visited.
entries.example: I came on a six-month tourist visa.

entries.definition: Moving pedestrians or vehicles, or the flux or passage thereof.
entries.example: The traffic is slow during rush hour.

entries.definition: A company that flies airplanes to transport people and goods.
entries.example: But already there are some commercial air­lines in the United States which use airplanes cap­able of more than 200 miles an hour.

entries.definition: A powered heavier-than-air aircraft with fixed wings: a fixed-wing aircraft with at least one engine or electric motor.
entries.example: on an airplane

entries.definition: An aircraft that is borne along by one or more sets of long rotating blades which allow it to hover, move in any direction including reverse, or land; and typically having a smaller set of blades on its tail to stabilize the aircraft.
entries.example: We flew over the city in a helicopter.

entries.definition: A collimated stream, spurt or flow of liquid or gas from a pressurized container, an engine, etc.
entries.example: In the floor of the valley the line passes hills of fantastic shape, like sleeping camels and inverted washbasins, and you can see the beautiful lakes Naivasha and Elementeita; at Eburru jets of steam spurt out of the ground.

entries.definition: A device, generally constructed from fabric, that is designed to employ air resistance to control the fall of an object or person, causing them to float instead of falling.
entries.example: The parachute opened soon after the jump.

entries.definition: The act of flying; the ability to fly.
entries.example: Most birds are capable of flight.

entries.definition: A person who steers a ship, a helmsman.
One who rides or travels in a vehicle, but who does not operate it and is not a member of the crew.
entries.example: It is never possible to settle down to the ordinary routine of life at sea until the screw begins to revolve. There is an hour or two, after the passengers have embarked, which is disquieting and fussy.

entries.definition: Portable cases, large bags, and similar equipment for manually carrying, pushing, or pulling personal items while traveling
entries.example: Please put your baggage in the trunk.

entries.definition: The bags and other containers that hold a traveller's belongings.
entries.example:
August 4, 1726, Jonathan Swift, letter to Alexander Pope
I am gathering up my luggage, and preparing for my journey.

entries.definition: A large (usually rectangular) piece of luggage used for carrying clothes, and sometimes suits, when travelling.
entries.example: My suitcase is stowed in the luggage rack.

entries.definition: Taken onto an airplane (or a ferry, etc.) with a passenger, rather than checked.
entries.example: It's a compact suitcase, but it makes a good carry-on bag.

entries.definition: A series of one or more shelves, stacked one above the other.
entries.example: The rack has three shelves for storing tools.

entries.definition: The transportation of goods (originally by water; now also (chiefly US) by land); also, the hiring of a vehicle or vessel for such transportation.
entries.example: [A]fter ſome Conſideration, that the City of Hamburgh might happen to be as good a Market for our Goods as London, we all took Freight with him, and having put my Goods on board, it was moſt natural for me to put my Steward on board to take care of them, […]

entries.definition: A bound collection of maps often including tables, illustrations or other text.
entries.example: We used an atlas to locate the mountain range.

entries.definition: Money paid for a transport ticket.
entries.example: train fare

entries.definition: A course or way which is traveled or passed.
entries.example: The route was used so much that it formed a rut.

entries.definition: A plan of the places to be visited during a journey.
entries.example: The revised itinerary includes a guided tour of the museum.
entries.usage: Typical combinations: travel itinerary, detailed itinerary, revised itinerary.

entries.definition: A paragraph or section of text or music with particular meaning.
entries.example: passage of scripture

entries.definition: The junction of two (or more) paths, streets, highways, or other thoroughfares.
entries.example: Near-synonym: crossroads

entries.definition: A geometrical figure consisting of two straight lines or bars intersecting each other such that at least one of them is bisected by the other.
entries.example: Put a cross for a wrong answer and a tick for a right one.

entries.definition: To do with a place or places.
entries.example: Do you know the way to the airport?  Come this way and I'll show you a shortcut.

entries.definition: A trail for the use of, or worn by, pedestrians.
entries.example: Yet ere to to-morrow's ſun ſhall ſhew his head, / The dewy paths of meadows we will tread, / For crowns and chaplets to adorn thy head.

entries.definition: A road, street, or similar thoroughfare.
entries.example: Penny Lane

entries.definition: A broad street, especially one bordered by trees or, in cities laid out in a grid pattern, one that is on a particular side of the city or that runs in a particular direction.
entries.example: Finding an address east to west is fairly simple . The numbering begins at Central Avenue and moves logically and predictably either west through the avenues or east through the streets, so you know that 2400 East Camelback is at Twenty-Fourth Street or 4300 West Indian School is at Forty-Third Avenue .

entries.definition: A main public road, especially a multi-lane, high-speed thoroughfare.
entries.example: The highway to the East Coast which ran through the borough of Ebbfield had always been a main road and even now, despite the vast garages, the pylons and the gaily painted factory glasshouses which had sprung up beside it, there still remained an occasional trace of past cultures.

entries.definition: A raised edge separating a road from the pavement.
entries.example: The driver stopped beside the curb.
entries.usage: Kerb is the usual British spelling.

entries.definition: A post bearing a sign that gives information on directions.
entries.example: Dozens of signposts have been stolen, forcing the local authorities to put up the sign at a 2m height and embed it in theft-resistant concrete when putting up replacements.

entries.definition: To cover something with paving slabs.
entries.example: Workers will pave the path with stone slabs.

entries.definition: A conveyance: a spacious device for carrying or transporting substances, objects, people or animals.
entries.example: But electric vehicles and the batteries that made them run became ensnared in corporate scandals, fraud, and monopolistic corruption that shook the confidence of the nation and inspired automotive upstarts.

entries.definition: Clipping of automatic (of a gearbox/transmission).
entries.example: It's an auto sedan which we picked up from a wholesaler locally.

entries.definition: Moving or operating quickly, as a train not making local stops.
entries.example: The express train runs directly to the city without stopping at every station.

entries.definition: A passenger vehicle for public use that runs on tracks in the road (called a streetcar or trolley in North America).
entries.example: Lizzie and she got a dozen of large bottles and the loan of a basket and we got a currant pan and a half-pound of cooked ham in the shop next door and got on the tram for Whitehall.

entries.definition: A wheeled vehicle, generally pulled by a horse.
entries.example: I have a coach waiting. During intermission, would you consent to accompany me for a cooling ride around the city?

entries.definition: An emergency vehicle designed for transporting seriously ill or injured people to a hospital.
entries.example: The NHS is bracing itself for its worst ever winter crisis descending in the next fortnight because of a worsening “flu-nami” that has left hospitals, GP surgeries and ambulances services under intense strain.

entries.definition: A small wheel or roller, specifically the wheel of a gun carriage.
entries.example: “Put that cannon up once, and I'll answer for it that no Injin faces it. 'Twill be as good as a dozen sentinels,” answered Joel. “As for mountin’, I thought of that before I said a syllable about the crittur. There's the new truck-wheels in the court, all ready to hold it, and the carpenters can put the hinder part to the whull, in an hour or two.”

entries.definition: A large and heavy motor vehicle designed to carry goods or soldiers; a truck
entries.example: But whenever one of the motor-trucks lumbering by bore a big U.S. on its rear panel Troy pushed his light ambulance ahead and skimmed past, just for the joy of seeing the fresh young heads rising pyramid-wise about the sides of the lorry, hearing the snatches of familiar songs—"Hail, hail, the gang's all here!" and "We won't come back till it's over over here!"—and shouting back in reply to a stentorian "Hi, kid, beat it!", "Bet your life I will, old man!"

entries.definition: A covered motor vehicle used to carry goods or (normally less than ten) persons, usually roughly cuboid in shape, Depending on the type of van, it can be bigger or smaller than a pickup truck and SUV, and longer and higher than a car but relatively smaller than a truck/lorry or a bus.
entries.example: While Santa Monica has a longstanding prohibition against public camping that includes living in vehicles, the van rental business has been a problem in Venice for years. […] Organizations that provide safe parking locations have limited capacity and are often unable to accommodate the kind of non-operational vans that are being repurposed as makeshift housing.

entries.definition: A heavier four-wheeled (normally horse-drawn) vehicle designed to carry goods (or sometimes people).
entries.example: These wagons and pack-mules will include transportation for all personal baggage, mess chests, cooking utensils, desks, papers, &c.

entries.definition: The act of conveying; carrying.
entries.example: The remainder of the men were employed in unbarreling our Pork and stringing it on poles for convenience of carriage, and carrying our Batteaux from the river to the pond.

entries.definition: A vehicle used in farms e.g. for pulling farm equipment and preparing the fields.
entries.example: The tractor pulled a trailer across the field.

entries.definition: A small, open, wheeled vehicle, drawn or pushed by a person or animal, often with two wheels on one axle, more often used for transporting goods than passengers.
entries.example: The grocer delivered his goods by cart.

entries.definition: A tricycle having a hooded cab to seat paying passengers.
entries.example: Southwark: The cause of the fire that seriously disrupted services between London Bridge and Waterloo East on August 17 has been traced to an overheated battery-powered pedicab under the aches [sic: arches] in Union Street.

entries.definition: An interval of space or time in which one set of events or phenomena is completed.
entries.example: the cycle of the seasons, or of the year

entries.definition: A building (or section of a building) used to store a car or cars, tools and other miscellaneous items.
entries.example: A little further on, to the right, was a large garage, where the charabancs stood, half in and half out of the yard.

entries.definition: A machine or device that converts other energy forms into mechanical energy, or imparts motion.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: drive, engine (sometimes synonymous)

entries.definition: Power derived from the motion of a horse.
entries.example: Shillibeer's bus came in 1829 drawn by three horses. Later two horses were found sufficient to pull these closed wagonettes, which eventually had outside seats, and later on the substitution of a motor for horsepower.

entries.definition: A circular device capable of rotating on its axis, facilitating movement or transportation or performing labour in machines.
entries.example: The departure was not unduly prolonged.[…]Within the door Mrs. Spoker hastily imparted to Mrs. Love a few final sentiments on the subject of Divine Intention in the disposition of buckets; farewells and last commiserations; a deep, guttural instigation to the horse; and the wheels of the waggonette crunched heavily away into obscurity.

entries.definition: A device used to slow or stop the motion of a wheel, or of a vehicle, usually by friction (although other resistive forces, such as electromagnetic fields or aerodynamic drag, can also be used); also, the controls or apparatus used to engage such a mechanism such as the pedal in a car.
entries.example: She slammed the brakes when she saw a child run in front of the car.

entries.definition: The ring-shaped protective covering around a wheel which is usually made of rubber or plastic composite and is either pneumatic or solid.
entries.example: pneumatic tyres

entries.definition: To use a car horn.
entries.example: They stood and observed how long it took for the other cars to honk.

entries.definition: A person in a crew
entries.example: One crew died in the accident.

entries.definition: A chief or leader.
entries.example: For out of the shal come a captaine, whych shall govern my people israhel.

entries.definition: A person who manages the property or affairs for another entity.
entries.example: The estate's steward managed the farms and buildings.

entries.definition: Having a hardness and severity of nature or manner.
entries.example: I haue beene wooed, as I intreat thee now, / Euen by the ſterne, and direfull God of warre, / VVhoſe ſinowie necke in battel nere did bow, / VVho conquers where he comes in euery iarre; […]

entries.definition: A situation which poses an immediate risk and which requires urgent attention.
entries.example: Cardiac arrest is an emergency requiring medical attention.

entries.definition: Something or someone that has been ruined.
entries.example: He was an emotional wreck after the death of his wife.

entries.definition: A sudden, intense, loud sound, as made for example by cymbals.
entries.example: The piece ended in a crescendo, building up to a crash of cymbals.

entries.definition: A violent collision or compression; a crash; destruction; ruin.
entries.example: The more highly the injured part is endowed with sensory nerves the more marked is the shock; a crush of the hand, for example, is attended with a more intense degree of shock than a correspondingly severe crush of the foot

entries.definition: Any of the following symbols: ‒ (figure dash), – (en dash), — (em dash), or ― (horizontal bar).
entries.example: She used a dash to add an explanation at the end of the sentence.

entries.definition: To become invisible or to move out of view unnoticed.
entries.example: Holly, mistletoe, red berries, ivy, turkeys, geese, game, poultry, brawn, meat, pigs, sausages, oysters, pies, puddings, fruit, and punch, all vanished instantly.

entries.definition: To vanish.
entries.example: The mountains disappear behind clouds in the afternoon.

entries.definition: Chance; accident, unpredictability.
entries.example: I will stand the hazard of the die.

entries.definition: Standard spelling of harbor.
entries.example: In West Wales it has never been possible until recently to exploit the magnificent natural harbour of Milford Haven, for there was no industrial hinterland.

entries.definition: Any of the genus Rumex of coarse weedy plants with small green flowers related to buckwheat, especially bitter dock (Rumex obtusifolius), and used as potherbs and in folk medicine, especially in curing nettle rash.
entries.example: And vnder neath him his courageous ſteed, / The fierce Spumador trode them downe like docks […]

entries.definition: A tool used to moor a vessel to the bottom of a sea or river to resist movement.
entries.example: Men that I knew around Wapatomac didn't wear high, shiny plug hats, nor yeller spring overcoats, nor carry canes with ivory heads as big as a catboat's anchor, as you might say.

entries.definition: To sink out of sight.
entries.example: The submarine submerged in the water.

entries.definition: A person who sails; one whose occupation is sailing or navigating ships or other waterborne craft.
entries.example: He's a talented sailor and has spent many years at sea.

entries.definition: Synonym of sailor, particularly on a maritime vessel.
entries.example: But was it responsible governance to pass the Longitude Act without other efforts to protect British seamen? Or might it have been subterfuge—a disingenuous attempt to shift attention away from the realities of their life at sea. […] Conditions were horrendous aboard most British naval vessels at the time. Scurvy and other diseases ran rampant, killing more seamen each year than all other causes combined, including combat.

entries.definition: A person or object that carries someone or something else.
entries.example: armored personnel carrier

entries.definition: A device or object that works by the operation of steam.
entries.example: Use a steamer to cook the vegetables without boiling them.

entries.definition: Someone who fits a lining to something.
entries.example: a liner of shoes

entries.definition: A craft for transportation on or in water, air, or space.
entries.example: But my hope was, that if I stood along this coast till I came to that part where the English traded, I should find some of their vessels upon their usual design of trade, that would relieve and take us in.

entries.definition: To carry; transport; convey.
entries.example: Trucks plowed through the water to ferry flood victims to safety.

entries.definition: A piece of fabric attached to a boat and arranged such that it causes the wind to drive the boat along. The sail may be attached to the boat via a combination of mast, spars and ropes.
entries.example: When we haue laught to ſee the ſailes conceiue / And grow big bellied with the wanton winde; […]

entries.definition: A flat-bottomed craft able to float and drift on water, used for transport or as a waterborne platform.
entries.example: They floated down the river on an inflatable raft

entries.definition: A small long and narrow boat, propelled by one or more people (depending on the size of canoe), using single-bladed paddles. The paddlers face in the direction of travel, in either a seated position, or kneeling on the bottom of the boat. Canoes are open on top, and pointed at both ends.
entries.example: The canoe is of pure black oak, and is in excellent preservation.

entries.definition: A type of lever used to propel a boat, having a flat blade at one end and a handle at the other, and pivoted in a rowlock atop the gunwale, whereby a rower seated in the boat and pulling the handle can pass the blade through the water by repeated strokes against the water's resistance, thus moving the boat.
entries.example:
The oar snaps in his hand
Before he reaches dry land
But the sound doesn't deafen his smile
Just pokes at wet sand
With an oar in his hand
Floats off down the river Nile
Floats off down the river Nile...

entries.definition: Any raised flat surface that can be walked on: a balcony; a porch; a raised patio; a flat rooftop.
entries.example: We ate breakfast on the wooden deck behind the house.

entries.definition: Any of various rotary machines that use the kinetic energy of a continuous stream of fluid (a liquid or a gas) to turn a shaft.
entries.example: Upstream from the house is a watermill, cased in gleaming white weather-boarding, which has been restored to working order. Near by is the water-driven turbine which [Rudyard] Kipling had installed in 1902 to light his mansion with electricity.

entries.definition: A rotating device with blades that pushes an aircraft or boat through air or water.
entries.example: The boat's propeller churned the water as it moved away.

entries.definition: On board; into or within a ship or boat; hence, into or within a railway car.
entries.example: We all climbed aboard.

entries.definition: To go aboard a craft or vessel for transportation.
entries.example: All passengers please embark now.

entries.definition: The hollow bed of running waters; (also) the bed of the sea or other body of water.
entries.example: The water coming out of the waterwheel created a standing wave in the channel.

entries.definition: An artificial waterway or artificially improved river used for travel, shipping, or irrigation.
entries.example: The canal carries boats between the river and the harbour.

entries.definition: A trench; a long, shallow indentation, as for irrigation or drainage.
entries.example: Digging ditches has long been considered one of the most demanding forms of manual labor.

entries.definition: A permanent track consisting of fixed metal rails to drive trains or similar motorized vehicles on.
entries.example: Many railroads roughly follow the trace of older land or water roads.

entries.definition: A transport system using rails used to move passengers or goods.
entries.example: That the young Mr. Churchills liked—but they did not like him coming round of an evening and drinking weak whisky-and-water while he held forth on railway debentures and corporation loans. Mr. Barrett, however, by fawning and flattery, seemed to be able to make not only Mrs. Churchill but everyone else do what he desired.

entries.definition: The power unit of a train that pulls the coaches or wagons.
entries.example: As on all other British Railways standard locomotives to date, the lubrication of motion pins and reversing gear is by grease nipple and gun.

entries.definition: An underground railway, especially for mass transit of people in urban areas.
entries.example: He is going to Westminster by subway.

entries.definition: Below the ground; below the surface of the Earth.
entries.example: There is an underground tunnel that takes you across the river.

entries.definition: An underground or underwater passage.
entries.example: In 1865 an outfit called the East London Railway Company bought the Brunel tunnel for £800,000, and in 1869 they opened a railway through it.

entries.definition: A horizontal bar extending between supports and used for support or as a barrier; a railing.
entries.example: Old Applegate, in the stern, just set and looked at me, and Lord James, amidship, waved both arms and kept hollering for help. I took a couple of everlasting big strokes and managed to grab hold of the skiff's rail, close to the stern.

entries.definition: To leave.
entries.example:
[…] he that hath no ſtomacke to this feaſt,
Let him depart, […]

entries.definition: To reach; to get to a certain place.
entries.example: We've just arrived at the hotel to book in, so we should arrive at Mike’s in time for lunch.

entries.definition: The place to which someone or something is going.
entries.example: The coastal town has become a popular holiday destination.
entries.usage: Typical combinations: final destination, tourist destination, reach a destination.

entries.definition: A period of time before an event occurs; the act of delaying; procrastination; lingering inactivity.
entries.example: the delay before the echo of a sound

entries.definition: To delay or put off an event, appointment, etc.
entries.example: “[…] Churchill, my dear fellow, we have such greedy sharks, and wolves in lamb's clothing. Oh, dear, there's so much to tell you, so many warnings to give you, but all that must be postponed for the moment.”

entries.definition: To delay or postpone.
entries.example: We're going to defer the decision until we have all the facts.

entries.definition: A period of rest or soothing.
entries.example: There was a brief lull in the conversation while everyone considered the question.

entries.definition: To reach the end of a period of validity.
entries.example: My passport will expire next month.

entries.definition: Owed or owing.
entries.example: He is due four weeks of back pay.

entries.definition: The charge for sending an item by post.
entries.example: Postage is included in the price of the book.

entries.definition: An act of stamping the foot, paw or hoof.
entries.example: The horse gave two quick stamps and rose up on its hind legs.

entries.definition: A bag or wallet.
entries.example: What, loo, man, see here of dyce a bale; / A brydelynge caste for that is in thy male!

entries.definition: A small pack or package; a little bundle or parcel
entries.example: Don't throw the crisp packet on the floor!

entries.definition: Something which is packed, a parcel, a box, an envelope.
entries.example: A dirty package was left in my home.

entries.definition: To tie; to confine by any ligature.
entries.example: They that reap must sheaf and bind.

entries.definition: A package wrapped, as for shipment or transport.
entries.example: I saw a brown paper parcel on my doorstep.

entries.definition: A burden; a weight to be carried.
entries.example: I struggled up the hill with the heavy load in my rucksack.

entries.definition: A heavy load.
entries.example:
I know that this was Life,—the track
⁠Whereon with equal feet we fared;
⁠And then, as now, the day prepared
The daily burden for the back.

entries.definition: To move or pass from one place, person or thing to another.
entries.example: to transfer the laws of one country to another; to transfer suspicion

entries.definition: To send or convey from one person, place or thing to another.
entries.example: The radio can transmit messages over long distances.

entries.definition: The act of passing over, across, or through something.
entries.example: In France you are now […] in the transit from one form of government to another.

entries.definition: To set free from restraint or danger.
entries.example: The hostage was delivered from her captors and thus preserved from any danger.

entries.definition: To move (something) from one place to another.
entries.example: Air conveys sound. Water is conveyed through the pipe.

entries.definition: The state of moving quickly or the capacity for rapid motion.
entries.example: How does Usain Bolt run at that speed?

entries.definition: A vector quantity that denotes the rate of change of position with respect to time, combining speed with a directional component.
entries.example: A car racing in a circle may retain the same speed while continually changing its velocity.

entries.definition: Fast; quick; rapid.
entries.example: swift action

entries.definition: A state where sovereignty rests with the people or their representatives, rather than with a monarch or emperor; a country with no monarchy.
entries.example: The United States is a republic; Norway is a constitutional monarchy.

entries.definition: The socialist and communist philosophy and political program founded by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels.
entries.example: The seminar examines Marxism and its influence on political movements.

entries.definition: Any of various economic and political theories advocating collective or governmental ownership and administration of the means of production and distribution of goods.
entries.example: Soil improvement often involves the movement of large quantities of earth, but the Chinese peasants face this task with a high degree of enthusiasm for socialism.

entries.definition: Any far-left political ideology or philosophy advocating holding the production of resources collectively, especially by seizing it through revolution.
entries.example: I want to gather together about twenty souls and sail away from this world of war and squalor and found a little colony where there shall be no money but a sort of communism as far as necessaries of life go, and some real decency.

entries.definition: Mode of rule or management.
entries.example: a prison regime

entries.definition: The body with the power to make and/or enforce laws to control a country, land area, people or organization.
entries.example: British government has historically centred exclusively on London.

entries.definition: Power or right to make or enforce rules, give orders, or impose obligation; or a position having such power or right.
entries.example: I have the authority to penalise the staff in my department, but not the authority to sack them.

entries.definition: Concerning or relating to politics, the art and process of governing.
entries.example: Political principles are rarely absolute, as political logic holds an imperfect result by compromise is better than a theoretically perfect abstention from the political process in the opposition.

entries.definition: A body of authoritative officials organized in nested ranks.
entries.example: Gay men and bisexuals were blamed for the [AIDS] epidemic for much the same reason that the church hierarchy in the Middle Ages accused Jewish people of creating bubonic plague by "poisoning the wells."

entries.definition: A system of government in which people choose their leaders by voting or decide policies themselves.
entries.example: Free elections are an important part of democracy.

entries.definition: Government by bureaus or their administrators or officers.
entries.example: However, when Britain left the European Union, ferries started to ply a direct sea link from Ireland, to save hauliers from custom's bureaucracy of driving via Britain.

entries.definition: Characterized by social equality and equal rights for all people.
entries.example: Ladies of yesteryear toured world capitals in sedate linen dresses, but such priggish frumpery hardly presents Americans as the carefree, egalitarian, and sensuous people the viewers of dubbed Baywatch episodes have come to expect.

entries.definition: Constant concern over material possessions and wealth; a great or excessive regard for worldly concerns.
entries.example: We accept that a third of the population live on the poverty line. We accept that only a handful of the most exceptional of the children of the poor will make it through to a third-level education. We accept massive examples of greed and dishonesty in public life. We except the values of materialism. What do we expect then—to be left un-harassed, we who have all the privileges?

entries.definition: A political upheaval in a government or state characterized by great change.
entries.example: The revolution had completely transformed the monarchy into a republic.

entries.definition: The change of something that is defective, broken, inefficient or otherwise negative, in order to correct or improve it
entries.example: The elections need to undergo a serious reform.

entries.definition: A series of events leading to a result or product.
entries.example: This product of last month's quality standards committee is quite good, even though the process was flawed.

entries.definition: A person who favors maintenance of the status quo.
entries.example: During the late 1950s and throughout the 1960s, this commitment brought him into frequent critical confrontation with entrenched forms of conservative thinking (in academic areas from history and social science to the more abstract domains of ethical and political philosophy),[…]

entries.definition: A severe breakdown or crisis involving loss of control.
entries.example: The banking crisis triggered a financial meltdown.

entries.definition: Of or pertaining to a municipality (a city or a corporation having the right of administering local government).
entries.example: More than 100 provincial and municipal firefighters were brought in, with helicopters and aircraft used to drop water and fire retardant, while bulldozers were digging firebreaks.

entries.definition: Not taking sides in a conflict such as war; nonaligned.
entries.example: The country remained neutral during the conflict.

entries.definition: Having two sides.
entries.example: General Wego W.K. Chiang, secretary general of the National Security Council, said that the visit of El Salvador Vice President Merino to Taipei on behalf of President Alfredo Cristiani was in response to an invitation of the ROC [Republic of China] Government which hopes to further strengthen bilateral relations between the two countries.

entries.definition: An enclosed area, often outdoor, for the presentation of sporting events (sports arena) or other spectacular events; earthen area, often oval, specifically for rodeos (North America) or circular area for bullfights (especially Hispanic America).
entries.example: A large crowd filled the seats of the arena.

entries.definition: A piece of cloth, often decorated with an emblem, used as a visual signal or symbol.
entries.example: The vote in the Bundestag (parliament) on Thursday makes defiling foreign flags equal to the crime of defiling the German flag. […] The new law also applies to acts of defilement besides burning, such as publicly ripping a flag up.

entries.definition: A flag or standard used by a military commander, monarch or nation.
entries.example: “To hold Arrakis,” the Duke said, “one is faced with decisions that may cost one his self-respect.” He pointed out the window to the Atreides green and black banner hanging limply from a staff at the edge of the landing field. "That honorable banner could come to mean many evil things."

entries.definition: The head of state of a republic, sometimes also the head of government as well, particularly (US politics) the head of the executive branch of the federal government of the United States of America.
entries.example: The vast majority of presidents have been male.

entries.definition: Foremost; first or highest in quality or degree.
entries.example:
2004, Philip Moore, Scouting an Anthropology of Sport, Anthropologica, Volume 46, Number 1, Canadian Anthropology Society, page 40,
This failure, for a team associated with one of the premier Australian Rules Football teams with the longest of traditions, is truly enormous.

entries.definition: A person who is trained to preach, to perform religious ceremonies, and to afford pastoral care at a Protestant church.
entries.example: The minister said a prayer on behalf of the entire congregation.

entries.definition: A person who keeps records, takes notes and handles general clerical work.
entries.example: I have a personal secretary to help me organize my clients.

entries.definition: In many countries, the legislative branch of government, a deliberative assembly or set of assemblies whose elected or appointed members meet to debate the major political issues of the day, make, amend, and repeal laws, authorize the executive branch of government to collect and spend money, and in some cases exercise judicial powers; a legislature.
entries.example: The row started over who will run for parliament in a wealthy rightwing constituency on the left bank in Paris, a safe seat for Sarkozy's ruling UMP.

entries.definition: In some bicameral legislative systems, the upper house or chamber.
entries.example: The bill must pass the senate before it becomes law.

entries.definition: The act of consulting together formally; serious conversation or discussion; interchange of views.
entries.example: Nor with such free and friendly conference / As he hath used of old.

entries.definition: The act of persons or things that meet.
entries.example: Meeting him will be exciting. I enjoy meeting new people.

entries.definition: The military installation from which troops are commanded and orders are issued; the military unit consisting of a commander and his support staff.
entries.example: The commander returned to headquarters for the briefing.

entries.definition: An act of delegating.
entries.example: Decentralisation of the railways was provided for by the establishment of Area Boards for each Region, which began to function on January 1, 1955, and by the extended delegation of powers to the Boards and their General Managers; […].

entries.definition: The interest, benefit, or wellbeing of someone or something.
entries.example: She appeared on behalf of the U.N. Secretary General at a conference held in behalf of the world's children.

entries.definition: A constituted body of officers representing the civil authority of government, empowered to maintain public order and safety, enforce the law, and prevent, detect, and investigate crime.
entries.example:
There are nine Principles of Police:
...
7 To maintain at all times a relationship with the public that gives reality to the historic tradition that the police are the public and that the public are the police; the police being only members of the public who are paid to give full-time attention to duties which are incumbent on every citizen, in the interests of community welfare and existence.

entries.definition: A man who is a leader in national or international affairs.
entries.example: The experienced statesman helped negotiate the peace agreement.

entries.definition: The chief executive of the municipal government of a city, borough, etc., formerly (historical) usually appointed as a caretaker by European royal courts but now usually appointed or elected locally.
entries.example: The office of mayor has been the tomb of many political ambitions.

entries.definition: An act of being of assistance to someone.
entries.example: I say I did him a service by ending our relationship – now he can freely pursue his career.

entries.definition: A ceremonial duty or service, particularly
entries.example: Golde (gaue he him)[…]for all maner of veſſels of euery offyce[…]

entries.definition: An administrative unit of government; office.
entries.example: Ashley Johnson is an energy, trade and economics expert at the National Bureau of Asian Research, based in the United States.

entries.definition: A part, portion, or subdivision.
entries.example: The customer service department handles complaints and returns.

entries.definition: The act of administering; government of public affairs; the service rendered, or duties assumed, in conducting affairs; the conducting of any office or employment; direction.
entries.example: […] the fact that the propertied classes are no longer the best educated, and the fact that the large number of people who owe their position solely to their general education do not possess that experience of the working of the economic system which the administration of property gives are important to understanding the role of the intellectual.

entries.definition: To govern, rule or control by superior authority or power.
entries.example: The title of this article evokes memories of the beginning of World War II and reveals one method dictators use to increase their power. In China’s case, Xi Jinping’s Anschluss of Hong Kong in June 2020 fits nicely with the way Hitler began his initial European expansion strategy, called Lebensraum (living space). In Zweites Buch, Hitler said that to dominate the world, Germany must expand its borders and areas it controls. The first way to start achieving Lebensraum would be through Anschluss — the unification of Austria and Germany. Further, he envisioned an expansion that would include Poland, Czechoslovakia, the rest of Europe and Russia.

entries.definition: The ability to do or undergo something.
entries.example: He has lost the power to speak.

entries.definition: The power to affect, control or manipulate something or someone; the ability to change the development of fluctuating things such as conduct, thoughts or decisions.
entries.example: I have absolutely no influence over him.

entries.definition: Influence someone or something.
entries.example: Higher rents affect students who live away from home.
entries.usage: Affect takes a direct object: affect attendance. Avoid adding on after affect.

entries.definition: The quality or condition of being important or worthy of note.
entries.example: The recording speed is also of importance in detecting flutters of high frequency.

entries.definition: The extent to which something matters; importance
entries.example: As a juror your opinion is of great significance for the outcome of the trial.

entries.definition: Non-Oxford British English and Australian standard spelling of organization.
entries.example: […] a number of commentators have noted how, during meetings and in committees, for example, organisation members often experience an attack of the sillies by playing the fool and horsing around.

entries.definition: The act of associating.
entries.example: And it is a characteristic of man that he alone has any sense of good and evil, of just and unjust, and the like, and the association of living beings who have this sense makes a family and a state.

entries.definition: The act of uniting or joining two or more things into one.
entries.example: The union of the two organisations created a larger charity.

entries.definition: A group sharing common characteristics, such as the same language, law, religion, or tradition.
entries.example: [W]e are not borne to our ſelues alone, but the prince, the countrie, the parents, freends, wiues, children and familie, euerie of them doo claime an intereſt in vs, and to euerie of them we muſt be beneficiall: otherwiſe we doo degenerate from that communitie and ſocietie, which by ſuch offices by vs is to be conſtrued, & doo become moſt vnprofitable: […]

entries.definition: An association or combination of businesses, financial institutions, or investors, for the purpose of engaging in a joint venture.
entries.example: A consortium of construction firms won the contract.

entries.definition: A group or association of cooperating members.
entries.example: the League of Nations

entries.definition: A long-established organization or type of organization, particularly one involved with education, public service, or charity work.
entries.example: The University of the South Pacific is the only internationally accredited institution of higher education in Oceania.

entries.definition: To bring together as one.
entries.example: The new government will try to unite the various factions.

entries.definition: Being the only one of its kind; unequaled, unparalleled or unmatched.
entries.example: Every person has a unique life, therefore every person has a unique journey.

entries.definition: A historically constituted, stable community of people, formed based on a common language, territory, economic life, ethnicity and/or psychological make-up manifested in a common culture.
entries.example: The Roma are a nation without a country.

entries.definition: Concerning all parts of the world.
entries.example: Pollution is a global problem.

entries.definition: Spanning the world; global.
entries.example: A large meteorite impact would cause worldwide extinction of life.

entries.definition: Pertaining to a league or treaty; derived from an agreement or covenant between parties, especially between nations.
entries.example: Yet the Romans, taking them [the Carthaginians] at an Advantage, vvhen they vvere in Streights; compell'd them, contrary to all Fœderal Right and Juſtice, by Nevv Articles, both to part with Sardinia, their Lavvful Territory, and alſo to pay them for the future, a Double Tribute.

entries.definition: Abroad, especially across the sea.
entries.example: Overseas branches of the company are doing well.

entries.definition: Located outside a country or place, especially one's own.
entries.example: foreign markets; foreign soil

entries.definition: Beyond the bounds of a country; in foreign countries.
entries.example: A closer look at North Korean history reveals what Pyongyang’s leaders really want their near-farcical belligerence to achieve — a reminder to the world that North Korea exists, and an impression abroad that its leaders are irrational and unpredictable.

entries.definition: Having to do with people and government office as opposed to the military or religion.
entries.example: She went into civil service because she wanted to help the people.

entries.definition: To leave the country in which one lives, especially one's native country, in order to reside elsewhere.
entries.example: Forced to emigrate in a body to America.

entries.definition: To move into a foreign country to stay permanently.
entries.example: He knows hardship. He has experienced life in a cold-water flat in Moldova before he immigrated to the States.

entries.definition: The exercise of sovereign power.
entries.example: England prospered under Elizabeth I's reign.

entries.definition: Any small model of a person or animal able to be moved by strings or rods, or in the form of a glove.
entries.example: The performer moved the puppet's arms with thin strings.

entries.definition: An impressive seat used by a monarch, often on a raised dais in a throne room and reserved for formal occasions.
entries.example: He approached the throne reverently.

entries.definition: A royal, imperial or princely headdress; a diadem.
entries.example: Before so many of Europe's crowns came tumbling off the heads of their royal owners, Continental Europe could show a rich variety in the matter of royal trains.

entries.definition: Something twisted, intertwined, or curled.
entries.example: a wreath of smoke    a wreath of clouds

entries.definition: Relating to the former Soviet Union.
entries.example: The museum displays Soviet spacecraft.

entries.definition: A country and archipelago of Oceania, to the east of Australia. Official name: New Zealand. Capital: Wellington.
entries.example:
The government of New Zealand is looking for a crew to lead the redevelopment of its research headquarters in Antarctica.
Built in the 1980s, the country’s Scott Base consists of 12 structures that officials want replaced by three large, interconnected buildings, plus a separate helicopter hangar.

entries.definition: A nation or civilization occupying the country around the Rhine, Elbe, and upper Danube Rivers in Central Europe, taken as a whole under its various governments.
entries.example: Ancient Germany, excluding from its independent limits the province weſtward of the Rhine, which had ſubmitted to the Roman yoke, extended itſelf over a third part of Europe. Almoſt the whole of modern Germany, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Livonia, Pruſſia, and the greater part of Poland, were peopled by the various tribes of one great nation, whoſe complexion, manners, and language, denoted a common origin and preſerved a ſtriking reſemblance.

entries.definition: A geographical area under the remote control of a country; especially to extract resources or exploit labor from that area.
entries.example: Much of the eastern United States was formerly a British colony; other areas were French, Spanish, Dutch, or Swedish colonies.

entries.definition: The condition of being free.
entries.example: The army is here, your liberty is assured.

entries.definition: The quality or state of being independent; lack of dependence; the state of not being reliant on, or controlled by, others.
entries.example: In 1947, India gained independence from the British Empire.

entries.definition: A dilapidated neighborhood where many people live in a state of poverty.
entries.example: Go to the half built-upon slums behind Battlebridge […] you will find groups of boys […] squatting in the mud, among the rubbish, the broken bricks, the dust-heaps, and the fragments of timber […]

entries.definition: A state of safety, protection or shelter.
entries.example: Rocks, dens, and caves! But I in none of these / Find place or refuge.

entries.definition: A place of safety or refuge.
entries.example: All the busy concerns of daily existence were utterly abhorrent to me. I loathed the sound of others' voices—I hated to be mixed up with their petty routine of ordinary cares; here was an asylum offered to me—here I might lay down all the offices of humanity, and dwell beside that grave whose rest was now my only desire.

entries.definition: All the people living in an area, or a group being studied.
entries.example: The population of the district doubled over twenty years.
entries.usage: Typical combinations: population growth, ageing population, population density.

entries.definition: Connected with the characteristics of a population.
entries.example: Demographic changes have increased demand for healthcare.
entries.usage: Typical combinations: demographic change, demographic data, demographic trend.

entries.definition: A resident of a city or town, especially one with legally recognized rights or duties.
entries.example: [T]hat large body of the working men who were not counted as citizens and had not so much as a vote to serve as an anodyne to their stomachs were likely to get impatient.

entries.definition: A person, animal or plant living at a certain location or in a certain area.
entries.example: The tiger is a resident of the Lower Amoor, and ranges as high as 53° north latitude. In winter he roams through the same forests with the reindeer, and occasionally dines upon venison of his own catching.

entries.definition: Of or relating to a group of people having common racial, ancestral, national, religious or cultural origins.
entries.example: The violence began when Serbian troops went into Croatia ostensibly to aid armed ethnic Serbians trying to create their own autonomous states there.

entries.definition: Of or relating to a race (or a people).
entries.example: the racial complexion

entries.definition: A group of people all descended from a common ancestor, in fact or belief, especially when the exact genealogies are not known.
entries.example: Members of the clan traced their ancestry to the same founder.

entries.definition: Permission from a company to sell its goods or services under its business system.
entries.example: They bought a franchise to open a restaurant under the company's name.
entries.usage: Selected the common business sense rather than voting rights.

entries.definition: To give a title to.
entries.example: The deed entitled her to an undivided interest in the property.

entries.definition: The selection of one thing or person over others (with the main adposition being "for" in relation to the thing or person, but possibly also "of")
entries.example: He has a preference for crisp wines.

entries.definition: A formalized choice on legally relevant measures such as employment or appointment to office or a proceeding about a legal dispute.
entries.example: The city council decided the matter should go to public vote.

entries.definition: To choose someone for an official position by voting.
entries.example: The residents will elect a new mayor in November.

entries.definition: One who responds; one who replies.
entries.example: Each respondent completed the survey anonymously.

entries.definition: A survey of people, usually statistically analyzed to gauge wider public opinion.
entries.example: A recent poll asked residents whether they supported the new tram line.

entries.definition: Eager or inordinate desire for some object that confers distinction, as preferment, honor, superiority, political power, or fame; desire to distinguish one's self from other people.
entries.example: My daughter, Johanna, wants to be a firefighter very much. She has a lot of ambition.

entries.definition: To name someone as a candidate for a particular role or position, including that of an office.
entries.example: We will nominate one student to represent our class.

entries.definition: A list of tasks to be completed, names to be consulted, conditions to be verified and similar.
entries.example: Use a checklist to ensure that nothing is left behind.

entries.definition: The act or process of following another person or thing.
entries.example: The company has a clear plan for succession when its director retires.

entries.definition: The condition or feeling of being safe; security; certainty.
entries.example: If you push it to the limit, safety is not guaranteed.

entries.definition: Health, safety, happiness and prosperity; well-being in any respect.
entries.example: Nothing was too small to receive attention, if a supervising eye could suggest improvements likely to conduce to the common welfare. Mr. Gordon Burnage, for instance, personally visited dust-bins and back premises, accompanied by a sort of village bailiff, going his round like a commanding officer doing billets.

entries.definition: A state of health, happiness or prosperity.
entries.example: which concernes our whole three Kingdomes, Parliaments, Religion, and every one of our well-beings, in this preſent world

entries.definition: Agreement or accord.
entries.example:
December 4 2010, Evan Thomas, "Why It’s Time to Worry", in Newsweek
America's social harmony has depended at least to some degree on economic growth. It is easier to get along when everyone, more or less, is getting ahead.

entries.definition: Firm in standing or position; not tottering or shaking; fixed; firm.

entries.definition: To thrive or grow well.
entries.example: The barley flourished in the warm weather.

entries.definition: To follow something in sequence or time.
entries.example: Autumn succeeds summer.

entries.definition: The region which the eye overlooks at one time; a view; a scene; an outlook.
entries.example: As when a Scout[…]Obtains the brow of ſome high-climbing Hill, / Which to his eye diſcovers unaware / The goodly proſpect of ſome forein land / Firſt-ſeen, or ſome renownd Metropolis / With gliſtering Spires and Pinnacles adornd, / Which now the Riſing Sun guilds with his beams.

entries.definition: A view, vista or outlook.
entries.example: And according to Hughes, HM Treasury is still sceptical about rail electrification. "It's not because they don't see electrification as a good thing, but I think when you look at it from the UK-wide perspective, if you have £x billion to spend on decarbonisation, you don't necessarily start with rail. Rail's not where you get the biggest bang for the buck in terms of decarbonisation."

entries.definition: The position from which something is observed or considered
entries.example: From the top of the hill you get a good viewpoint of the town.

entries.definition: A point of view; a perspective.
entries.example: Bathing once a month may save time, but from a cleanliness standpoint, it's not effective.

entries.definition: A place from which something can be viewed.
entries.example: Perched on the edge of the cliff was a hidden outlook.

entries.definition: A non-specific rule or principle that provides direction to action or behaviour.
entries.example: He considered the Ten Commandments more as a guideline than a requirement.

entries.definition: A set of principles guiding right and wrong behaviour.
entries.example: A strong work ethic helps her finish difficult tasks on time.
entries.usage: Selected the ordinary noun rather than the uncommon adjective.

entries.definition: To imply but stop short of explicitly stating (something).

entries.definition: To give advice to; to offer an opinion to, as worthy or expedient to be followed.
entries.example: The dentist advised me to brush three times a day.

entries.definition: Something which is proposed, or offered for consideration or acceptance.
entries.example: proposals for the construction of a new building

entries.definition: A clue.
entries.example: I needed a hint to complete the crossword.

entries.definition: To assert or announce formally, officially, explicitly, or emphatically.
entries.example: He declared him innocent.

entries.definition: To agree, verify or concur; to answer positively.
entries.example: She affirmed that she would go when I asked her.

entries.definition: A demand of ownership made for something.
entries.example: a claim of ownership

entries.definition: To announce or declare.

entries.definition: A condition; a set of circumstances applying at any given time.
entries.example: a state of being

entries.definition: To give public notice of, especially for the first time; to make known.
entries.example: Her [Queen Elizabeth’s] arrival was announced through the country by a peal of cannon from the ramparts.

entries.definition: To make or become clear or bright by freeing from impurities or turbidity.
entries.example: What's the best way to clarify cooking oil?

entries.definition: To help.
entries.example: This book will assist you in getting your life in order.

entries.definition: Help; assistance; succor, relief.
entries.example: He came to my aid when I was foundering.

entries.definition: To mentally support; to motivate, give courage, hope or spirit.
entries.example: I encouraged him during his race.

entries.definition: To bring about; to put into practice; to carry out.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: realize, actualize, materialize; embody; accomplish

entries.definition: Someone who watches over something; a person in charge of something or someone.

entries.definition: To allow to enter; to grant entrance (to), whether into a place, into the mind, or into consideration.

entries.definition: Of or pertaining to Africa.

entries.definition: Related to Europe.

entries.definition: Following the religion of Judaism.

entries.definition: Related to Arabia.

entries.definition: Of or pertaining to Portugal.

entries.definition: Upright, as opposed to italic.

entries.definition: Of or pertaining to Russia or Russians.

entries.definition: Of or pertaining to Spain.
entries.example: Spanish borders

entries.definition: Of, from, or pertaining to Switzerland or the Swiss people.

entries.definition: Of or relating to Greece, its people, its language, or its culture.

entries.definition: Pertaining to Italy.
entries.example: Italian borders

entries.definition: An island of Oceania.

This is all that I can have a certain knowledge of as to that side of Australia ...

entries.definition: A country in North America. Capital: Ottawa. Largest city: Toronto.
entries.example: Father narrated the story of how Canada developed over a short period to surpass other countries, including Britain, from which it had emerged.

entries.definition: The United Kingdom, a kingdom and country in Northern Europe including the island of Great Britain as well as Northern Ireland on the northeastern portion of the island of Ireland.
entries.example: With the eclipse of Empire, and the emergence of America and Russia, it was inevitable that we would lose comparative power and influence—and to be sure we have been in relative economic decline since the middle of the nineteenth century (when we were still producing two thirds of the world's energy, and half its iron and cotton cloth and when per capita income in Britain was over twice that in Germany and one third greater than in France).

entries.definition: A country located primarily in Western Europe. Official name: French Republic. Capital and largest city: Paris.
entries.example: For a long time the dormouse and polecat had seemed to him overfeeble enemies for his restless valour, even as the granary floor seemed to afford too narrow a field. Every day he read the papers of the previous day in the servants' hall of the houses he visited, and it appeared to him that this war in America, which was hailed as the awakening of the spirit of liberty and justice in the New World, ought to produce a revolution in France.

entries.definition: The system through which goods and services are produced, distributed, and consumed.
entries.example: Tourism contributes significantly to the local economy.
entries.usage: Common learner sense selected in place of an unsuitable or less useful source default.

entries.definition: The buying and selling of goods and services on a market.
entries.example: The new port increased trade between the two regions.

entries.definition: A gathering of people for the purchase and sale of merchandise, often periodic at a set time.
entries.example: The right to hold a weekly market was an invaluable privilege not given to all towns in the Middle Ages.

entries.definition: The tendency to work persistently.

entries.definition: A person who traffics in commodities for profit.

entries.definition: Related to finances.
entries.example: For financial reasons, we're not going to be able to continue to fund this program.

entries.definition: A sum or source of money.
entries.example: the fund of a bank, commercial house, manufacturing corporation, etc.

entries.definition: To make a donation; to give away something of value to support or contribute towards a cause or for the benefit of another.
entries.example: She donates 100 dollars to Red Cross every year.

entries.definition: To give property to (someone) as a gift; specifically, to provide (a person or institution) with support in the form of a permanent fund of money or other benefits.
entries.example: His [John, King of England's] Acts and Orders for the VVeale-publike vvere beyond moſt: hee being either the firſt, or the chiefeſt, vvho appointed thoſe noble Formes of Ciuill gouernement in London, and moſt Cities, and Incorporate Tovvnes of England, endovving them alſo vvith their greateſt Franchiſes; […]

entries.definition: An advertisement in a common media format, usually radio or television.
entries.example: She was in a commercial for breakfast cereal.

entries.definition: To give (especially public) notice of (something); to announce publicly.
entries.example: The shop will advertise its sale in the local newspaper.

entries.definition: A distinctive phrase of a person or group of people (such as a movement or political party); a motto.
entries.example: "Right-ho," I [Bertie Wooster] said, not much liking the assignment, but liking less the idea of endeavouring to thwart this incandescent aunt in her current frame of mind. Safety first, is the Wooster slogan.

entries.definition: To buy something.
entries.example: Customers can purchase tickets online.

entries.definition: An interest in land granting exclusive use or occupation of real estate for a limited period; a leasehold.
entries.example: Their lease gives them the right to occupy the flat for one year.

entries.definition: To incur, stand, or bear without serious detriment, as an act which might under other circumstances be injurious; (usually after an expression of ability, as could, able, difficult) to be able or rich enough; to spare.
entries.example: I think we can afford the extra hour it will take.  We can only afford to buy a small car at the moment.

entries.definition: The sale of goods directly to the consumer, encompassing the storefronts, mail-order, websites, etc., and the corporate mechanisms, branding, advertising, etc. that support them.
entries.example: She works in retail.

entries.definition: Retail foodstuffs and other household supplies.
entries.example:
1776: Adam Smith, The Wealth of Nations
Where ten thousand pounds can be employed in the grocery trade, the wages of the grocer's labour make but a very trifling addition...

entries.definition: To sell at a reduced price.
entries.example: Sales were slow even after the shop discounted the product.

entries.definition: An advancement in rank or position.
entries.example: I'll have to give myself a promotion!

entries.definition: A piece of paper or other token that entitles the holder to a discount, or that can be exchanged for goods and services.
entries.example: a voucher for a free kettle

entries.definition: A section of a ticket, showing the holder to be entitled to some specified accommodation or service, as to a passage over a designated line of travel, a particular seat in a theater, a discount, etc.
entries.example: Present the coupon to receive a discount on your ticket.

entries.definition: Money or other items used to facilitate transactions.
entries.example: Wampum was used as a currency by Amerindians.

entries.definition: An act of exchanging or trading.
entries.example: All in all, it was an even exchange.

entries.definition: To exchange or give (something) in an non-normal exchange (for something else).
