entries.definition: A document showing that something has been paid for.
entries.example: Keep your receipt in case you need to return the equipment.
entries.usage: Typical combinations: original receipt, request a receipt, proof of receipt.

entries.definition: A bill; a commercial document issued by a seller to a buyer indicating the products, quantities and agreed prices for products or services that the seller has already provided the buyer with. An invoice indicates that, unless paid in advance, payment is due by the buyer to the seller, according to the agreed terms.
entries.example: I've already rendered the invoices for payment.

entries.definition: Money or goods collected by a government (or an entity to whom the government has delegated this power, e.g. in tax farming) to fund itself and its services, for example by levying a charge on income, purchases (sales), property or harvest, other than that money which is collected by the government in exchange for specific goods (e.g. the purchase of surplus vehicles).
entries.example: [They paid a] "mushroom tax" in addition to their regular tax of butter and meat. They had to give 1 dre of dried mushrooms annually to the district administrative centres.

entries.definition: To impose (a tax or fine) to collect monies due, or to confiscate property.
entries.example: to levy a tax

entries.definition: A system of government-imposed duties levied on imported or exported goods; a list of such duties, or the duties themselves.
entries.example: This question may be placed in another light. It is agreed on all sides, that numbers are the best scale of wealth and taxation, as they are the only proper scale of representation. Would the convention have been impartial or consistent, if they had rejected the slaves from the list of inhabitants, when the shares of representation were to be calculated, and inserted them on the lists when the tariff of contributions was to be adjusted?

entries.definition: That which one is morally or legally obligated to do.
entries.example: Do your duty by me! -No, we don't have a duty to keep you abreast.

entries.definition: To apply, enforce, or establish (something, often regarded as burdensome as a restriction or tax: see verb sense 1.2.2) with authority.
entries.example: Congress imposed new tariffs.

entries.definition: To use up.
entries.example: The power plant consumes 30 tons of coal per hour.

entries.definition: To pay out (money).
entries.example: I've already spent hundreds of dollars buying dog chow.

entries.definition: To incur a charge of; to require payment of a (specified) price.
entries.example: This shirt cost $50, while this was cheaper at only $30.

entries.definition: A spending or consuming, often a disbursement of funds.
entries.example: She went to great expense to ensure her children would get the best education.

entries.definition: Money received by a business or government.
entries.example: Ticket sales provide most of the museum's revenue.
entries.usage: Typical combinations: annual revenue, generate revenue, tax revenue.

entries.definition: remarkably great, big, vast in an often unpleasant way; (of behaviour) Highly or conspicuously offensive.
entries.example: a gross mistake; gross injustice; gross negligence; a gross insult

entries.definition: The act or an instance of receding or withdrawing.
entries.example: […]that light may break forth from the deepest enclosures of darkness, and mercy may rejoice upon the recessions of justice, and grace may triumph upon the ruin of sin, and God may be glorified in the miracles of our conversion, and the wonders of our preservation and glories of our being saved.

entries.definition: A state of mind producing serious, long-term lowering of enjoyment of life or inability to visualize a happy future; any of several mental disorders with this state of mind as a central feature.
entries.example: I used to suffer from depression, but now I'm mostly content with my life.

entries.definition: A crucial or decisive point or situation; a turning point.
entries.example: The sudden loss of funding created a crisis for the charity.

entries.definition: The condition of not being threatened, especially physically, psychologically, emotionally, or financially.
entries.example: Chad always carries a gun for his own security.

entries.definition: A document constituting evidence of a long-term debt, by which the bond issuer (the borrower) is obliged to pay interest when due, and repay the principal at maturity, as specified on the face of the bond certificate. The rights of the holder are specified in the bond indenture, which contains the legal terms and conditions under which the bond was issued. Bonds are available in two forms: registered bonds, and bearer bonds.
entries.example: The company issued a bond that pays interest annually and is repaid after ten years.

entries.definition: An action, state of mind, or object one has an obligation to perform for another, adopt toward another, or give to another.
entries.example: Revenge the jeering and disdain'd contempt / Of this proud king, who studies day and night / To answer all the debt he owes to you / Even with the bloody payment of your deaths.

entries.definition: Deficiency in amount or quality; a falling short; lack.
entries.example: The crop output this year has been comparatively small, owing to the deficit in rainfall.

entries.definition: An act, instance of, or state of expansion or increase in size, especially by injection of a gas or liquid.
entries.example: The inflation of the balloon took five hours.

entries.definition: An act or instance of deflating.
entries.example: The loss caused utter deflation and disappointment among the fans.

entries.definition: To decrease, shrink, diminish, reduce in size or intensity.
entries.example: Their supplies began to dwindle after a week.

entries.definition: Of a quantity, to become smaller.
entries.example: The quality of our products has decreased since the main designer left.

entries.definition: To reduce in size or number.
entries.example: Joe and Edna moved to a bungalow after deciding to downsize when the children had left home.

entries.definition: Become smaller, fewer or weaker.
entries.example: The number of visitors declined after the admission fee increased.
entries.usage: Typical combinations: decline gradually, decline sharply, decline in.

entries.definition: To make smaller.
entries.example: The existence of many nations and national characters is part of the cultural wealth of mankind, and there is no reason to seek to diminish their number.

entries.definition: To bring down the size, quantity, quality, value or intensity of something; to diminish, to lower.
entries.example: to reduce weight, speed, heat, expenses, price, personnel etc.

entries.definition: (of a quantity, etc.) To become larger or greater, to greaten.
entries.example: His rage only increased when I told him of the lost money.

entries.definition: The action of increasing or becoming greater.
entries.example: the seminary that furnisheth matter for the formation and increment of animal and vegetable bodies

entries.definition: An increase in size, number, value, or strength.
entries.example: Nanoelectronics is one of the area's few growth industries .

entries.definition: To enhance.
entries.example: The new photographs enrich the museum's exhibition.

entries.definition: Of or relating to exportation or exports.
entries.example: The company ships its products in export packaging.

entries.definition: Something brought in from an exterior source, especially for sale or trade.
entries.example: Trump’s July 8 announcement of a 50% tariff on copper imports beginning August 1 sent prices surging 13% in one day, up to a record high of $5.69 per pound.

entries.definition: To increase (something) in extent or intensity; to intensify or step up.
entries.example: Violence escalated during the election.

entries.definition: To change (something) from a smaller form or size to a larger one; to spread out or lay open.
entries.example: You can expand this compact umbrella to cover a large table.

entries.definition: A flow inward or into something; a coming in.
entries.example: I'll buy a new computer when I get an influx of cash.

entries.definition: Someone who is wealthy.
entries.example: The affluents are most similar to the professional want-it-alls in their reasons for preferring specific hospitals and in their demographic characteristics.

entries.definition: An adequate quantity of; enough.
entries.example: We have sufficient supplies to last the winter.

entries.definition: Equal to or fulfilling some requirement.
entries.example: powers adequate to a great work

entries.definition: Extra.
entries.example: I have no spare time.

entries.definition: A reduction in cost or expenditure.
entries.example: The shift of the supplier gave us a saving of 10 percent.

entries.definition: Superfluous; exceeding what is necessary (and therefore no longer needed because other things fulfill its task or purpose).
entries.example: It is allowed, that Senates and great Councils are often troubled with redundant, ebullient, and other peccant Humours, with many Diſeaſes of the Head and more of the Heart; […]

entries.definition: A deficiency or need (of something desirable or necessary); an absence, want, dearth.
entries.example: It is a question of money, or lack of same.

entries.definition: A team; a group of people who work together for a common purpose.
entries.example: a company of knights

entries.definition: A business partnership; the name under which it trades.
entries.example: She works for a small accounting firm in the city centre.

entries.definition: A company, business, organization, or other purposeful endeavor.
entries.example: The government sponsored enterprises (GSEs) are a group of financial services corporations which have been created by the United States Congress.

entries.definition: One who exerts power, or has the power to act.
entries.example: Seeing we are so wonderfully endowed with priceless gifts by our Heavenly Father, will he not require usury at our hands? He will. But he has made us agents to ourselves, which makes us responsible for the way in which we use the talents he has given us, for the manner we expend the gold and silver, the wheat and fine flour, the cattle upon a thousand hills, and the wine and oil, for they all belong to Him

entries.definition: That which has a distinct existence as an individual unit, often used for organizations which have no physical form.
entries.example: The organisational and administrative tasks involved in welding the railways into a single entity have also received much publicity.

entries.definition: To spend money, time, or energy on something, especially for some benefit or purpose; used with in.
entries.example: We'd like to thank all the contributors who have invested countless hours into this event.

entries.definition: Ideas, advice or information contributed to a task or discussion.
entries.example: The designer asked for input from the users.

entries.definition: Anything that is produced; a result.
entries.example: The product of last month's quality standards committee is quite good, even though the process was flawed.

entries.definition: The act or process of acquiring.
entries.example: The acquisition of sports equipment can be fun in itself.

entries.definition: Items made or sold for use or trade.
entries.example: The goods arrived at the warehouse this morning.

entries.definition: Freight carried by a ship, aircraft, or motor vehicle.
entries.example: The plane was overloaded with cargo. It was a cargo of live animals.

entries.definition: To provide for compensation if some specified risk occurs. Often agreed by policy (contract) to offer financial compensation in case of an accident, theft or other undesirable event.
entries.example: I'm not insured against burglary.

entries.definition: Anything that assures a certain outcome.
entries.example: Can you give me a guarantee that he will be fit for the match?

entries.definition: Consistently dependable or producing trustworthy results.
entries.example: The team used a reliable method to measure air quality.
entries.usage: A reliable measurement is consistent across repetitions; validity concerns what it measures.

entries.definition: The process of achieving agreement through discussion.
entries.example: The specifics of the contract are still under negotiation.

entries.definition: Senses relating to caring for or waiting on someone, or accompanying or being present.
entries.example: The fift [beadsman] had charge ſick perſons to attend, / And comfort thoſe, in point of death vvhich lay; […]

entries.definition: Being away from a place; withdrawn from a place; existing but not present; (sometimes) missing.
entries.example: Owing to his own illness and then his family's, Ramzi has often been absent from class this month. We will help him catch up with his studies.

entries.definition: An exchange of goods or services for currency or credit.
entries.example: He celebrated after the sale of company.

entries.definition: The sale of products, often in large quantities, to retailers or other merchants.
entries.example: The company sells its products wholesale to local shops.

entries.definition: A public event where goods or property are sold to the highest bidder.
entries.example: Auctions come in a wide variety. In a “Dutch auction”, often used to sell flowers and fruit, prices start high and gradually drop until a bidder is willing to pay up. A “Japanese auction” is a bit like poker: bids rise with each round and anyone who wants to win must bid every time. Vendors using auctions rid themselves of the headache of choosing prices and instead just pick the rules bidders must follow.

entries.definition: twice a day, two times per day
entries.example: It has been repeatedly documented that moving patients from a TID dosing regimen to BID or OD vastly improves compliance, and thus the medicine's effectiveness.

entries.definition: An indefinite quantity or amount; a lot (now usually qualified by great or good).
entries.example: There is a vast deal of difference in memories, as well as in every thing else, and therefore you should make allowance for your cousin, and pity her deficiency.

entries.definition: The act of conducting or carrying out (business, negotiations, plans).
entries.example: The transaction was made on Friday with the supplier.

entries.definition: The amount of money taken as sales transacted in a given period.
entries.example: The company had an annual turnover of $500,000.

entries.definition: A place where waste or garbage is left; a ground or place for dumping ashes, refuse, etc.; a disposal site.
entries.example: a toxic waste dump

entries.definition: A proportional part or share; the share or proportion assigned to each in a division.
entries.example: Each team received an equal quota of the available materials.

entries.definition: A portion of something, especially a portion given or allotted to someone.
entries.example: Each of the robbers took a share of the loot.

entries.definition: An advantage; help or aid from something.
entries.example: She can't read, so the voice recording was made for her benefit.

entries.definition: The price paid for obtaining, or price received for providing, money or goods in a credit transaction, calculated as a fraction of the amount or value of what was borrowed.
entries.example: Our bank offers borrowers an annual interest of 5%.

entries.definition: A store or supply.
entries.example: The shop keeps a large stock of batteries.

entries.definition: A registry of pecuniary transactions; a written or printed statement of business dealings or debts and credits, and also of other things subjected to a reckoning or review.
entries.example: The firm failed to file its accounts on time.

entries.definition: Sediment or rock that is not native to its present location or is different from the surrounding material. Sometimes refers to ore or gems.
entries.example: Newly discovered oil and gas deposits at Nan-ch'ung in Szechwan also promise to be of increasing importance.

entries.definition: One of several payments made at agreed intervals to pay a total amount.
entries.example: We paid the first instalment when we signed the agreement.

entries.definition: A written order directing a bank to pay money to a person or entity.
entries.example: I was not carrying cash, so I wrote a cheque for the amount.

entries.definition: Money in the form of notes or bills and coins, as opposed to checks, credit or electronic transactions.
entries.example: How are you off for cash? After you bounced those checks last time, they want to be paid in cash.

entries.definition: A piece of currency, usually metallic and in the shape of a disc, but sometimes polygonal, or with a hole in the middle.
entries.example: ...the coins were of all countries and sizes - doubloons, and louis d'ors, and guineas, and pieces of eight...

entries.definition: The currency of Kenya, Somalia, Tanzania and Uganda.
entries.example: The price is quoted in Kenyan shillings.

entries.definition: A reddish-brown metallic chemical element (symbol Cu) with the atomic number 29; also, the metal made up of this element.
entries.example: Men talke much […] of the Philoſophers ſtone, that it turneth copper into gold; […]

entries.definition: A collection of valuable things; accumulated wealth; a stock of money, jewels, etc.
entries.example: It seems there was a worm that slept upon a pile of treasure, which it had zealously heaped up under a stone bluff.

entries.definition: Riches; a great amount of valuable assets or material possessions.
entries.example: Money talks, but true wealth whispers.

entries.definition: The collective property and liabilities of someone, especially a deceased person.
entries.example: The lawyer divided the estate according to the will.

entries.definition: To have (something) as, or as if as, an owner; to have, to own.
entries.example: He does not even possess a working telephone.

entries.definition: Money or property bequeathed to someone in a will.
entries.example: Her grandfather left her a small legacy in his will.

entries.definition: Senses relating to moving from a higher to a lower position.
entries.example: they descended the river in boats

entries.definition: To return (money) to (someone); to reimburse.
entries.example: If you find this computer for sale anywhere at a lower price, we’ll refund you the difference.

entries.definition: Of the same rank; equal.
entries.example: two coordinate terms

entries.definition: To work together with others to achieve a common goal.
entries.example: Let's collaborate on this project, and get it finished faster.

entries.definition: Having worth, merit, or value.
entries.example: These banished men that I have kept withal / Are men endued with worthy qualities

entries.definition: Having a great value.
entries.example: valuable gemstones

entries.definition: Low or reduced in price.
entries.example: Where there are many sellers and few purchases, land will be cheap.

entries.definition: Something that motivates, rouses, or encourages.
entries.example: I have no incentive to do housework right now.

entries.definition: To cause to move faster; to quicken the motion of; to add to the speed of.
entries.example: Press the pedal gently to accelerate the car.

entries.definition: Quick; acting without delay.
entries.example: He was very prompt at getting a new job.

entries.definition: A fixed amount of money paid to a worker, usually calculated on a monthly or annual basis, not hourly, as wages. Implies a degree of professionalism and/or autonomy.
entries.example: This is hire and salary, not revenge.

entries.definition: Money one earns by working or by capitalising on the work of others.
entries.example: The struggle with ways and means had recommenced, more difficult now a hundredfold than it had been before, because of their increasing needs. Their income disappeared as a little rivulet that is swallowed by the thirsty ground.

entries.definition: An amount of money paid to a worker for a specified quantity of work, usually calculated on an hourly basis and expressed in an amount of money per hour.
entries.example: Before her promotion, her wages were 20% less.

entries.definition: The act of paying.
entries.example: Payment will be made at the end of the month.

entries.definition: To compensate (someone) with payment; especially, to repay money spent on someone's behalf.
entries.example: The company will reimburse you for your expenses for the business trip.

entries.definition: A list of employees who receive salary or wages, together with the amounts due to each.
entries.example: Magazines kept aristocrats on the payroll to facilitate access to jet-set playgrounds like Corfu and Mustique.

entries.definition: Something given in exchange for goods or services rendered.
entries.example: “Mr. Quatermain,” said the former, “I am well off, and I am bent upon this business. You may put the remuneration for your services at whatever figure you like in reason, and it shall be paid over to you before we start. Moreover, I will arrange in the event of anything untoward happening to us or to you, that your son shall be suitably provided for. You will see from this offer how necessary I think your presence. Also if by chance we should reach this place, and find diamonds, they shall belong to you and Good equally. I do not want them. But of course that promise is worth nothing at all, though the same thing would apply to any ivory we might get. You may pretty well make your own terms with me, Mr. Quatermain; and of course I shall pay all expenses.”

entries.definition: Money provided to reduce the cost of an activity or product.
entries.example: A government subsidy made the new bus route financially viable.
entries.usage: Typical combinations: government subsidy, receive a subsidy, subsidy scheme.

entries.definition: To gain (success, reward, recognition) through applied effort or work.
entries.example: You can have the s'mores: you earned them, clearing the walkway of snow so well.

entries.definition: A task, project, or enterprise that someone attempts to carry out.
entries.example: Restoring the old theatre is a major undertaking.
entries.usage: Common learner sense selected in place of an unsuitable or less useful source default.

entries.definition: One’s calling in life; one's working occupation or profession, especially when pursued seriously or over a long period of time.
entries.example: When they’ve tortured and scared you for twenty-odd years, / Then they expect you to pick a career

entries.definition: A declaration of faith.
entries.example: She died only a few years after her profession.

entries.definition: An activity or task with which one occupies oneself; usually specifically the productive activity, service, trade, or craft for which one is regularly paid; a job.
entries.example: With no particular appearance of regret Annesley Greatorex detached himself from the occupation of typing letters and came across to his employer's chair.

entries.definition: A task.
entries.example: I've got a job for you: could you wash the dishes?

entries.definition: A divine calling to establish one's lifestyle.
entries.example: The Catholic Church supports and teaches us that there are three vocations: the single life, married life, and the religious life or priesthood.

entries.definition: An effort expended on a particular task; toil, work.
entries.example: […]So I ſet myſelf to enlarge my Cave and Works farther into the Earth; for it was a looſe ſandy Rock, which yielded eaſily to the Labour I beſtowed on it[…]

entries.definition: All the workers employed by a specific organization or state, or on a specific project.
entries.example: The rail sector's ageing workforce (28% of workers are over 50 years old) means that about 15,000 people could retire from the industry by 2025.

entries.definition: A person who feels compelled to work excessively, including while at home.
entries.example: All workaholics should move to Hong Kong, where working hours average over 50 per week.

entries.definition: Collection of people in an organization, such as employees and office staff, members of the military, etc.
entries.example: People like to see such friendly relationship existing between the respective personnels of their Army, Navy and Marine Corps.

entries.definition: One who occupationally provides assistance by working with records, accounts, letters, etc.; an office worker.
entries.example:
As office boy I made such a mark
That they gave me the post of a junior clerk.

entries.definition: Any face-to-face meeting, especially of an official or adversarial nature.
entries.example: (Aaron Burr narrating): It was at about this time that I learned exactly what it was that Hamilton had said of me, and knew that this world was far too narrow a place to contain the two of us. Hamilton's friend made one further attempt to get him off the hook but only further impaled the slanderer by remarking that should Colonel Burr wish to enquire of any other conversation of Hamilton concerning Burr, a prompt and frank avowal or denial would be given. This was too much. I told Van Ness to set a time and place for an interview [referring to a duel with pistols].

entries.definition: To start (something) again that has been stopped or paused from the point at which it was stopped or paused; continue, carry on.
entries.example: We will resume this discussion tomorrow at nine.

entries.definition: To bestow commendation on; to represent favorably; to suggest, endorse or encourage as an appropriate choice.
entries.example: The board recommends Philips, given his ample experience in similar positions.

entries.definition: To retain (someone) as an employee.
entries.example: Our company employs hundreds of people.

entries.definition: A person who has been hired, especially in a cohort.
entries.example: We pair up each of our new hires with one of our original hires.

entries.definition: A (usually self-sustaining) chemical reaction involving the bonding of oxygen with carbon or other fuel, with the production of heat and the presence of flame or smouldering.
entries.example: But to me it was not despicable; I said, "Oh, you fire, I love you, you dainty pink creature, for you are beautiful—and that is enough!" and was going to gather it to my breast.

entries.definition: Alternative spelling of layoff.
entries.example: Pogba zipped a pass to Cavani and his lay-off went to the ever-lurking Fernandes. Once more, his return ball to Cavani was instant, and the Uruguayan smacked home for his 11th goal this season.

entries.definition: To discharge; to end the employment or service of.
entries.example: The company dismissed me after less than a year.

entries.definition: To accomplish or complete, as an obligation.
entries.example: Whenever the Vice President and a majority of either the principal officers of the executive departments or of such other body as Congress may by law provide, transmit to the President pro tempore of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives their written declaration that the President is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office, the Vice President shall immediately assume the powers and duties of the office as Acting President. (1965, Amendment XXV)

entries.definition: To give up; to relinquish ownership of.
entries.example: And if the perfection of well-speaking might bring any glorie sutable unto a great personage, Scipio and Lelius would never have resigned the honour of their Comedies[…]unto an Affrican servant[…].

entries.definition: A bag; especially a large bag of strong, coarse material for storage and handling of various commodities, such as potatoes, coal, coffee; or, a bag with handles used at a supermarket, a grocery sack; or, a small bag for small items, a satchel.
entries.example: The farmer filled a sack with potatoes.

entries.definition: To stop working on a permanent basis, usually because of old age or illness.
entries.example: Having made a large fortune, he retired.

entries.definition: To proceed, spring up or rise, as a consequence, from facts, arguments, premises, combination of circumstances, consultation, thought or endeavor.
entries.example: Pleasure and peace do naturally result from a holy and good life.

entries.definition: State or condition of not meeting a desirable or intended objective, opposite of success.
entries.example: For Liverpool, their season will now be regarded as a relative disappointment after failure to add the FA Cup to the Carling Cup and not mounting a challenge to reach the Champions League places.

entries.definition: The expulsion from the womb of a foetus or embryo before it is fully developed, with loss of the foetus.
entries.example: Swines-bread, so used, doth not onely speed / A tardy labour; but (without great heed) / If over it a Child-great Woman stride, / Instant abortion often doth betide.

entries.definition: The result of no longer possessing an object, a function, or a characteristic due to external causes or misplacement.
entries.example: loss of limb; weight loss; loss of cognitive functions; loss of appetite.

entries.definition: A chance for advancement, progress or profit.
entries.example: seize the opportunity

entries.definition: An opportunity or possibility.
entries.example: We had the chance to meet the president last week: we have a good/strong chance of making / to make a profit.

entries.definition: To pick; to make the choice of; to select.
entries.example: I chose a nice ripe apple from the fruit bowl.

entries.definition: To become something different.
entries.example: The tadpole changed into a frog.

entries.definition: To find an answer or solution to a problem or question; to work out.
entries.example: True piety would effectually solve such scruples.

entries.definition: To change with a specific direction, progress.
entries.example: Let's see how things develop and then make our decision.

entries.definition: Able to continue without using up resources or causing serious harm.
entries.example: The project aims to create a sustainable source of clean energy.
entries.usage: Specify what can be sustained: resource use, financial operations or a long-term policy.

entries.definition: To make (something) better; to increase the value or productivity (of something).
entries.example: Painting the woodwork will improve this house.

entries.definition: To direct or be in charge of.
entries.example: Even though Jack is a novice, he manages his team with great success.

entries.definition: To control an activity according to rules or laws.
entries.example: The agency regulates the disposal of industrial waste.

entries.definition: An approval, by an authority, generally one that makes something valid.
entries.example: The whalers had been operating in the contested waters off the island with sanction from the Japanese government.

entries.definition: To work or act together, especially for a common purpose or benefit.
entries.example: In polling by the Pew Research Center in November 2008, fully half the respondents thought the two parties would cooperate more in the coming year, versus only 36 percent who thought the climate would grow more adversarial.

entries.definition: The body of binding rules and regulations, customs, and standards established in a community by its legislative and judicial authorities.
entries.example: Not unnaturally, "Auntie" took this communication in bad part.[…]Next day she[…]tried to recover her ward by the hair of the head. Then, thwarted, the wretched creature went to the police for help; she was versed in the law, and perhaps had spared no pains to keep on good terms with the local constabulary.

entries.definition: Relating to the law or to lawyers.
entries.example: legal profession

entries.definition: A regulation, law, guideline.
entries.example: All participants must adhere to the rules.

entries.definition: The act of regulating or the condition of being regulated.
entries.example: The regulation of traffic improved safety near the school.

entries.definition: A formal binding agreement concluded by subjects of international law, namely, states and international organizations; a convention, a pact.
entries.example: to sign a peace treaty

entries.definition: An understanding between entities to follow a specific course of conduct.
entries.example: to enter an agreement

entries.definition: A document issued by some authority, creating a public or private institution, and defining its purposes and privileges.
entries.example: The university was established by a royal charter.

entries.definition: An amendment to an official treaty.
entries.example: The 1992 Protocol amended the definitions of other terms, including ‘ship’, ‘oil’ and ‘incident’: Art. 2.

entries.definition: That which is normal or typical.
entries.example: Unemployment is the norm in this part of the country.

entries.definition: A standard by which something is evaluated or measured.
entries.example: Near-synonym: criterion

entries.definition: plural of criterion
entries.example: For quotations using this term, see Citations:criteria.

entries.definition: Falling within an accepted range of size, amount, power, quality, etc.
entries.example: The room contains a standard double bed.

entries.definition: To let one have as a suitable share of something.
entries.example: to allow a servant his liberty; to allow a free passage; to allow one day for rest

entries.definition: The act or practice of admitting.
entries.example: The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge have ended months of intense speculation by announcing they are expecting their first child, but were forced to share their news earlier than hoped because of the Duchess's admission to hospital on Monday.

entries.definition: To keep up, impose or bring into effect something, not necessarily by force.
entries.example: The police are there to enforce the law.

entries.definition: The condition of failing to meet an obligation.
entries.example: He failed to make payments on time, and he is now in default.

entries.definition: To refuse to accept; to forswear.
entries.example: She even rejected my improved offer.

entries.definition: Something that constrains; a restriction.
entries.example: An engineer must recognize the difference between a constraint (to work within) and a problem (to be eliminated via resolution).

entries.definition: Of or about an office or public trust.
entries.example: official duties

entries.definition: obligatory; required or commanded by authority.
entries.example: Attendance at a school is usually mandatory for children.

entries.definition: Powerful; possessing power; effective.
entries.example: harsh and potent injuries

entries.definition: simple past and past participle of bind
entries.example: I bound the splint to my leg.

entries.definition: The act of binding oneself by a social, legal, or moral tie to someone.
entries.example: Signing the contract creates an obligation to pay on time.

entries.definition: An enclosed space; a courtyard; an uncovered area shut in by the walls of a building, or by different buildings; also, a space opening from a street and nearly surrounded by houses; a blind alley.
entries.example: The girls were playing in the court.

entries.definition: Dominant, having power over all others.
entries.example: The US supreme court has ruled unanimously that natural human genes cannot be patented, a decision that scientists and civil rights campaigners said removed a major barrier to patient care and medical innovation.

entries.definition: To make (a bill) into law.
entries.example: The practical effect of the Government's new anti-strike bill on the rail disputes in Great Britain is awaited, after the legislation was enacted.

entries.definition: To pass laws (including the amending or repeal of existing laws).
entries.example: If they can't get people to do the right thing by talking then they will try to legislate and enforce the statutes.

entries.definition: Fairness, impartiality, or justice as determined in light of "natural law" or "natural right".
entries.example: Sufficeth what they in their graue wiſedoomes ſhall proſcribe, I in no ſorte will ſeeke to acquite, nor preſumptuouſly attempte to diſpute againſt the equity of their iudgementes, but humble and proſtrate appeale to their mercies.

entries.definition: Unblemished (figuratively or literally); clean and pure; innocent.
entries.example: one's fair name

entries.definition: Factually right, correct; factual.
entries.example: It is a just assessment of the facts.

entries.definition: An adverse judgment or opinion formed beforehand or without knowledge of the facts.
entries.example: Many of the inhabitants of our Eastern States refuse to eat Squirrels of any kind, from some prejudice or other; but we can assure our readers that the flesh of this species, and many others, is both tender and well-flavoured, and when nicely broiled, does not require a hunter’s appetite to recommend it.

entries.definition: Discernment, the act of discriminating, discerning, distinguishing, noting or perceiving differences between things, with the intent to understand rightly and make correct decisions.
entries.example: Have you felt the weight of the considerations which have been presented, in order to show the importance of discrimination on the subject of revealed truth?

entries.definition: To find fault with, blame, censure.
entries.example: […] and their thoughts the meanwhile accusing or else excusing one another.

entries.definition: To file a legal action against someone, generally a non-criminal (civil) action.
entries.example: sue someone for selling a faulty product

entries.definition: To start criminal proceedings against.
entries.example: to prosecute a man for trespass, or for a riot

entries.definition: To strongly criticise or denounce; to excoriate.
entries.example: The president condemned the terrorists.

entries.definition: To express feelings of pain, dissatisfaction, or resentment.
entries.example: Joe was always complaining about the noise made by his neighbours.

entries.definition: To abstain, either as an individual or a group, from using, buying, or dealing with someone or some organization as an expression of protest.
entries.example: There is probably not a citizen in the United States who wears a hat that has not heard of John Stetson, and does not know that the Stetson hat is one of if not the best made. For some cause the Knights [of Labor] have boycotted the Stetson hats, and have notified all dealers that if they sell them they also will be boycotted.

entries.definition: A period of time devoted to a particular activity.
entries.example: counseling session

entries.definition: To resolve differences, or to bring about a settlement, between conflicting parties.
entries.example: Negotiators managed to mediate a ceasefire.

entries.definition: An appeal, petition, urgent prayer or entreaty.
entries.example: Even if only one person answers my plea for someone to correspond with it will be a blessing.

entries.definition: An application to a superior court or judge for a decision or order by an inferior court or judge to be reviewed and overturned.
entries.example: The lawyer filed an appeal against the court's decision.

entries.definition: To deny the truth or validity of (a statement or statements).
entries.example: His testimony contradicts hers.

entries.definition: To successfully convince (someone) to agree to, accept, or do something, usually through reasoning and verbal influence.
entries.example: That salesman was able to persuade me into buying this bottle of lotion.

entries.definition: A debate or discussion of opposing opinions; (generally) strife.
entries.example: [A]nd it is without all controuerſie, that learning doth make the minds of men gentle, generous, maniable, and pliant to gouernment; whereas Ignorance makes them churliſh, thwart, and mutinous; […]

entries.definition: The act of speaking in a quiet voice, especially without vibration of the vocal cords; the sound thus produced.
entries.example: I spoke in a near whisper.

entries.definition: A repressed or obscure utterance; an instance of muttering.
entries.example: The prisoners were docile, and accepted their lot with barely a mutter.

entries.definition: Any low, indistinct sound, like that of running water.
entries.example: The delightful murmur of water running over pebbles is heard a few yards off

entries.definition: Free from sound or noise; absolutely still; perfectly quiet.
entries.example: How silent is this town!

entries.definition: Not having the power of speech; dumb.
entries.example: Thus, while the mute Creation downward bend / Their sight, and to their Earthy Mother tend, / Man looks aloft; and with erected Eyes / Beholds his own hereditary Skies. / From ſuch rude Principles our Form began; / And Earth was Metamorphos'd into Man.

entries.definition: To inquire into or study in order to ascertain facts or information.
entries.example: to investigate the causes of natural phenomena

entries.definition: Attestation of a fact or event; testimony.
entries.example: She can bear witness, since she was there at the time.

entries.definition: To provide an acceptable explanation for.
entries.example: How can you justify spending so much money on clothes?

entries.definition: Just; fair; agreeable to reason.
entries.example: The episode also opens with an inspired bit of business for Homer, who blithely refuses to acquiesce to an elderly neighbor’s utterly reasonable request that he help make the process of selling her house easier by wearing pants when he gallivants about in front of windows […]

entries.definition: Having sufficient or the required properties for a certain purpose or task; appropriate to a certain occasion.
entries.example: Doctors told Matthew Parker’s family there was only a 1% chance of finding a suitable donor for Matthew because his body had rejected a previous transplant.

entries.definition: Untrue, not factual, factually incorrect.
entries.example: Also the rule of false position, with dyuers examples not onely vulgar, but some appertaynyng to the rule of Algeber.

entries.definition: A public official whose duty it is to administer the law, especially by presiding over trials and rendering judgments; a justice.
entries.example: The parts of a judge in hearing are four: to direct the evidence; to moderate length, repetition, or impertinency of speech; to recapitulate, select, and collate the material points of that which hath been said; and to give the rule or sentence.

entries.definition: A group of individuals chosen from the general population to hear and decide a case in a court of law.
entries.example: And so the jury and he approached, as if this were a time of peace instead of one of the greatest world disturbances ever known in history, the question whether the prosecution had proved to the jury’s satisfaction that George Joseph Smith was guilty of murder. The jury were the shield which stood between him and death, unless, to the jury’s satisfaction, he was proved to be guilty. Yet while they were the shield of the man accused, they were also the Sword of the State; and if the man were proved guilty, they were the servants of the State to punish him. Their respective functions were these: he the judge, had to settle the law, and the jury must take the law from him. The jury were judges of fact.

entries.definition: An occasion on which a person or thing is tested to find out how well they perform or how suitable they are.
entries.example: all thy vexations / Were but my trials of thy love and thou / Hast strangely stood the test here

entries.definition: To imagine or suppose (something) to be true, or to exist, without proof.
entries.example: to suspect the presence of disease

entries.definition: The judicial order for a punishment to be imposed on a person convicted of a crime.
entries.example: The judge declared a sentence of death by hanging for the infamous child rapist.

entries.definition: The act of taking someone into legal custody.
entries.example: The police made an arrest after examining the evidence.

entries.definition: A place or institution for the confinement of persons held against their will in lawful custody or detention, especially (in US usage) a place where people are held for minor offenses or with reference to some future judicial proceeding.
entries.example: serve time in jail

entries.definition: A place or institution where people are held against their will, in the US especially for long-term confinement, as of those convicted of serious crimes or otherwise considered undesirable by the government.
entries.example: The cold stone walls of the prison had stood for over a century.

entries.definition: To restrict (someone or something) to a particular scope or area; to keep in or within certain bounds.
entries.example: Now let not nature's hand / Keep the wild flood confined! let order die!

entries.definition: Supervise or direct an activity or group of people.
entries.example: A supervisor will oversee the installation work.
entries.usage: Common learner sense selected in place of an unsuitable or less useful source default.

entries.definition: To oversee or direct (a task or organization).
entries.example: Without someone to supervise them, the group will lack direction.

entries.definition: To restrain within boundaries; to limit; to confine
entries.example: After suffering diahrroea, the patient was restricted to a diet of rice, cold meat, and yoghurt.

entries.definition: To control or keep in check.
entries.example: As with vicarious mismenstruation, the abnormal cessation only requires strict attention to the general health, with such measures to restrain hemorrhage as have already been indicated.

entries.definition: To give in trust; to put into charge or keeping; to entrust; to consign; used with to or formerly unto.
entries.example: Commit these numbers to memory.

entries.definition: A violation of divine will or religious law.
entries.example: As a Christian, I think this is a sin against God.

entries.definition: A specific act committed in violation of the law, especially criminal law.
entries.example: the commission of a crime

entries.definition: Bad or immoral behaviour. (Especially often, a habit that harms oneself or others)
entries.example: Pride is a vice, not a virtue.

entries.definition: Something (usually money) given in exchange for influence or as an inducement to breaking the law.
entries.example:
c. 1613-1625, Henry Hobart, Yardly v. Ellill
Undue reward for anything against justice is a bribe.

entries.definition: To steal from, especially using force or violence.
entries.example: He robbed three banks before he was caught.

entries.definition: A criminal who plunders at sea; commonly attacking merchant vessels, though often pillaging port towns.
entries.example: You should be cautious due to the Somali pirates.

entries.definition: To take illegally, or without the owner's permission, something owned by someone else without intending to return it.
entries.example: Three irreplaceable paintings were stolen from the gallery.

entries.definition: One who carries out a theft.
entries.example: water-thieves and land-thieves

entries.definition: An act of killing a person unlawfully, especially with predetermination.
entries.example: Throwing that punch was a murder whether you meant for it to happen or not.

entries.definition: The act of intentionally killing oneself.
entries.example: As a nation of freemen, we must live through all time, or die by suicide.

entries.definition: To trick or mislead.
entries.example: It feels painful to begin seeing clearly, that you’ve been deceived by the very people and institutions you trusted to guide you.

entries.definition: To violate rules in order to gain, or attempt to gain, advantage from a situation.
entries.example: My brother flunked biology because he cheated on his mid-term.

entries.definition: The crime of stealing or otherwise illegally obtaining money by use of deception tactics.
entries.example: The bank investigated a case of fraud involving false account details.

entries.definition: Someone who tells a lie; especially, a person who frequently lies.
entries.example: He simply said, "We know, the Big Satan is a big liar."

entries.definition: A machine or other device designed to catch (and sometimes kill) animals, either by holding them in a container, or by catching hold of part of the body.
entries.example: I put down some traps in my apartment to try and deal with the mouse problem.

entries.definition: Something designed to fool, dupe, outsmart, mislead or swindle.
entries.example: It was just a trick to say that the house was underpriced.

entries.definition: To speak or behave so as to give a false or simulated appearance.
entries.example: You don't have to pretend that the soup tastes fine.

entries.definition: A person with poor judgment or little intelligence.
entries.example: You were a fool to cross that busy road without looking.

entries.definition: An indication of infamy or disgrace.
entries.example: But to have as an enforced dining companion a man who was probably a Papist, certainly a rake, and bore the stigma of cowardice, was anathema.

entries.definition: To admit to the truth, particularly in the context of sins or crimes committed.
entries.example: I confess to spray-painting all over that mural!

entries.definition: To adapt to something by more closely matching it, especially something normative.
entries.example:
There is a worm by Phoebus bred,
By leaves of mulberry is fed,
Which unprovided where to dwell,
Conforms itself to weave a cell.

entries.definition: To restore a friendly relationship; to bring back or return to harmony.
entries.example: to reconcile people who have quarrelled

entries.definition: To do as ordered by (a person, institution etc), to act according to the bidding of.
entries.example: obey the rules

entries.definition: To yield to an overpowering force or overwhelming desire.
entries.example: succumb to temptation

entries.definition: A legal sentence.
entries.example: The penalty for his crime was to do hard labor.

entries.definition: Senses referring to subjective quality.
entries.example: The tree frog that they encountered was truly a fine specimen.

entries.definition: A legal agreement in which a borrower pledges real property as collateral for a loan used to purchase or refinance that property.
entries.example: The appriser, therefore, (as the holder of a mortgage was then called,) entered upon possession, and in the language of Hotspur, "came me cranking in," and cut the family out of another monstrous cantle of their remaining property.

entries.definition: The state of having complete legal control of something; possession; proprietorship.
entries.example: Other evidence of former ownerships such as notice-boards, number plates, and makers' plates, are often discovered unexpectedly. […] It has not been used for many years, and although it was impracticable to photograph the engine in the small confines of the shed it was possible to obtain a picture of the plate which it still carries showing the former ownership.

entries.definition: The right by law to be the entity which determines who may publish, copy and distribute a piece of writing, music, picture or other work of authorship.
entries.example: Copyright is a separate legal area from trademarks.

entries.definition: A particular benefit, advantage, or favor; a right or immunity enjoyed by some but not others; a prerogative, preferential treatment.
entries.example: All first-year professors here must teach four courses a term, yet you're only teaching one! What entitled you to such a privilege?

entries.definition: To ascribe; attribute; credit with.
entries.example: Nationalisms often accredit all the unemployment issues to immigration.

entries.definition: Information which may lead one to a certain point or conclusion.
entries.example: Give me a clue because the question is too vague.

entries.definition: A way or means of approaching or entering; an entrance; a passage.
entries.example: The door provides access to the premises.

entries.definition: Having a name that is unknown or withheld.
entries.example: An anonymous donor paid for the new library books.

entries.definition: Real and authentic rather than false or counterfeit.
entries.example: The dealer confirmed that the painting was genuine.
entries.usage: Common learner sense selected in place of an unsuitable or less useful source default.

entries.definition: A particular method for performing a task.
entries.example: One of the hidden glories of Victorian engineering is proper drains. Isolating a city’s effluent and shipping it away in underground sewers has probably saved more lives than any medical procedure except vaccination.

entries.definition: A course of action to be followed regularly; a standard procedure.
entries.example: Checking the equipment is part of our daily routine.

entries.definition: An effect; something that follows a cause as a result.
entries.example: The lobule margins, furthermore, are arched away from the lobe, with the consequence that (when fully inflated) the abaxial leaf surface forms the interior lining of the lobule.

entries.definition: The desire to purchase goods and services.
entries.example: Prices usually go up when demand exceeds supply.

entries.definition: To ask for (something).
entries.example: The corporal requested reinforcements.

entries.definition: To need something.
entries.example: These plants require plenty of sunlight.

entries.definition: A formal written request made by an individual or a group of people to a sovereign or political authority, often containing many signatures, soliciting some grace, right, mercy, or the redress of some wrong or grievance.
entries.example: We're looking to get 10,000 people to sign the petition to have the bird colony given legal protection.

entries.definition: An order to do something.
entries.example: I was given a command to cease shooting.

entries.definition: To teach by giving instructions.
entries.example: Listen carefully when someone instructs you how to assemble the furniture.

entries.definition: Extreme force.
entries.example: The violence of the storm, fortunately, was more awesome than destructive.

entries.definition: A clash or disagreement, often violent, between two or more opposing groups or individuals.
entries.example: The conflict between the government and the rebels began three years ago.

entries.definition: A quick hostile or predatory incursion or invasion in a battle.
entries.example: Marauding chief! his sole delight / The moonlight raid, the morning fight.

entries.definition: Deviation from moral normality; extreme wickedness, nefariousness, or cruelty.
entries.example: Not until the war ended and journalists were able to enter Cambodia did the world really become aware of the enormity of Pol Pot’s oppression.

entries.definition: A series of operations undertaken to achieve a set goal.
entries.example: an election campaign

entries.definition: A contest, a struggle.
entries.example: the battle of life

entries.definition: A contortion of the body in an attempt to escape or to perform a difficult task.
entries.example: The trapped animal's struggle shook the cage.

entries.definition: A violent release of energy (sometimes mechanical, nuclear, or chemical); an act or instance of exploding.
entries.example: A man was injured by an explosion caused by drilling into a missed shot at the Mendota mine above Silver Plume, Colo.

entries.definition: A medieval primitive cannon, used chiefly in sieges for throwing heavy stone balls.
entries.example: They planted in divers places twelve great bombards, wherewith they threw huge stones into the air, which, falling down into the city, might break down the houses.

entries.definition: An explosive device used or intended as a weapon, especially, one dropped from an aircraft.
entries.example: The size of the ground hole crater from the blast indicates it was a bomb.

entries.definition: A violent gust of wind (in windy weather) or apparent wind (around a moving vehicle).
entries.example: And see where surly Winter passes off, / Far to the north, and calls his ruffian blasts; / His blasts obey, and quit the howling hill.

entries.definition: To break from internal pressure.
entries.example: I blew the balloon up too much, and it burst.

entries.definition: A small particle of glowing matter, either molten or on fire, resulting from an electrical surge or excessive heat created by friction.
entries.example: A spark from the fire landed on the carpet.

entries.definition: To shine with a flickering light; to glimmer.
entries.example: We could see the lights of the village twinkling in the distance.

entries.definition: An explosive mixture of saltpetre (potassium nitrate), charcoal and sulfur; formerly used in gunnery but now mostly used in fireworks.
entries.example: They have been a bold, heroic, and purely self dependent nation, never having either courted,—or been subdued by—other Tribes or Europeans. But what early mind—a power—could face gunpowder and the ﬁrelocks? Hence their annihilation!

entries.definition: A closed container for liquids or gases.
entries.example: The propane is stored in these tanks.

entries.definition: A complete assembly, consisting of an artillery tube and a breech mechanism, firing mechanism or base cap, which is a component of a gun, howitzer or mortar, which may include muzzle appendages.
entries.example: Holonyms: gun, field gun; howitzer; mortar

entries.definition: Any object used as a weapon by being thrown or fired through the air, such as stone, arrow or bullet.
entries.example: The Rhodians, who used leaden bullets, were able to project their missiles twice as far as the Persian slingers, who used large stones.

entries.definition: An instrument of attack or defense in combat or hunting, e.g. most guns, missiles, or swords.
entries.example: The club that is now mostly used for golf was once a common weapon.

entries.definition: A handgun
entries.example: The police officer placed the pistol in a locked evidence box.

entries.definition: A firearm fired from the shoulder; improved range and accuracy is provided by a long, rifled barrel.
entries.example: Still, a dozen men with rifles, and cartridges to match, stayed behind when they filed through a white aldea lying silent amid the cane, and the Sin Verguenza swung into slightly quicker stride.

entries.definition: A projectile, usually of metal, shot from a gun at high speed.
entries.example: The police found a bullet near the doorway.

entries.definition: A butt or mark to shoot at, as for practice, or to test the accuracy of a firearm, or the force of a projectile.
entries.example: Take careful aim at the target.

entries.definition: To make (something) deviate from its original path or position.
entries.example: The shield deflected the ball away from the window.

entries.definition: A set of tasks that fulfills a purpose or duty; an assignment set by an employer, or by oneself.
entries.example: The team's mission is to deliver medical supplies to the remote village.

entries.definition: The visible part of fire; a stream of burning vapour or gas, emitting light and heat.
entries.example: Long after his cigar burnt bitter, he sat with eyes fixed on the blaze. When the flames at last began to flicker and subside, his lids fluttered, then drooped; but he had lost all reckoning of time when he opened them again to find Miss Erroll in furs and ball-gown kneeling on the hearth[…].

entries.definition: A sudden bright light.
entries.example: A sudden flare of light appeared on the horizon.

entries.definition: A bright, sparkling light; shininess or brilliance.
entries.example: As yet there had been no symptom of the news having any better foundation than in the fears of those who brought it, but The Boot had not been deserted five minutes, when there appeared, coming across the fields, a body of men who, it was easy to see, by the glitter of their arms and ornaments in the sun, and by their orderly and regular mode of advancing.

entries.definition: To emit heat and light without a flame.
entries.example: Iron glows red hot when heated to near its melting point.

entries.definition: The (typically sharp-edged) part of a knife, sword, razor, or other tool with which it cuts.
entries.example: Sword. — The blade is straight, tapers gradually, is 32 9/16 inches long from shoulder to point, and is fullered on both sides, commencing 2 inches from the shoulder, to about 17 inches from the point, to a thickness of ·035 inch.

entries.definition: A long bladed weapon with a grip and typically a pommel and crossguard (together forming a hilt), which is designed to cut, stab, slash and/or hack.
entries.example: He took out his sword and stabbed the man in the stomach.

entries.definition: A tool with a heavy blade used for chopping.
entries.example: He used an ax to split the firewood.

entries.definition: A tool with a heavy head and a handle used for pounding.
entries.example: Bobby used a hammer and nails to fix the two planks together.

entries.definition: A projectile consisting of a shaft, a point and a tail with stabilizing fins that is shot from a bow.
entries.example: The Citizens in their rage, imagining that euery poſt in the Churche had bin one of yᵉ Souldyers, ſhot habbe or nabbe at randon^([sic – meaning random]) uppe to the Roode lofte, and to the Chancell, leauing ſome of theyr arrowes ſticking in the Images.

entries.definition: A long stick with a sharp tip used as a weapon for throwing or thrusting, or anything used to make a thrusting motion.
entries.example:
It's not like you killed someone
It's not like you drove a spiteful spear into his side
Talk to Jesus Christ as if he knows the reasons why
He did it all for you

entries.definition: A hard, protective head covering, typically part of armour.
entries.example: Now that she had rested and had fed from the luncheon tray Mrs. Broome had just removed, she had reverted to her normal gaiety. She looked cool in a grey tailored cotton dress with a terracotta scarf and shoes and her hair a black silk helmet.

entries.definition: Anything that protects or defends; defense; shelter; protection.
entries.example: Knock go and come; God's vassals drop and die; And sword and shield, In bloody field, Doth win immortal fame.

entries.definition: To supply with something necessary in order to carry out a specific action or task; to provide with (e.g. weapons, provisions, munitions, rigging).
entries.example:
1698-1699, Edmund Ludlow, Memoirs
Gave orders for equipping a considerable fleet.

entries.definition: To make ready for a specific future purpose; to set up; to assemble or equip; to forearm.
entries.example: We prepared the spacecraft for takeoff.

entries.definition: To make a living; earn money for necessities.
entries.example: It is difficult to provide for my family working on minimum wage.

entries.definition: To prepare and arrange (originally military unit or units, i.e., to array troops) for use.
entries.example: "Deploy two units of infantry along the enemy's flank," the general ordered.

entries.definition: To strike.
entries.example: One boy hit the other.

entries.definition: A stroke; a blow.
entries.example: He, […]with a careless beat, / Struck out the mute creation at a heat.

entries.definition: To delete or cross out; to scratch or eliminate.
entries.example: Please strike the last sentence.

entries.definition: A hit or strike with one's fist.
entries.example: Another Karadeniz cross led to Cudicini's first save of the night, with the Spurs keeper making up for a weak punch by brilliantly pushing away Christian Noboa's snap-shot.

entries.definition: A cut of meat, often containing a section of a rib.
entries.example: I only like lamb chops with mint jelly.

entries.definition: An act of stabbing or thrusting with an object to hurt or kill someone.
entries.example: A knife was flashing in his hand, and just as he was about to take a stab at me, the smith grabbed his arm from behind.

entries.definition: A circumstance in which a choice must be made between two or more alternatives that seem equally undesirable.
entries.example: A strong dilemma in a desperate case! / To act with infamy, or quit the place.

entries.definition: A dire or unfortunate situation.
entries.example: Though we say we are quite clear about it and understand when someone uses the expression, unlike that other expression, maybe we're in the same plight with regard to them both.

entries.definition: A hidden or easily overlooked problem or danger.
entries.example: Hidden fees are a common pitfall when comparing cheap travel packages.
entries.usage: Selected the common figurative sense rather than a concealed trap in the ground.

entries.definition: An agreement or arrangement between multiple parties to do something harmful, immoral or subversive; an instance of collusion.
entries.example: Conspiracies, like all other exercises of human ingenuity, are of very different kinds. The gloomy plots arranged in old Italian halls...

entries.definition: Lacking something; devoid.
entries.example: Now, though this region may scarcely be said to be wedded to science, being to all intents a virgin territory as respects the enquirer into natural history, still it is greatly destitute of the treasures of the vegetable kingdom.

entries.definition: Extreme shortage of food in a region.
entries.example: It was reserved for Christians to torture bread, the staff of life, bread for which children in whole districts wail, bread, the gift of pasture to the poor, bread, for want of which thousands of our fellow beings annually perish by famine; it was reserved for Christians to torture the material of bread by fire, to create a chemical and maddening poison, burning up the brain and brutalizing the soul, and producing evils to humanity, in comparison of which, war, pestilence, and famine, cease to be evils.

entries.definition: To die because of lack of food or of not eating.
entries.example: During the Cultural Revolution I was exiled to Xincai County in Henan Province. There, 36 percent of the people starved to death in the early 1960s.

entries.definition: Used with “of”, to take something away from (someone) and keep it away; to deny someone something.
entries.example: "By means of the Golden Cap I shall command the Winged Monkeys to carry you to the gates of the Emerald City," said Glinda, "for it would be a shame to deprive the people of so wonderful a ruler."

entries.definition: To deliberately take hold of; to grab or capture.
entries.example: She seized the rope before it fell into the water.

entries.definition: To follow urgently, originally with intent to capture or harm; to chase.
entries.example: pursue one's dreams

entries.definition: An expression of intent to injure or punish another.
entries.example: There is no terror, Cassius, in your threats.

entries.definition: To hurt the feelings of; to displease; to make angry; to insult.
entries.example: Your accusations offend me deeply.

entries.definition: Characterized by aggression; highly combative; prone to behave in a way that involves attacking (especially if unjustly) or arguing.
entries.example: an aggressive policy, war, person, nation

entries.definition: To move into.
entries.example: Under some circumstances police are allowed to invade a person's privacy.

entries.definition: An intentional interference with another's property or person.
entries.example: External infrastructure issues such as severe weather and trespass caused 17.1% of [train] cancellations, [...].

entries.definition: To thrust oneself in; to come or enter without invitation, permission, or welcome; to encroach; to trespass.
entries.example: to intrude on families at unseasonable hours; to intrude on the lands of another

entries.definition: To break or disregard (a rule or convention).
entries.example: Drinking-and-driving violates the law.

entries.definition: An attempt to cause damage, injury to, or death of an opponent or enemy.
entries.example: From 1906 to 1960, there were forty-six recorded shark attacks, half of which were fatal.

entries.definition: A violent onset or attack with physical means, for example blows, weapons, etc.
entries.example: The army made an assault on the enemy.

entries.definition: A confrontation; a dare.
entries.example: Congratulations on managing to use the phrase “preponderant criterion” in a chart (“On your marks”, November 9th). Was this the work of a kakorrhaphiophobic journalist set a challenge by his colleagues, or simply an example of glossolalia?

entries.definition: Military action.
entries.example: They sued for peace after the long siege.

entries.definition: To encircle something or simultaneously extend in all directions.
