entries.definition: A very young human being, from birth to somewhere between six months and two years of age after birth, needing almost constant care and attention.
entries.example: The infant slept while her mother spoke to the nurse.

entries.definition: A person, especially a minor, both or (rarely) one of whose parents have died.
entries.example: Rudolf was the bold, bad Baron of traditional melodrama. Irene was young, as pretty as a picture, fresh from a music academy in England. He was the scion of an ancient noble family; she an orphan without money or friends.

entries.definition: Young; not fully developed.
entries.example: There are certain Climates, where the Mind ripens and attains ſooner to Perfection than in others: nay there are ſome Conſtitutions of Body, where the humours are ſo exactly mixt, that they form an admirable Temper; the Effects thereof are diſcoverable in the firſt Juvenile Years, and leave very fine Remains, even in a decrepit Age.

entries.definition: A young person.
entries.example: As soon as Julia returned with a constable, Timothy, who was on the point of exhaustion, prepared to give over to him gratefully. The newcomer turned out to be a powerful youngster, fully trained and eager to help, and he stripped off his tunic at once.

entries.definition: The quality or state of being young.
entries.example: Serene, smiling, enigmatic, she faced him with no fear whatever showing in her dark eyes. The clear light of the bright autumn morning had no terrors for youth and health like hers.

entries.definition: To go; walk; proceed.
entries.example: (Colin alone) Ah, Colin, thou’rt a prodigal; a thriftless loon thou’st been, that cou’d na’ keep a little pelf to thysall when thou had’st got it; now thou may’st gang in this poor geer to thy live's end, and worse too for aught I can tell; ’faith, mon, ’twas a smeart little bysack of money thou hadst scrap’d together, an the best part of it had na’ being last amongst thy kinsfolk, in the Isles of Skey and Mull; muckle gude may it do the weams of them that ha’ it! There was Jamie MacGregor and Sawney MacNab, and the twa braw lads of Kinruddin, with old Charley MacDougall, my mother's first husband's second cousin: by my sol I cou’d na’ see such near relations, and gentlemen of sich auncient families gang upon bare feet, while I rode a horseback: I had been na’ true Scot, an I cou’d na’ ge’en a countryman a gude last upon occasion (as he is going out, Miss Aubrey enters.)

entries.definition: A person between thirteen and nineteen years old (inclusive).
entries.example: Most teenagers will undergo lots of changes before reaching adulthood.

entries.definition: The transitional period of physical and psychological development between childhood and maturity, beginning at the onset of puberty and with an endpoint defined either legally (at the age of majority, such as 18 in many jurisdictions) or psychocognitively (at various ages, depending on individual experience).
entries.example: Near-synonyms: teenagehood, teenhood, teenagerhood, teenagedom, teenagerdom, teendom

entries.definition: Race; family; breed; kind.
entries.example: the starfish and its kin the sea urchin

entries.definition: People, persons.
entries.example: There were a lot of folk in the streets.

entries.definition: Connected to or depending on something else; comparative.
entries.example: We've been discussing the relative merits of various methods of transportation.

entries.definition: Closely acquainted; familiar.
entries.example: an intimate friend

entries.definition: High in price; expensive.
entries.example: The dearer the jewel, the greater the love expressed.

entries.definition: Often used as an affectionate term of address: a person who is very dear to one.
entries.example: Pass the wine, would you, darling?

entries.definition: One who loves and cares for another person in a romantic way; a sweetheart, love, soulmate, boyfriend, girlfriend, or spouse.
entries.example: […]loue is blinde, and louers cannot ſee / The pretty follies that themſelues commit,[…]

entries.definition: Much loved, dearly loved.
entries.example: But I found at laſt, by hearing and conſidering of things that are Divine, which indeed I heard of you, as alſo of beloved Faithful, that was put to death for his Faith and good-living in Vanity-fair, That the end of these things is death. [Rom[ans] 6. 21, 22, 23.] And that for theſe things ſake, the wrath of God cometh upon the children of diſobedience. [Eph[esians] 5. 6.]

entries.definition: A polite form of address for a woman or lady.
entries.example: Mrs Grey wondered if the outfit she was trying on made her look fat. The sales assistant just said, “It suits you, madam”.

entries.definition: A female host.
entries.example: The host and hostess greeted their guests at the door.

entries.definition: A female landlord.
entries.example: In a large bedroom upstairs, the window of which was thickly curtained with a great woollen shawl lately discarded by the landlady, Mrs. Rolliver, were gathered on this evening nearly a dozen persons, all seeking vinous bliss; all old inhabitants of the nearer end of Marlott, and frequenters of this retreat.

entries.definition: A woman, specifically one with great control, authority or ownership.
entries.example: She was the mistress of the estate-mansion, and owned the horses.

entries.definition: A woman whose main employment is homemaking, maintaining the upkeep of her home and tending to household affairs; often, such a woman whose sole [unpaid] employment is homemaking.
entries.example:
2000, Uli Kusch, "Mr. Torture", Helloween, The Dark Ride
Mr Torture sells pain / To the housewives in Spain / He knows just what they crave / Mr Torture

entries.definition: A woman whose spouse has died and who has not remarried.
entries.example: The widow lived alone after her husband's death.
entries.usage: The local dictionary lacks this common learner meaning; the original sense remains available in history.

entries.definition: An adult or adolescent female servant or cleaner (short for maidservant). (In feudal times this could be anyone from a high-ranking assistant to a low-ranking cleaner.)
entries.example: She was a fat, round little woman, richly apparelled in velvet and lace, […]; and the way she laughed, cackling like a hen, the way she talked to the waiters and the maid,[…]—all these unexpected phenomena impelled one to hysterical mirth, and made one class her with such immortally ludicrous types as Ally Sloper, the Widow Twankey, or Miss Moucher.

entries.definition: A girl or unmarried young woman.
entries.example: The historical novel follows a young maiden who leaves her village.

entries.definition: All the persons who live in a given house or other home; a family including attendants, servants etc.; a domestic or family establishment.
entries.example: And calls, without affecting airs, / His household twice a day to prayers.

entries.definition: A task, especially a regularly needed task for the upkeep of a home or similar, such as housecleaning or preparing meals.
entries.example: Before we moved in together, my partner and I divided up the chores: he cooks and vacuums, and I do the dishes and laundry.

entries.definition: One which receives or entertains a guest, socially, commercially, or officially.
entries.example: A good host is always considerate of the guest’s needs.

entries.definition: A person that leases real property; a lessor.
entries.example:
Brethren, brethren, it were better to haue this communitie,
Then to haue this difference in degrees:
The landlord his rent, the lawyer his fees.
So quickly the poore mans ſubſtance is ſpent […]

entries.definition: One who holds a lease (a tenancy).
entries.example: Long even before the last tenant had occupied it, the room had been regarded with fear and aversion, and the end of that last tenant had in no way lightened the gloom that hung about the place.

entries.definition: A recipient of hospitality, especially someone staying by invitation at the house of another.
entries.example: The guests were let in by the butler.

entries.definition: A person or company who purchases or receives a product or service from a business or merchant or intends to do so.
entries.example: Every person who passes by is a potential customer.

entries.definition: A customer, a buyer or receiver of goods or services.
entries.example: The lawyer met her client to discuss the contract.

entries.definition: To meet (someone) or find (something), especially unexpectedly.
entries.example: It fits Ioues ſonne / VVraſtle vvith Lyons, and to tugge vvith Beares, / Grapple vvith Dragons, and incounter VVhales.

entries.definition: The act of one who chases another; a pursuit.
entries.example: The chase ended when the police blocked the road.

entries.definition: To fail to hit, catch, grasp, etc.
entries.example: I fired the gun, but the bullet missed the target.

entries.definition: The act of appointing a person to hold an office or to have a position of trust.
entries.example: His appointment as treasurer was deemed suitable.

entries.definition: To go with or attend as a companion or associate; to keep company with; to go along with.
entries.example: Geoffrey accompanied the group on their pilgrimage.

entries.definition: Relying upon; depending upon.
entries.example: At that point I was dependent on financial aid for my tuition.

entries.definition: A person authorized to act as representative for another; a deputy.
entries.example: Each region sent a delegate to the national conference.

entries.definition: A person who lacks courage.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: big baby, baby

entries.definition: To suggest a plan, course of action, etc.
entries.example: I propose going to see a film.

entries.definition: An appointment, especially to speak or perform.
entries.example: The lecturer has three speaking engagements this week.

entries.definition: To enter into the conjugal or connubial state; to take a husband or a wife.
entries.example: Neither of her daughters showed any desire to marry.

entries.definition: A marriage ceremony; a ritual officially celebrating the beginning of a marriage.
entries.example: Her announcement was quite a surprise, coming a month after she published the words "I hate weddings with a passion and a fury I can only partially explain rationally."

entries.definition: The period of time immediately following a marriage.
entries.example: The new minister and his wife were a young, pleasant-faced couple, still on their honeymoon, and full of all good and beautiful enthusiasms for their chosen lifework.

entries.definition: To touch with the lips or press the lips against, usually to show love or affection or passion, or as part of a greeting.
entries.example: He […] kissed her lips with such a clamorous smack, / That at the parting all the church echoed.

entries.definition: The legal dissolution of a marriage.
entries.example: Richard obtained a divorce from his wife some years ago, but hasn't returned to the dating scene.

entries.definition: Not accompanied by anything else; one in number.
entries.example: Can you give me a single reason not to leave right now?

entries.definition: Only.
entries.example: He saw now clearly that the sole crew of the vessel was these two dead men, and though he could not see their faces, he saw by their outstretched hands, which were all of ragged flesh, that they had been subjected to some strange exceptional process of decay.

entries.definition: Relating to particular persons or things, each to each; particular; own.
entries.example: They returned to their respective places of abode.

entries.definition: All; every; qualifying a singular noun, indicating all examples of the thing so named seen as individual or separate items (compare every).
entries.example: Make sure you wash each bowl well.

entries.definition: A person considered alone, rather than as belonging to a group of people.
entries.example: He is an unusual individual.

entries.definition: A person who regularly travels between home and work or study.
entries.example: The commuter catches the same train every weekday.

entries.definition: British standard spelling of neighborhood.
entries.example: These developments, most of which have taken place during the past 30 years, are remarkable in view of the low traffic density, except in the neighbourhood of Oslo, and the very extensive undeveloped areas of mountain and virgin forest.

entries.definition: One who belongs to a group.
entries.example: “Were it not for the fancy French and Latin in it, I'd have swore it was the sort of thing I do not print as a rule, but being as how the order was from one of the members upstairs...”

entries.definition: One who is in charge of something.
entries.example: The boss of the company was going to Spain for work.

entries.definition: A person whose job is to manage something, such as a business, a restaurant, or a sports team.
entries.example: Although they did not want to risk wasting money, faster-climbing managers did value generosity and fair-mindedness.

entries.definition: A person with the official task of overseeing the work of a person or group, or of other operations and activities.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: superintendent, manager, boss, executive, overseer

entries.definition: Placed in a lower class, rank, or position.
entries.example: The several kinds […] and subordinate species of each are easily known.

entries.definition: Either of a pair of people or things that belong together.
entries.example: Each dancer waited for their partner before the music began.

entries.definition: A fellow member of a profession, staff, academic faculty or other organization; an associate, a workmate.
entries.example: Mostly, the microbiome is beneficial.[…]Research over the past few years, however, has implicated it in diseases from atherosclerosis to asthma to autism. Dr Yoshimoto and his colleagues would like to add liver cancer to that list.

entries.definition: A mate, companion, or associate.
entries.example:
[… these tears] Which weep the comrade of my choice,
⁠An awful thought, a life removed,
⁠The human-hearted man I loved,
A spirit, not a breathing voice.

entries.definition: A state of being acquainted with a person; originally indicating friendship, intimacy, but now suggesting a slight knowledge less deep than that of friendship; acquaintanceship.
entries.example: I know of the man; but have no acquaintance with him.

entries.definition: The condition of being friends.
entries.example: But (as the Poet ſaith) Malè ſarta gratia, nequicquam coit, & reſcinditur: Friendſhip, that is but euill peeced, will not ioine cloſe, but falleth aſunder againe:

entries.definition: A warm feeling of love or fondness.
entries.example: She showed affection for her grandson by hugging him warmly.
entries.usage: Selected the ordinary emotional sense rather than the archaic act of affecting something.

entries.definition: comparative form of strange: more strange
entries.example: Truth is stranger than fiction.

entries.definition: A trainee, especially in a skilled trade.
entries.example: To this end a well-equipped and keenly-run apprentice training school has been in operation at Eastleigh since 1958 and here apprentices are given a good grounding in a number of trades, followed by a thorough training in the trade to which they become allocated.

entries.definition: One appointed as the substitute of others, and empowered to act for them, in their name or their behalf; a substitute in office.
entries.example: the deputy of a prince

entries.definition: Somebody who possesses great bravery and carries out extraordinary or noble deeds.
entries.example: My mom died a hero on duty.

entries.definition: A female hero.
entries.example: The heroine rescued the villagers from the flood.

entries.definition: A female who performs on the stage or in films.
entries.example: A while ago somewhere I don't know when / I was watchin' a movie with a friend / I fell in love with the actress / She was playin' a part that I could understand

entries.definition: A senior secretary or official with administrative or legal duties, sometimes in charge of some area of government such as finance or justice.
entries.example: Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster

entries.definition: One who exercises control and direction of a military or naval organization.
entries.example: I think if post commanders of the unchaplained posts could employ acceptable clergymen […] then the needs might be met.

entries.definition: One who directs; the person in charge of managing a department or directorate (e.g., director of engineering), project, or production (as in a show or film, e.g., film director).
entries.example: Francis Gurry is director of WIPO.

entries.definition: One who supports something; an advocate.
entries.example: Proponents of the race — notably Mayor Michael R. Bloomberg and Mary Wittenberg, director of the marathon — said the event would provide a needed morale boost, as well as an economic one.

entries.definition: A body of one or more persons convened for the accomplishment of some specific purpose, typically with formal protocols.
entries.example: My uncle is on the committee.

entries.definition: A committee that leads or governs (e.g. city council, student council).
entries.example: He turned back to the scene before him and the enormous new block of council dwellings. The design was some way after Corbusier but the block was built up on plinths and resembled an Atlantic liner swimming diagonally across the site.

entries.definition: Specialised, involving detailed knowledge of a restricted topic.
entries.example: This was a highly specialist job, and it has been very carefully carried out so that it is very hard to see that these windows are now modern replacements.

entries.definition: A person or party that is consulted.
entries.example: We hired a consultant to advise us on energy use.

entries.definition: Of or relating to the medical or surgical treatment of non-human animals, especially domestic and farm animals.
entries.example: Max used all his veterinary knowledge to save the goose stuck in the fence.

entries.definition: A person trained to provide guidance and support, especially with personal difficulties.
entries.example: The counsellor helped the student discuss her worries about exams.

entries.definition: One who solicits
entries.example:
Stephen Cavendish: I'm not going to say any more until I've spoken to my solicitor.
 DCI Tom Barnaby: That might be a good idea, sir.

entries.definition: A lawyer; one who advises or represents others in legal matters as a profession.
entries.example: If those attempts are unsuccessful, the attorney requesting the interrogatories may file a motion for sanctions with the court. The sanctions range from attorney fees to prohibiting the nonanswering party from presenting or defending claims.

entries.definition: An official who presides over a sports match.
entries.example: And you, O King, and you, O Goldry Bluszco, are likewise bound by oath to wrastle fairly and to abide by the ruling of me, the Red Foliot, whom ye are content to choose as your umpire.

entries.definition: To discard, put away.
entries.example: Today, haute couture is finished, snorts [Pierre] Bergé at his most gallic, no more than a licence to flog scent and handbags, and a pastime for bored supermodels and cashiered pop stars.

entries.definition: Someone (especially male) who is skilled in the work of fighting fire.
entries.example: By February 1944 there were over two thousand women employed at the Alabama Dry Dock and Shipbuilding Company [...]. There were also female firemen on almost every shipyard crane [...].

entries.definition: A person trained to care for people who are ill or injured.
entries.example: The nurse checked the patient's temperature.

entries.definition: One who gardens; one who grows plants or cultivates a garden.
entries.example: "Ponder the fact that God has made you a gardener, to root out vice and to plant virtue." — St. Catherine of Siena

entries.definition: A person whose profession is cutting the hair and beards of usually male customers.
entries.example: There's also a barber's shop and that staple of railway stations up and down the UK - a WH Smith.

entries.definition: The act of cutting of the hair, often done professionally by a barber, hair stylist, or beautician.
entries.example: I booked a haircut for Friday afternoon.

entries.definition: A person who catches fish, either as a job or as a leisure activity.
entries.example: The fisherman repaired his net before going out to sea.

entries.definition: A person who prepares and sells meat (and sometimes also slaughters the animals).
entries.example: He looked in vain into the stalls for the butcher who had sold fresh meat twice a week, on market days...

entries.definition: A man who is about to marry.
entries.example: The groom waited at the front of the room for the ceremony to begin.

entries.definition: A person given as a pledge or security for the performance of the conditions of a treaty or similar agreement, such as to ensure the status of a vassal.
entries.example:
And there with alle was made hostage on bothe partyes and made hit as sure as hit myghte be that whether party had the vyctory soo to ende.
"And therewithal was made hostage on both parties, and made it as sure as it might be, that whether party had the victory, so to end."

entries.definition: Labour, work, especially of a grueling nature.
entries.example: […] he set to work again and made the snow fly in all directions around him. After some further toil his efforts were rewarded, and a very shabby door-mat lay exposed to view.

entries.definition: A person who begs.
entries.example: “[…] They talk of you as if you were Croesus—and I expect the beggars sponge on you unconscionably.” And Vickers launched forth into a tirade very different from his platform utterances. He spoke with extreme contempt of the dense stupidity exhibited on all occasions by the working classes.

entries.definition: A person who is held in servitude as the property of another person, and whose labor (and often also whose body and life) is subject to the owner's volition and control.
entries.example: Fear of their cargo bred a savage cruelty into the crew. One captain, to strike terror into the rest, killed a slave and dividing heart, liver and entrails into 300 pieces made each of the slaves eat one, threatening those who refused with the same torture. Such incidents were not rare.

entries.definition: Initialism of the Australian Capital Territory: a federal territory of Australia.
entries.example: Osteoporosis Australia is calling for the 'no hat, no play' policy in school playgrounds to be reassessed in the ACT and Tasmania, because children are not getting enough sunlight.

entries.definition: To conduct (oneself) well, or in a given way; to conform.
entries.example: You need to behave yourself, young lady.

entries.definition: An action or act; something that is done.
entries.example: One small deed can have one strong effect or more.

entries.definition: To make familiar by use; to cause to accept; to habituate, familiarize, or inure.
entries.example: Early exposure to pet allergens and pet-related bacteria accustoms the body to allergens.

entries.definition: To act in response.
entries.example: How did she react to the news?

entries.definition: To say something in return; to answer; to reply.
entries.example: to respond to a question or an argument

entries.definition: To bend back (light, etc.) from a surface.
entries.example: A mirror reflects the light that shines on it.

entries.definition: Begin to use a policy, method or idea.
entries.example: Several universities have adopted a more flexible admissions policy.
entries.usage: Use adopt an approach or policy; the object is the idea or practice selected.

entries.definition: To feed and cause to grow; to supply with food or other matter which increases weight and promotes health.
entries.example: He planteth an ash, and the rain doth nourish it.

entries.definition: To cut down grass or crops.
entries.example: He mowed the lawn every few weeks in the summer.

entries.definition: To help keep from falling.
entries.example: Don’t move that beam! It supports the whole platform.

entries.definition: To expel air from the lungs through the nose or mouth by action of the diaphragm, to breathe out.
entries.example: Inhale slowly, then exhale through your mouth.

entries.definition: The place where water, air or other fluid is taken into a pipe or conduit; opposed to outlet.
entries.example: Leaves blocked the pump's water intake.

entries.definition: To cause (a person or animal) to recover from a faint; to cause (a person or animal) to return to a state of consciousness.
entries.example: Near-synonym: rescue

entries.definition: Of a person, to continue to live; to remain alive.
entries.example: Whether by a miracle or by good luck, all twenty passengers survived.

entries.definition: An intense, blinding light.
entries.example: the frame of burnished steel that cast a glare

entries.definition: To see or view (someone, or something tangible) briefly and incompletely.
entries.example: Morning!—the Vestal Mother of the Sun / Seem'st thou to be, since from thy bosom born, / (Thou that first glimpsest—like a white-stoled nun!—) / He springeth forth—Oh! thou triumphal Morn!— / His race of glory and of joy to run; […]

entries.definition: To turn (one's eyes or look) at something, often briefly.
entries.example: Deare heart forbeare to glance thine eye aſide, / What needſt thou wound with cunning when thy might / Is more then my ore-preſt defence can bide?

entries.definition: A short, soft, high-pitched sound, as made by a baby bird.
entries.example: I don't want to hear a peep out of you!

entries.definition: To stare intently or earnestly.
entries.example: They gazed at the stars for hours.

entries.definition: To look with difficulty, or as if searching for something.
entries.example: […] I should be still / Plucking the grass, to know where sits the wind, / Peering in maps for ports, and piers, and roads;

entries.definition: To look fixedly (at something).
entries.example: She found him staring with raised eyebrows at her.

entries.definition: To look at on all sides or in all its aspects; to view or consider with continued attention; to regard with deliberate care; to meditate on; to study, ponder, or consider.
entries.example: To love, at least contemplate and admire, / What I see excellent.

entries.definition: A solemn promise to perform some act, or behave in a specified manner, especially a promise to live and act in accordance with the rules of a religious order.
entries.example: The old hermit, up in the mountains, took a vow of silence.

entries.definition: A solemn pledge or promise that invokes a deity, a ruler, or another entity (not necessarily present) to attest the truth of a statement or sincerity of one's desire to fulfill a contract or promise.
entries.example: take an oath

entries.definition: To make a solemn promise (to do something).
entries.example: pledge allegiance to the flag

entries.definition: A device designed to be placed in the mouth and blown, or driven by steam or some other mechanism, to make a whistling sound.
entries.example: A lovely crisp exhaust: a feeling of almost unlimited power combined with complete freedom of running: and, to crown it all, a most melodious and wholly American chime whistle—these were my immediate impressions as we stormed rapidly out of Göttingen, intent on winning back some of the lost time.

entries.definition: To give a written or spoken response, especially to a question, request, accusation or criticism; to answer.
entries.example: (intransitive) Please reply to my letter.

entries.definition: To give (someone) notice (of some event).
entries.example: The dispatcher immediately notified the volunteer fire department of the emergency call.

entries.definition: To declare with assurance or plainly and strongly; to state positively.
entries.example: Numerous experimental tests and other observations have been offered in favor of animal mind reading, and although many scientists are skeptical, others assert that humans are not the only species capable of representing what others do and don’t perceive and know.

entries.definition: To make plain, manifest, or intelligible; to clear of obscurity; to illustrate the meaning of.
entries.example: The issue was explained to the governor in detail.

entries.definition: A dispute or heated argument (especially one that is verbal).
entries.example: We got into a silly quarrel about what food to order.

entries.definition: An argument or disagreement; a failure to agree.
entries.example: But is not this dispute over the question whether we have free will or not very like a dispute that we might engage in over the color of a tree — whether it be green or blue?

entries.definition: A fact or statement used to support a proposition; a reason.
entries.example: There is no greater, at leaſt no more palpable and convincing Argument of the Exiſtence of a Deity than the admirable Art and Wiſdom that diſcovers itſelf in the make and conſtitution, the order and diſpoſition, the ends and uſes of all the parts and members of this ſtately fabrick of Heaven and Earth.

entries.definition: A speaking or noticing of anything, usually in a brief or cursory manner.
entries.example: I will make mention of thy righteousness.

entries.definition: A rushed action.
entries.example: Why are you in such a big hurry?

entries.definition: To move or act in a quick fashion.
entries.example: We hastened to the station when we heard the announcement.

entries.definition: A strong desire to do something.
entries.example: After seeing the advert for a soft drink, I had a sudden urge to buy a bottle.

entries.definition: A person who habitually scolds, in particular a troublesome and angry woman.
entries.example:
A ſclaunderous tunge, a tunge of a ſkolde,
Worketh more miſchiefe than can be tolde;
That, if I wiſt not to be controlde,
Yet ſomwhat to ſay I dare well be bolde,

entries.definition: A supernatural detriment or hindrance; a bane.
entries.example: If ye will not heare, and if yee will not lay it to heart, to giue glory vnto my name, saith the Lord of hostes; I will euen send a curse vpon you, and will curse your blessings: yea, I haue cursed them already, because yee doe not lay it to heart.

entries.definition: To take an oath, to promise intensely, solemnly, and/or with legally binding effect.
entries.example: The knight swore not to return to the palace until he had found the treasure.

entries.definition: To cause someone to become annoyed or angry.
entries.example: Don't provoke the dog; it may try to bite you.

entries.definition: To give a sermon.
entries.example: Our pastor can preach very well.

entries.definition: A brag; ostentatious positive appraisal of oneself.
entries.example: His boast that he could finish the race in ten minutes proved unrealistic.

entries.definition: To make playful or unkind jokes about someone.
entries.example: His classmates sometimes tease him about his enormous backpack.

entries.definition: An imitation, usually of lesser quality.
entries.example:
Is tortured thirst itself too sweet a cup?
Gall, and more bitter mocks, shall make it up.

entries.definition: Primarily physical senses.
entries.example: I touched his face softly.

entries.definition: A close embrace, especially when charged with an emotion such as affection, joy, relief, lust, anger, aggression, compassion, or the like, as opposed to being characterized by formality, equivocation or ambivalence (a half-embrace).
entries.example: She greeted her brother with a warm hug.

entries.definition: The act of striking the palms of the hands, or any two surfaces, together.
entries.example: He summoned the waiter with a clap.

entries.definition: To express approval (of something) by clapping the hands.
entries.example: After the performance, the audience applauded for five minutes.

entries.definition: To bend (any thin material, such as paper) over so that it comes in contact with itself.
entries.example: Next, fold the paper over, so the right half is on top of the left half.

entries.definition: To rest on one's bent knees, sometimes only one; to move to such a position.
entries.example: When the flames at last began to flicker and subside, his lids fluttered, then drooped ; but he had lost all reckoning of time when he opened them again to find Miss Erroll in furs kneeling on the hearth and heaping kindling on the coals, and her pretty little Alsatian maid beside her, laying a log across the andirons.

entries.definition: The act of seizing or capturing.

entries.definition: To ask for the presence or participation of someone or something.
entries.example: We invited our friends round for dinner.

entries.definition: Whose arrival is a cause of joy; received with gladness; admitted willingly to the house, entertainment, or company.
entries.example: a welcome visitor

entries.definition: To welcome in a friendly manner, either in person or through another means such as writing.
entries.example: My lord, the mayor of London comes to greet you.

entries.definition: An utterance or gesture expressing greeting or honor towards someone, (now especially) a formal, non-verbal gesture made with the arms or hands in any of various specific positions.
entries.example: The soldiers greeted the dignitaries with a crisp salute.

entries.definition: To extol or honour in a solemn manner.
entries.example: to celebrate the name of the Most High

entries.definition: To express one’s sympathetic pleasure or joy to the person(s) it is felt for
entries.example: Remind me to congratulate Dave and Lisa on their wedding.

entries.definition: To make something holy by religious rite, sanctify.
entries.example: The priest will bless the new church.

entries.definition: To join in, to take part, to involve oneself (in something).
entries.example: For the second year, foreign amateur runners were allowed to participate in a 10-kilometer race, a half-marathon or a full marathon in Pyongyang, the capital. The races were a part of the April 15 birthday celebration of Kim Il-sung, the former leader of North Korea and father of his successors: Kim Jong-il, a son, and Kim Jong-un, a grandson.

entries.definition: A wish of happiness or safety at parting, especially a permanent departure.
entries.example: He bid farewell to all of his fans.

entries.definition: To sort or arrange according to characteristic or class.
entries.example: They appear […] no way assorted to those with whom they must associate.

entries.definition: To be equivalent or similar in character, quantity, quality, origin, structure, function etc.
entries.example: Coordinate term: equate

entries.definition: Agreement of opinion, will, or action.
entries.example: These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Iesus, and with his brethen.

entries.definition: A characteristic or quality of a thing.
entries.example: His finest attribute is his kindness.

entries.definition: Remember a past event or piece of information.
entries.example: I cannot recall where I put the spare key.
entries.usage: Common learner sense selected in place of an unsuitable or less useful source default.

entries.definition: To recall; to collect one's thoughts again, especially about past events.
entries.example: I remember the concert clearly, but I can't recollect why I had decided to go there.

entries.definition: To cause one to experience a memory (of someone or something); to bring to the notice or consideration (of a person).
entries.example: I am aware, reader, and you need not remind me, that it is a dreadful thing for a parson to be warlike: […]

entries.definition: To tell again, often differently, what one has read or heard; to paraphrase.
entries.example: She will retell the story from her perspective in the next meeting.

entries.definition: To do or say again (and again).
entries.example: The scientists repeated the experiment in order to confirm the result.

entries.definition: Consideration of past times.
entries.example: My mind, calmer and stronger now than last night, made for itself some imperious rules, prohibiting under deadly penalties all weak retrospect of happiness past; commanding a patient journeying through the wilderness of the present...

entries.definition: To affect (someone) strongly and often favourably; to inspire admiration from (someone).
entries.example: You impressed me with your command of Urdu.

entries.definition: To get or be over without touching or resting on; to overcome.
entries.example: this difficulty may perhaps be surmounted by care and art

entries.definition: To discipline (one's body, appetites etc.) by suppressing desires; to practise abstinence on.
entries.example: Some people seek sainthood by mortifying the body.

entries.definition: To be in every part of; to spread through; to permeate.
entries.example: Cruel wars pervade history.

entries.definition: To restore to a former place, position, condition, etc.; to put back.
entries.example: When you've finished using the telephone, please replace the handset.

entries.definition: To use in place of something else, with the same function.
entries.example: I had no shallots so I substituted onion.

entries.definition: To recognize someone or something as different from others based on its characteristics.
entries.example: It had begun to take a leading place even in the days of the Ptolemies, and in scientific, as distinguished from purely literary work, it had assumed a position of primary importance early in the Christian era.

entries.definition: To modify so as to create a difference or distinction.
entries.example: A humble instance of Ablaut may be quoted which took place in the seventeenth century, when the word then was differentiated into the two forms then and than.

entries.definition: To bend or move (something) out of a given plane or direction, often the horizontal or vertical.
entries.example: He had to incline his body against the gusts to avoid being blown down in the storm.

entries.definition: To incline, deviate, or bend, from a vertical position; to be in a position thus inclining or deviating.
entries.example: a leaning column

entries.definition: Moving or directed toward one side.
entries.example: Giving Mary a sideways glance, he said,[…].

entries.definition: To use or experience the sense of touch.
entries.example: You can feel a heartbeat if you put your fingers on your breast.

entries.definition: A mental or emotional state, composure.
entries.example: I've been in a bad mood since I was dumped by my ex-boyfriend.

entries.definition: A person's internal state of being and involuntary physiological response to an object or a situation, based on or tied to physical state and sensory data.
entries.example: He was thinking; but the glory of the song, the swell from the great organ, the clustered lights, […], the height and vastness of this noble fane, its antiquity and its strength—all these things seemed to have their part as causes of the thrilling emotion that accompanied his thoughts.

entries.definition: A general tendency or orientation towards a certain type of mood, a volatile state; a habitual way of thinking, behaving or reacting.
entries.example: to have a good, bad, or calm temper

entries.definition: Mode of action; way of performing or doing anything.
entries.example: The treacherous manner of his mournful death.

entries.definition: The position of the body or way of carrying oneself.
entries.example: The ballet dancer walked with a graceful attitude.

entries.definition: A being involved in the action of a story; a persona.
entries.example: [I]n a tragedy, or epick poem, the hero of the piece must be advanced foremost to the view of the reader or spectator; he must outshine the rest of all the characters; he must appear the prince of them, like the sun in the Copernican system, encompassed with the less noble planets …

entries.definition: Of people, a set of non-physical psychological and social qualities that make one person distinct from another.
entries.example: The president has a unique personality.

entries.definition: An identifying characteristic, habit or trend.
entries.example: inherited traits and acquired traits

entries.definition: The idea of all that is good or excellent (in every sense of those terms) in a human being, collectively instantiated by a varying number of human traits known as "the virtues", the enumeration of which vary by the many virtue systems which have developed within different cultures, religions, and historical periods.
entries.example: Her honesty and patience are qualities of moral virtue.

entries.definition: An important or main item.
entries.example: a water feature

entries.definition: A person or animal's natural height when standing upright.
entries.example: His tall stature made him easy to spot in the crowd.

entries.definition: The soft tissue of the body, especially muscle and fat.
entries.example: The flesh of chicken, fowl, and turkey has much shorter fibre than that of ruminating animals, and is not intermingled with fat,—the fat always being found in layers directly under the skin, and surrounding the intestines.

entries.definition: The human race in its entirety.
entries.example: One small step for a man can be a giant leap for mankind.

entries.definition: Of or belonging to the species Homo sapiens or its closest relatives.
entries.example: Some powers diuine, or els infernall, mixt / Their angry ſeedes at his conception: / For he was neuer ſprong of humaine race, / Since with the ſpirit of his fearefull pride, / He dares so doubtleſly reſolue of rule.

entries.definition: A composite material consisting largely of calcium phosphate and collagen and making up the skeleton of most vertebrates.
entries.example: Ne take noon hede to brynge togidere þe parties of þe boon þat is to-broken or dislocate, til viij. daies ben goon in þe wyntir, & v. in þe somer; for þanne it schal make quytture, and be sikir from swellynge; & þanne brynge togidere þe brynkis eiþer þe disiuncture after þe techynge þat schal be seid in þe chapitle of algebra.

entries.definition: The series of vertebrae, separated by disks, that encloses and protects the spinal cord, and runs down the middle of the back in vertebrate animals.
entries.example: The backbone supports the body and protects the spinal cord.

entries.definition: The system that provides support to an organism, where in vertebrates it is internal and consists of bones and cartilage, and external in some other animals.
entries.example: At the foot of a pretty big pine, and involved in a green creeper, which had even partly lifted some of the smaller bones, a human skeleton lay, with a few shreds of clothing, on the ground.

entries.definition: The main bones of the head considered as a unit; including the cranium, facial bones, and mandible.
entries.example: All the time six or eight large Chinese gongs were being beaten by the vigorous arms of as many young men, producing such a deafening discord that I was glad to escape to the round house, where I slept very comfortably with half a dozen smoke-dried human skulls suspended over my head.

entries.definition: The control center of the central nervous system of an animal located in the skull, consisting of the cerebrum, cerebellum, and brainstem, which is responsible for perception, cognition, attention, memory, emotion, and action.
entries.example: The Ueynes are ſpred foorth throughout the whole bodie, howbeit from one welhead, that is to ſay from the Liuer: ſo be the Sinews, howbeit from the Brayne; So likewiſe are the Heartſtrings, howbeit from the Heart.

entries.definition: The capability for rational thought.
entries.example: Despite advancing age, his mind was still as sharp as ever.

entries.definition: Of matter and nature.
entries.example: It's not so much a physical place as a state of mind.

entries.definition: Of or relating to the mind or specifically the total emotional and intellectual response of an individual to external reality.
entries.example: I don't mean all of your friends—only a small proportion—which, however, connects your circle with that deadly, idle, brainless bunch—the insolent chatterers at the opera,[…], the neurotic victims of mental cirrhosis, the jewelled animals whose moral code is the code of the barnyard—!

entries.definition: The soft skin on each side of the face, below the eyes; the outer surface of the sides of the oral cavity.
entries.example: There are some shrewd contents in yon same paper, / That steals the colours from Bassanio's cheek: / Some dear friend dead; else nothing in the world / Could turn so much the constitution / Of any constant man. What, worse and worse!— […]

entries.definition: The part of the face above the eyebrows and below the hairline.
entries.example: 'This question the Dodo could not answer without a great deal of thought, and it sat for a long time with one finger pressed upon its forehead (the position in which you usually see Shakespeare, in the pictures of him), while the rest waited in silence. At last the Dodo said, ‘everybody has won, and all must have prizes.’'

entries.definition: The bony ridge over the eyes, upon which the eyebrows are located.
entries.example: He wiped the sweat from his brow.

entries.definition: One of the hairs which grows along the edge of eyelids.
entries.example: An eyelash had fallen onto her cheek.

entries.definition: Either of the two fleshy protrusions around the opening of the mouth.
entries.example: […]thine owne lippes teſtifie againſt thee.

entries.definition: The front opening of a creature through which food is ingested.
entries.example: "Open your mouth and say 'aah'," directed the doctor.

entries.definition: The flexible muscular organ in the mouth that is used to move food around, for tasting and that is moved into various positions to modify the flow of air from the lungs in order to produce different sounds in speech.
entries.example: But lering and lurking here and there like ſpies,

entries.definition: The front part of the neck.
entries.example: The wild pitch bounced and hit the catcher in the throat.

entries.definition: A deep narrow valley with steep sides, often containing a river.
entries.example: The river runs through a deep gorge.
entries.usage: Common learner sense selected in place of an unsuitable or less useful source default.

entries.definition: The bottom of a face, (specifically) the typically jutting jawline below the mouth.
entries.example: What does it mean to have a pointy chin instead of a flat chin?

entries.definition: One of the bones, usually bearing teeth, which form the framework of the mouth.
entries.example: The dentist examined her jaw after she complained of pain.

entries.definition: The part of the body connecting the head and the trunk found in humans and some animals.
entries.example: Giraffes have long necks.

entries.definition: Facial hair on the chin, cheeks, jaw and neck.
entries.example: He trimmed his beard before the interview.

entries.definition: The part of an animal's body between the base of the neck and arm socket.
entries.example: The parrot was sitting on Steve's shoulder.

entries.definition: A major appendage of human or animal, used for locomotion (such as an arm, leg or wing).
entries.example:
UUhoſe hands are made to gripe a warlike Lance—
Their ſhoulders broad, for complet armour fit,
Their lims more large and of a bigger ſize
Than all the brats yſprong from Typhons loins:

entries.definition: The joint between the upper arm and the forearm.
entries.example: Up to the elbowes naked were there Armes.

entries.definition: The complex joint between forearm bones, carpus, and metacarpals where the hand is attached to the arm; the carpus in a narrow sense.
entries.example: With a flick of the wrist, he threw the frisbee to a team-mate.

entries.definition: The shortest and thickest digit of the hand that for humans has the most mobility and can be made to oppose (moved to touch) all of the other fingers.
entries.example: He pressed the button with his thumb.

entries.definition: Any of various evergreen trees from the family Palmae or Arecaceae, which are mainly found in the tropics.
entries.example: A tall palm provides shade beside the beach.

entries.definition: A slender jointed extremity of the human hand, (often) exclusive of the thumb, and the corresponding part, irrespective of including a thumb, in many other animals.
entries.example: Humans have two hands and ten fingers. Each hand has one thumb and four fingers.

entries.definition: A hand with the fingers clenched or curled inward.
entries.example: The boxer's fists rained down on his opponent in the last round.

entries.definition: A box, now usually a large strong box with a secure convex lid.
entries.example: The clothes are kept in a chest.

entries.definition: The belly, or that part of the body between the thorax and the pelvis, not including the back; or in some lower vertebrates, the portion between the cardiac and caudal regions.
entries.example: The doctor gently examined the patient's abdomen.

entries.definition: Any of a series of long curved bones occurring in 12 pairs in humans and other animals and extending from the spine to or toward the sternum.
entries.example: On an early winter afternoon, clear but not cold, when the vegetable world was a weird multitude of skeletons through whose ribs the sun shone freely, a gleaming landau came to a pause on the crest of a hill in Wessex.

entries.definition: The part of the body between the pelvis and the stomach.
entries.example: The belt fitted comfortably around her waist.

entries.definition: The larger part of an organism, composed of tissues that perform similar functions.
entries.example: bodily organs

entries.definition: A large organ in the body that stores and metabolizes nutrients, destroys toxins and produces bile. It is responsible for thousands of biochemical reactions.
entries.example: Steve Jobs is a famous liver transplant recipient.

entries.definition: An organ in animals that stores food in the process of digestion.
entries.example: Our stomachs and livers have an enzyme known as alcohol dehydrogenase that breaks down ethanol to make it less toxic for our bodies, said Atlanta gastroenterologist Dr. Preston Stewart.

entries.definition: In female mammals, the organ in which the young are conceived and grow until birth; the uterus.
entries.example: I danced myself right out the womb / Is it strange to dance so soon?

entries.definition: An organ in the body that filters the blood, producing urine.
entries.example: The liver and the kidneys of animals have long been gastronomically popular for their aphrodisiac properties.

entries.definition: A biological organ of vertebrates that controls breathing and oxygenates the blood.
entries.example: I made a speaking trumpet of my hands and commenced to whoop “Ahoy!” and “Hello!” at the top of my lungs. […] The Colonel woke up, and, after asking what in brimstone was the matter, opened his mouth and roared “Hi!” and “Hello!” like the bull of Bashan.

entries.definition: A specialized cell, group of cells, or organ of endothelial origin in the human or animal body that synthesizes a chemical substance, such as hormones or breast milk, and releases it, often into the bloodstream (endocrine gland) or into cavities inside the body or its outer surface (exocrine gland).
entries.example: A sweat gland releases fluid onto the skin.

entries.definition: A room or set of rooms
entries.example: Once upon a midnight dreary, while I pondered, weak and weary, / Over many a quaint and curious volume of forgotten lore, / While I nodded, nearly napping, suddenly there came a tapping, / As of some one gently rapping, rapping at my chamber door.

entries.definition: The alimentary canal of an animal through which food passes after having passed all stomachs.
entries.example: Nutrients are absorbed through the wall of the intestine.

entries.definition: The upper leg of a human, between the hip and the knee.
entries.example: I coniure thee by Rosalines bright eyes, By her High forehead, and her Scarlet lip, By her Fine foote, Straight leg, and Quiuering thigh, And the Demeanes, that there Adiacent lie, That in thy likenesse thou appeare to vs.

entries.definition: United, combined
entries.example: the joint influences of culture and climate

entries.definition: In humans, the joint or the region of the joint in the middle part of the leg between the thigh and the shank.
entries.example: Penny was wearing a miniskirt, so she skinned her exposed knees when she fell.

entries.definition: The upper legs of a seated person.
entries.example: The child fell asleep on her father's lap.
entries.usage: Common learner sense selected in place of an unsuitable or less useful source default.

entries.definition: The skeletal joint which connects the foot with the leg; the uppermost portion of the foot and lowermost portion of the leg, which contain this skeletal joint.
entries.example: She twisted her ankle while stepping off the pavement.

entries.definition: The rear part of the foot, where it joins the leg.
entries.example: He [the stag] calls to mind his strength and then his speed, / His winged heels and then his armed head.

entries.definition: Each of the five digits on the end of the human foot.
entries.example: An old traditional prescription for provoking erotic inclinations ran as follows, The toe of the foot of a man, anointed with oil, or honey, or the ashes of a weasel.

entries.definition: A contractile form of tissue which animals use to effect movement.
entries.example: Muscle consists largely of actin and myosin filaments.

entries.definition: A tiny opening in the skin.
entries.example: I could sense the sweat dripping out of all my pores.

entries.definition: A normally regular beat felt when arteries near the skin (for example, at the neck or wrist) are depressed, caused by the heart pumping blood through them; the qualitative nature of this beat.
entries.example: Her pulse was thready and weak.

entries.definition: Any of the muscular- and elastic-walled blood vessels forming part of the circulation system by which blood is conveyed away from the heart regardless of its oxygenation status; see pulmonary artery.
entries.example: As we age, the major arteries of our bodies frequently become thickened with plaque, a fatty material with an oatmeal-like consistency that builds up along the inner lining of blood vessels. The reason plaque forms isn’t entirely known, but it seems to be related to high levels of cholesterol inducing an inflammatory response, which can also attract and trap more cellular debris over time.

entries.definition: A bundle of neurons with their connective tissue sheaths, blood vessels and lymphatics.
entries.example: The nerves can be seen through the skin.

entries.definition: Any substance produced by one tissue and conveyed by the bloodstream to another to effect physiological activity.
entries.example: Interfemale dominance may be facilitated by female sex hormones as well as adrenal testosterone...

entries.definition: Exempt; not subject to.
entries.example: As a diplomat, you are immune from prosecution.

entries.definition: An external phenomenon that has an influence on a system, by triggering or modifying an internal phenomenon; for example, a spur or incentive that drives a person to take action or change behaviour.
entries.example: an economic stimulus

entries.definition: Any cyclic biological or physiological pattern or activity.
entries.example: Sleep and waking follow a daily biorhythm.

entries.definition: A style of living that reflects the attitudes and values of a person or group.
entries.example: Don't leave me stranded here / I can't get used to this lifestyle

entries.definition: An action performed on a regular basis.
entries.example: It’s become a habit of mine to have a cup of coffee after dinner.

entries.definition: Any of the manners by which living beings perceive the physical world: for humans sight, smell, hearing, touch, taste.
entries.example: Let fancy still my sense in Lethe steep.

entries.definition: The sense or faculty by which objects are perceived through the agency of light; the sense by which we see.
entries.example: Sight is a precious gift.

entries.definition: Vision or the faculty of sight.
entries.example: good eyesight

entries.definition: Visual perception.
entries.example: He changed seats to get a complete view of the stage.

entries.definition: Related to or affecting the vision.
entries.example: Earless ghost swift moths become “invisible” to echolocating bats by forming mating clusters close[…]above vegetation and effectively blending into the clutter of echoes that the bat receives from the leaves and stems around them. Many insects probably use this strategy, which is a close analogy to crypsis in the visible world—camouflage and other methods for blending into one’s visual background.

entries.definition: Able to be seen.
entries.example: When the sun rises, the world becomes visible.

entries.definition: Not clearly expressed; stated in indefinite terms.
entries.example: It follows from what has been said that a vague thought has more likelihood of being true than a precise one. To try and hit an object with a vague thought is like trying to hit the bull's eye with a lump of putty: when the putty reaches the target, it flattens out all over it, and probably covers the bull's eye along with the rest. To try and hit an object with a precise thought is like trying to hit the bull's eye with a bullet. The advantage of the precise thought is that it distinguishes between the bull's eye and the rest of the target.

entries.definition: Unable to see, or only partially able to see.
entries.example: Even a blind hen sometimes finds a grain of corn.

entries.definition: Stupid.
entries.example: You are so dumb! You don't even know how to make toast!

entries.definition: Of or pertaining to the ear.
entries.example: The aural surgeon attends Mondays and Thursdays, at half-past one.

entries.definition: Of or concerning the teeth.
entries.example: dental care

entries.definition: Not asleep; conscious.
entries.example: By quarter to six all this had me so awake and agitated that even the Balinese wind chimes that I hung up in the garden to relax me began to sound like Big Ben.

entries.definition: To open the mouth widely and take a long, rather deep breath, often because one is tired or bored, and sometimes accompanied by pandiculation.
entries.example: I could see my students yawning, so I knew the lesson was boring them.

entries.definition: To have a nap; to sleep for a short period of time, especially during the day.
entries.example: I like to nap for twenty minutes after lunch.

entries.definition: To sleep lightly or briefly; to nap, snooze.
entries.example: I didn’t sleep very well, but I think I may have dozed a bit.

entries.definition: With little or no sound; free of disturbing noise.
entries.example: I can't hear the music; it is too quiet.

entries.definition: In a state of sleep; also, broadly, resting.
entries.example: I was asleep when you called.

entries.definition: A person who is severely impaired or deficient in some non-physical way.
entries.example: Many a one, who perhaps doesn't suspect it, is a moral cripple, or maybe a mental cripple.

entries.definition: Unable to walk properly because of a problem with one's feet or legs.
entries.example: With the years, this horse has little by little gone lame.

entries.definition: Any member of a race of beings from (especially Scandinavian and other Germanic) folklore, usually depicted as having some sort of supernatural powers and being skilled in crafting and metalworking, often as short with long beards, and sometimes as clashing with elves.
entries.example: [T]he elf king and his queen made a royal progress every noon with a splendid retinue of dwarves and sprites, […]

entries.definition: The condition of being pregnant; an instance of this.
entries.example: News that the duchess is in the "very early stages" of pregnancy with the third-in-line to the throne was officially released after she was taken to the King Edward VII hospital in central London, suffering from hyperemesis gravidarun, very acute morning sickness.

entries.definition: past participle of bear; given birth to.
entries.example: Although not born in the country, she qualifies for nationality through her grandparents.

entries.definition: A flexible sleeve made of latex or other impermeable material such as polyurethane or sheepskin, worn over an erect penis during sexual intercourse as a contraceptive or as a way to prevent the spread of STIs during PIV, anal, or oral.
entries.example: buy a pack of condoms

entries.definition: A living organism (originally a plant) produced asexually from a single ancestor, to which it is genetically identical.
entries.example: This new species is a clone of the mimosa plant.

entries.definition: A perceived change in some function, sensation or appearance of a person that indicates a disease or disorder, such as fever, headache or rash; strictly, a symptom is felt or experienced by the patient, while a sign can be detected by an observer.
entries.example: The doctor told that his coughing and sneezing was the symptom of standing for too long in the rain.

entries.definition: An abnormal condition of a human, animal or plant that causes discomfort or dysfunction; distinct from injury insofar as the latter is usually instantaneously acquired.
entries.example: The tomato plants had some kind of disease that left their leaves splotchy and their fruit withered.

entries.definition: An instance (episode) of a disease or poor health.
entries.example: Her grandmother had passed away after a long illness.

entries.definition: A low, mournful cry of pain, sorrow or pleasure.
entries.example: let out a deep moan

entries.definition: The entry and growth of disease-causing organisms in the body.
entries.example: The infection spread from the cut to the surrounding skin.

entries.definition: Harm, hurt, damage.
entries.example: “But marriage in secret, Nikolay Vsyevolodovitch — a fatal secret. I receive money from you, and I'm suddenly asked the question, 'What's that money for?' My hands are tied; I cannot answer to the detriment of my sister, to the detriment of the family honour.”

entries.definition: An acute myocardial infarction, sometimes fatal, caused by the sudden occurrence of coronary thrombosis, which obstructs the blood supply to the heart and leads to necrosis of heart muscle tissue.
entries.example: Before kick-off, a section of Chelsea's support sadly let themselves and their club down by noisily interrupting the silence held in memory of the Hillsborough disaster and for Livorno midfielder Piermario Morosini, who collapsed and died after suffering a heart attack during a Serie B game on Saturday.

entries.definition: Damaged or separated into pieces; the past participle of break.
entries.example: The storm had broken several branches.

entries.definition: To render unable; to take away an ability of, as by crippling.
entries.example: The accident disabled his right arm for several weeks.

entries.definition: Not valid; not true, correct, acceptable, or appropriate.
entries.example: Your argument is invalid because it uses circular reasoning.

entries.definition: Willing to wait if necessary; not losing one's temper while waiting.
entries.example: Be patient: your friends will arrive in a few hours.

entries.definition: A failure to function in an expected or complete manner. Usually refers to a disorder in a bodily organ (e.g. erectile dysfunction), a mental disorder, or the improper behavior of a social group.
entries.example: Cerebellar dysfunction is characterized by truncal ataxia, a broad-based stance, dysmetria in which the limbs either overstep (hypermetria) or understep (hypometria), and tremor that is most pronounced when the animal attempts a goal-orientated movement (intention tremor).

entries.definition: Diabetes mellitus; any of a group of metabolic diseases whereby a person (or other animal) has high blood sugar due to an inability to produce, or inability to metabolize, sufficient quantities of the hormone insulin.
entries.example: In the UK, one in 10 people over 40 live with type 2 diabetes, while one in four have high blood pressure, a condition described as a “silent killer” because it increases the risk of heart attack and stroke but rarely causes symptoms beforehand.

entries.definition: The state of being obese.
entries.example: The fowls, ducks, and goats all looked fat and thriving on the refuse food of a dense population, and the Chinamen's pigs were in a state of obesity that foreboded early death.

entries.definition: Having a higher weight, especially body fat, than what is generally considered healthy for a given body type and height.
entries.example: Before her diet, Jane was noticeably overweight, but she shed five kilos in the next two months.

entries.definition: A state of abnormally high blood pressure of arterial blood (arterial hypertension) or of the intra-ocular fluid.
entries.example: Once stroke was classified by a risk factor-free method, the stronger relationship between hypertension and lacunar versus nonlacunar infarction patients disappeared.

entries.definition: To cause loss of the ability to move all or part of the body.
entries.example: The injury could paralyse his legs if the spinal cord were damaged.

entries.definition: Experiencing a sensation of whirling and of being giddy, unbalanced, or lightheaded.
entries.example: I stood up too fast and felt dizzy.

entries.definition: Exhibiting unsoundness or disorder of mind; not sane; utterly mad.
entries.example: What is the cause of insanity? Nobody can answer such a sweeping question as that, but we know that certain diseases, such as syphilis, break down and destroy the brain cells and result in insanity. In fact, about one-half of all mental diseases can be attributed to such physical causes as brain lesions, alcohol, toxins, and injuries. But the other half—and this is the appalling part of the story—the other half of the people who go insane apparently have nothing organically wrong with their brain cells. entries.example: He was out of temper after waiting an hour for the bus.
entries.usage: This expression is dated; be in a bad mood is more common in everyday speech.

entries.definition: Sheets, pillowcases and other fabric coverings used on a bed.
entries.example: Fresh bed linen is provided every week.

entries.definition: To be likely to experience something, especially something undesirable.
entries.example: This low-lying road is prone to flooding after heavy rain.

entries.definition: A course designed for people who are starting to learn a subject.
entries.example: The beginning course introduces basic keyboard skills.
entries.usage: Beginner course or introductory course is more usual.

entries.definition: Straps worn around the waist to hold clothing or for decoration.
entries.example: The shop sells leather belts in several sizes.

entries.definition: Any of several mechanisms that regulate the periodicity of biological functions, such as the circadian rhythm.
entries.example:
2005 US Department of Health - Your guide to healthy sleep
Your biological clock is actually a tiny bundle of cells in your brain that responds to light signals received through your eyes.

entries.definition: A black waterproof coat worn in rainy weather.
entries.example: The woman in the black raincoat left her umbrella at reception.

entries.definition: A garment worn from the waist down that is black in colour and has no separate legs.
entries.example: She paired a black skirt with a white blouse.

entries.definition: Tea leaves which have been "fermented" (actually, oxidized) before drying to enhance their flavour (cf. green tea).
entries.example: The producer dries the oxidized leaves to make black tea.

entries.definition: A pair of trousers made from black fabric.
entries.example: The restaurant asks its servers to wear black trousers.

entries.definition: A cocktail of stout and champagne (or sometimes a cheaper type of sparkling white wine).
entries.example: The bartender mixed a black velvet with stout and champagne.

entries.definition: Solid pieces of material, often used for building or play.
entries.example: The children built a tower from wooden blocks.

entries.definition: The continuous circulation of blood in the cardiovascular system; bloodstream.
entries.example: Exercise increases blood flow to the working muscles.

entries.definition: A sample of blood.
entries.example: The nurse collected a blood sample for testing.

entries.definition: The opening or flowering of blossoms.
entries.example: The spring bloom of flowers attracts bees to the orchard.

entries.definition: A knitted upper-body garment that is blue in colour.
entries.example: I left my blue sweater on the chair near the window.

entries.definition: A residential school, where the students are housed on-site (the school provides board and lodging as well as education), sometimes involuntarily, typically at a pre-collegiate level.
