It was in these boarding schools where Native language, culture and ceremony would be beaten out of the Native children in order to 'Kill the Indian and Save the Child'.

entries.definition: A trip made by boat or ship.
entries.example: Our boat trip lasted two hours.

entries.definition: Reserve something before the time it is needed.
entries.example: You should book in advance if you want a weekend appointment.

entries.definition: An arrangement to hold a book for someone to borrow or buy.
entries.example: My book reservation is ready for collection at the library.

entries.definition: Hard structures forming the skeleton.
entries.example: The X-ray showed that none of the bones in her hand were broken.

entries.definition: A building or room which contains lanes for bowling.
entries.example: We booked two lanes at the bowling alley.

entries.definition: A place where a variety of plants are grown, primarily for scientific or educational reasons, but are normally open to the public, and include ornamental plants from around the world.
entries.example: The botanical garden has a collection of tropical plants.

entries.definition: A board on which messages may be posted, especially one in a public space.
entries.example: Somewhere near Fillmore she found the symbol tacked to the bulletin board of a laundromat, among other scraps of paper offering cheap ironing and baby sitters.

entries.definition: stunningly beautiful; amazing
entries.example: He went to the Grand Canyon and spent a week taking in the breathtaking scenery all around him.

entries.definition: To raise fish and encourage them to reproduce.
entries.example: The farm breeds fish in large freshwater tanks.

entries.definition: A UK organization that promotes cultural relations and educational opportunities internationally.
entries.example: She attended an English workshop offered by the British Council.

entries.definition: The national library of the United Kingdom.
entries.example: I searched the British Library's catalogue for an old newspaper.

entries.definition: A museum in London with collections relating to human history and culture.
entries.example: We included a visit to the British Museum in our London itinerary.

entries.definition: Increase your knowledge and experience of the world.
entries.example: Living abroad can broaden your horizons.
entries.usage: The usual expression is broaden one's horizons, with horizons in the plural.

entries.definition: To develop a wider understanding of the world or a subject.
entries.example: Studying overseas can broaden one's view of different ways of life.
entries.usage: Broaden one's horizons is a common alternative.

entries.definition: The brother of one's spouse or the husband of one's sibling.
entries.example: My brother-in-law helped us move the furniture.

entries.definition: Large road vehicles carrying multiple passengers.
entries.example: Two buses stop outside the university library.

entries.definition: A pass that allows the user to travel on buses for a certain duration or a certain number of trips.
entries.example: A city block, chock full of empty heroin bags, used condoms, dirty diapers and expired bus passes. Sewer grates, straining under the weight of quarter water bottles and wrappers from cheap snacks and cakes.

entries.definition: Paths followed by scheduled bus services.
entries.example: The map shows all the local bus routes.

entries.definition: A small card with a person's name and professional information (such as occupation, business phone number, e-mail address, etc.).
entries.example: She gave me her business card after the meeting.

entries.definition: A high-quality class of travelling (especially in airlines), higher than economy class or budget, lower than first class.
entries.example: He flew business class because the long journey required an overnight flight.

entries.definition: The shared values, habits and expectations of a workplace or business community.
entries.example: New employees attend a workshop on the company's business culture.

entries.definition: The branch of ethics that examines questions of moral right and wrong arising in the context of business practice or theory.
entries.example: The course discusses business ethics and fair treatment of employees.

entries.definition: A university division, or its teaching staff, specializing in business subjects.
entries.example: The business faculty offers courses in accounting and management.

entries.definition: An academic subject covering various elements of business, such as accountancy and marketing.
entries.example: Business studies includes subjects such as accounting and marketing.

entries.definition: Travel for business purposes, often paid for at least partially by the employer.
entries.example: I had occasion […] to make a somewhat long business trip to Chicago, and on my return […] I found Farrar awaiting me in the railway station. He smiled his wonted fraction by way of greeting, […] and finally leading me to his buggy, turned and drove out of town. I was completely mystified at such an unusual proceeding.

entries.definition: Enclosures made of bars, wire, or similar material.
entries.example: The rescue centre keeps recovering birds in large cages.

entries.definition: Keys used to unlock a cabin or a room on a ship.
entries.example: Please return your cabin keys before leaving the ferry.

entries.definition: A streetcar moved by gripping to rotating loop of cable running along the track.
entries.example: We took the cable car up the steep street.

entries.definition: A library counter dealing with loans and inquiries.
entries.example: Return your books to the circulation desk.

entries.definition: A form used to request a library item from storage or a closed collection.
entries.example: Fill in a call slip to request the manuscript.

entries.definition: Illegal activity taking place on the grounds of a college or university.
entries.example: Better lighting may help reduce campus crime.

entries.definition: Wax or similar objects with a wick that burns to produce light.
entries.example: We lit candles when the electricity failed.

entries.definition: To be unable to finish something by the required time.
entries.example: I cannot meet the deadline because the survey results have not arrived.

entries.definition: A particular design or type of car produced by a manufacturer.
entries.example: This car model is available with either two or four doors.

entries.definition: The hiring of automobiles (motor cars) for relatively short periods.
entries.example: Car rental is included in the holiday package.

entries.definition: The rubber coverings around the wheels of a car.
entries.example: Check your car tyres before a long journey.
entries.usage: Tyres is British spelling; tires is American spelling.

entries.definition: Any index formed with index cards, as was common in many businesses before the microcomputer revolution.
entries.example: Near-synonym: card catalogue

entries.definition: A set of cards used to list and locate library resources.
entries.example: The old card catalog lists books by author and subject.

entries.definition: A small form used to give feedback about a service or experience.
entries.example: We filled in a comment card after our meal.

entries.definition: Cutting and shaping wood to make an object or decoration.
entries.example: She enjoys carving wood into small animal figures.
entries.usage: Wood carving is the usual noun for the craft.

entries.definition: Research performed in detail on a single individual, group, incident or community, as opposed to, for instance, a sample of the whole population.
entries.example: The report uses a case study of one village to examine the effects of flooding.

entries.definition: Detailed investigations of particular people, organisations or situations.
entries.example: The seminar uses case studies of three successful businesses.

entries.definition: Options concerning buildings, equipment, or services available for use.
entries.example: The accommodation brochure lists several choices of facilities, including a gym and a pool.
entries.usage: Choices of facilities is more natural than choices for facilities when comparing amenities.

entries.definition: Devices that record sound on magnetic tape cassettes.
entries.example: The archive keeps cassette recorders for playing old interview tapes.

entries.definition: An electronic device that plays compact discs.
entries.example: She takes it to the living room, grateful for the ancient CD player that still sits proudly on the trolley beneath the window like a prized relic because Simiso is of the generation that will simply not part with things no matter how many deaths they die.

entries.definition: compact disk - read only memory: an optical disc containing data that can be read (but not changed) by a computer
entries.example: The old textbook includes a CD-ROM with practice exercises.

entries.definition: Informal clothing suitable for ordinary activities.
entries.example: You can wear casual clothes to the welcome party.

entries.definition: Informal clothing worn for everyday activities.
entries.example: Casual wear is acceptable in the office on Fridays.

entries.definition: Amounts of money requested for goods or services.
entries.example: The hotel lists all additional charges on the invoice.

entries.definition: Provide what a particular person or group wants or needs.
entries.example: The evening classes cater to adults who work during the day.

entries.definition: Rooms, equipment, or services used to prepare and serve food.
entries.example: The conference venue has catering facilities for two hundred guests.

entries.definition: People who prepare, serve or organise food and drink.
entries.example: The catering staff arranged the buffet before the guests arrived.

entries.definition: A hall situated in the middle of a building or complex.
entries.example: The information desk is in the central hall beside the staircase.
entries.usage: Central hall is the more usual expression; Centre Hall could also be a place name.

entries.definition: A person responsible for running a centre.
entries.example: The centre manager approved our request to use the meeting room.

entries.definition: Any of various heating systems in which a central source of heat is used to distribute heat (and sometimes hot water) throughout a building in a controlled manner.
entries.example: The central heating kept the house warm throughout winter.

entries.definition: A street name that may be used in different towns and cities.
entries.example: The address on the invitation is 18 Central Avenue.
entries.usage: This name alone does not identify a particular street or city.

entries.definition: A large public, urban park in the borough of Manhattan in New York City.
entries.example: I've been walkin' Central Park, singing after dark / People think I'm crazy

entries.definition: A name commonly used for a city's main or centrally located railway station.
entries.example: The meeting instructions say to wait outside Central Station.
entries.usage: This name alone does not identify a particular city or station.

entries.definition: A document showing completion of training or a qualification in caring for children.
entries.example: She earned a certificate in childcare before applying to the nursery.
entries.usage: Certificate in childcare is more conventional; the exact qualification varies by institution.

entries.definition: An organization established to help people or support a public benefit rather than make profits.
entries.example: The charitable organisation provides meals for people without stable housing.

entries.definition: A hospital supported by charitable donations or providing charitable care.
entries.example: The charity hospital offers treatment to patients who cannot afford the fees.

entries.definition: To announce or record one's own arrival at a hotel, airport etc.
entries.example: We got to the hotel last night and checked in at the front desk.

entries.definition: To record the departure or withdrawal of someone or something (such as guests, employees, books, etc.).
entries.example: He checked his favorite mystery out for the twenty-third time.

entries.definition: An infection affecting the lungs or airways in the chest.
entries.example: He stayed home because a chest infection made breathing uncomfortable.

entries.definition: A room equipped for experiments involving substances and their reactions.
entries.example: Wear safety goggles in the chemistry lab.

entries.definition: A road name that may be used in different towns and villages.
entries.example: Turn left into Church Road at the traffic lights.
entries.usage: This name alone does not identify a particular road.

entries.definition: A folder or booklet containing preprinted cheques for use by the holder of a bank account.
entries.example: She wrote a payment cheque from her chequebook.

entries.definition: A small plastic card issued by a bank or similar which is a guarantee of payment of cheques written by the cardholder (up to a specified maximum amount).
entries.example: Banks have decided to end cheque guarantee card payments from July 2011. / The 24 members of the current cheque card system said that they had made the move in order to reflect consumer trends, with the popularity of the payment method in "terminal decline".

entries.definition: Give your attention or effort to a particular activity or subject.
entries.example: Please concentrate on the final question for the next five minutes.

entries.definition: A show featuring circus acts such as acrobatics or juggling.

entries.definition: A day devoted to celebrating children and promoting their welfare.
entries.example: The school organised games for Children's Day.
entries.usage: The date and customs vary between countries.

entries.definition: The process or industry of making cheese from milk.

entries.definition: The growth of a city in size or area.
entries.example: The city's expansion has brought new housing to former farmland.

entries.definition: A governing body of people elected to oversee management of a city and represent the interests of residents.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: town council, municipal council, common council, select council, consulate (obsolete), capitoulate (historical, Toulouse)

entries.definition: A picture or view of a city seen from above.
entries.example: The overhead view of the city shows the river winding through the centre.
entries.usage: An overhead view of the city is the conventional word order.

entries.definition: People who travel regularly between home and work or study.
entries.example: Commuters crowded onto the early train.

entries.definition: A student chosen to speak for the members of a class.

entries.definition: People who gain control of a place or people by force.

entries.definition: Tools and machines used to remove dirt.

entries.definition: A line of reasoning that is easy to understand.

entries.definition: People who study in the same class.

entries.definition: A rough surface with relatively large particles or fibres.

entries.definition: Clothes that feel pleasant to wear and allow easy movement.
entries.example: Wear comfortable clothes for the stretching class.

entries.definition: People who work together.
entries.example: My colleagues helped me finish the report.

entries.definition: Keep checking the time, often because you want work or an activity to end.
entries.example: I tend to clock-watch when a meeting runs past lunchtime.

entries.definition: Library shelves that readers cannot browse directly.

entries.usage: Closed stacks is a common library term.

entries.definition: An examination in which students may not consult books or notes.

entries.usage: Closed-book exam is the conventional form.

entries.definition: A library collection kept away from open shelves and supplied by staff on request.

entries.definition: A camera system that sends video to selected monitors, often for security.

entries.definition: A small café or restaurant typically selling light refreshments along with coffee-based drinks.

entries.definition: A machine that prepares coffee.

entries.definition: A container that gathers and holds liquid.

entries.definition: Groups of objects gathered together.

entries.definition: A collection of names and details used to reach people.

entries.definition: A person who writes and develops computer programs.

entries.definition: Computer hardware that processes audio input and output.

entries.definition: Managing pressure or worry in a way that allows you to function.

entries.definition: A social gathering of people wearing disguises or costumes, and amusing themselves with dancing, conversation, or other diversions.

entries.definition: A medicine or medication used to treat coughs, usually in liquid or syrup form.

entries.definition: A payment required to attend a course.

entries.definition: The type or physical form in which money is used.

entries.definition: plural of decade.

The dramatic fall in crime since the 1990s has persuaded many that they were right. Locking up the worst criminals while they are young, fit and dangerous clearly makes America safer. But keeping sad cases[…]incarcerated past pensionable age serves little purpose. Prison has diminishing returns, and America long ago passed the point where jailing more people makes sense.

entries.definition: Balloons used to decorate a room or event.

entries.definition: Give a formal talk to an audience.

entries.definition: A counter where deliveries are received, collected, or arranged.

entries.definition: A building occupied by a university or organisational department.

entries.definition: A large store containing many different departments, each of which deals in the sale of different goods or services.

entries.definition: The personal name chosen for a child, usually by their parents.

entries.definition: To provide written authorisation for a patient to obtain medicine.
entries.example: The doctor gave me a prescription for the tablets.
entries.usage: Write a prescription or prescribe medicine is often more natural.

entries.definition: To surrender (someone or something); to inform on (someone).
entries.example: He was surrounded, so gave himself up.

entries.definition: Present a formal talk to an audience.
entries.example: She will give a speech about renewable energy at the conference.

entries.definition: To state that an arrangement or fact has been accepted or verified.
entries.example: The hotel will give confirmation of your booking by email.

entries.definition: To receive comments about work or performance.

entries.definition: Alternative spelling of guide book.

entries.definition: A trip where a knowledgeable guide leads a group to a destination, providing commentary and historical context while often handling logistics like accommodation and transportation.
entries.example: Oliver immediately gets a guided tour, Felix wheeling through libraries and endless colour-coded rooms, up and down staircases and along echoing halls where various "dead relly[s]" stare down from the walls.

entries.definition: Visit a hospital or be admitted there for medical care.
entries.example: He had to go to hospital after injuring his ankle.

entries.definition: Listening to understand the overall meaning rather than every detail.

entries.definition: A sustained increase in the average temperature of the Earth, sufficient to cause climate change.

entries.definition: A medal made of, or having the color of, gold, given as a prize for winning.
entries.example: Great Britain has collected its first gold medal of the London Games after Heather Stanning and Helen Glover won the coxless pairs with a stunning performance that will spark a mass outpouring of celebration and relief across the country.

entries.definition: A street name that may be used in different places.
entries.example: The delivery address is 12 Gold Street.

entries.definition: In golf, the implement used to hit the golf ball.
entries.example: Once the tough job is done for Prosser, he says he can then get his golf clubs back out - they have been in the cupboard untouched for a decade.

entries.definition: The ability to see clearly.
entries.example: You need good eyesight to read these tiny labels without glasses.

entries.definition: Shoes that are suitable, comfortable, or well made.

entries.definition: Effective control of the direction of a vehicle.
entries.example: Good steering is essential on a narrow mountain road.

entries.definition: A celebration held before someone leaves a place or group.
entries.example: We organized a goodbye party for our departing colleague.

entries.definition: A plan or set of principles adopted by a government.
entries.example: The new government policy offers grants for home insulation.

entries.definition: Paid for with money provided by a government.
entries.example: The government-funded project will restore the bridge.

entries.definition: Recognize and understand the most important words in a text or speech.
entries.example: Try to identify the keywords before answering the listening question.
entries.usage: Identify or pick out keywords is more usual than grasp keywords.

entries.definition: A school that awards advanced degrees, such as doctoral degrees; a postgraduate school.

entries.definition: Notices telling people that someone is graduating or that a graduation will take place.

entries.definition: The visible arrangement of fibres and markings in wood.

entries.definition: The arrangement of lines or fibres visible in a material such as wood.

entries.definition: People or things that are especially well liked.

entries.definition: The floor of a building closest to ground level.

entries.definition: Unwanted vegetation or other plant-origin waste, able to be composted.

entries.definition: A bus operated under the Greyhound transport brand.

entries.definition: A conversation in which several people exchange ideas about a topic.
entries.example: The lecture ended with a group discussion about climate policy.

entries.definition: An arrangement that allows someone to use a gym, usually for a fee.
entries.example: My gym membership includes fitness classes twice a week.

entries.definition: Female chickens or other female birds.

entries.definition: A strong wind.

entries.definition: Partly human in nature or ancestry, especially in a fictional description.

entries.definition: A short school holiday in the middle of the term, generally lasting a week.

entries.definition: Animals whose feet end in firm, hard hooves.

entries.definition: Buildings providing accommodation for students.

entries.definition: A device operated by hand to move water or another fluid.
entries.example: Villagers use a hand pump to draw water from the well.

entries.definition: Hands whose bones have been fractured.

entries.usage: Use broken hands as a noun phrase or his hands are broken as a complete clause.

entries.definition: To be able or permitted to use or enter something.

entries.definition: Insects that cause damage, spread disease or otherwise have unwanted effects.

entries.definition: Able to damage people's health or well-being.

entries.definition: To have a healthy heart and lungs capable of demanding physical activity.

entries.definition: To undergo a surgical procedure.
entries.example: She had an operation to repair her injured knee.

entries.definition: A section of an organization offering specialist advice to customers or users who have problems, especially with computer equipment or systems.

entries.definition: The main administrative centre for a company or organisation.

entries.definition: Alternative spelling of health care.

entries.definition: An examination to assess a person's general health.

I did lots of push-ups and pull-ups, and my only regret is that I stopped doing them as a young adult when I finally got to work out in health clubs instead of my basement or garage.

entries.definition: Individual contractions of the heart that pump blood.

entries.definition: a disease which affects the functions of the heart.

entries.definition: A device or mark that shows temperature or exposure to heat.
entries.example: The heat indicator changes colour when the pan becomes hot.

entries.definition: Hair from a horse, sometimes used to make brushes or other products.

entries.usage: Horsehair is normally written as one word.

entries.definition: The activity of riding a horse.

entries.definition: A beverage (a tisane) made by steeping herbs (sometimes also includes other plants, such as spices), other than tea leaves, in hot water.

entries.definition: A group of cattle kept or moving together.

entries.definition: A family that provides accommodation for a visiting person, often a student.

entries.definition: A senior or important position in a hierarchy.

entries.definition: Employees who have received extensive training.

entries.definition: Education beyond a level viewed as basic, such as any beyond universal government-funded secondary education.

entries.definition: Buildings with many storeys that rise high above the ground.

entries.definition: A camera that produces good images and is well made.

entries.definition: A set of hotel rooms marketed for newly married couples.

entries.definition: A museum displaying objects and information about the past.

entries.definition: Maps from the past or maps showing past geographical conditions.

entries.definition: A film intended to frighten viewers through suspense, danger, or disturbing events.

entries.definition: An organisation that helps people find or manage housing.

entries.definition: People; members of the human species.

entries.definition: The use of a substance as food or drink by people.

entries.definition: An identifying number assigned to a room.
entries.example: Write your room number on the breakfast order form.

entries.definition: A room containing a number of beds (and often some other furniture and/or utilities) for sleeping, often applied to student and backpacker accommodation of this kind.
entries.example: She will be much more likely to meet his wishes after a residence at the castle, than an imprisonment on short commons in her dormitory in Welbeck Street; for in one case she only learnt how much she could endure, in the other she will find how much she can enjoy.

entries.definition: A system whereby students, visiting a foreign country to study, board with a local family at an affordable price.
entries.example: Whether you’re crossing paths with shepherds in the mountains or staying with a family at a homestay, the warmth of the people will linger in your heart long after your trip ends.

entries.definition: Oneness, singularity, seen as a component of a whole number; a magnitude of one.
entries.example: Number, we define, to be, a certayne Mathematicall Sũme, of Vnits. [Note the worde, Vnit, to expresse the Greke Monas, & not Vnitie: as we haue all, commonly, till now, vsed.]

entries.definition: A row house or terraced house.
entries.example: Their townhouse has a small courtyard at the back.

entries.definition: A bedroom containing a bed for two people.
entries.example: The flat has a double bedroom and a smaller study.

entries.definition: A bedroom containing two separate beds.
entries.example: We booked a twin bedroom for two nights.

entries.definition: A bedroom intended for one occupant or containing one single bed.
entries.example: The flat has a single bedroom suitable for one student.
entries.usage: Single room may describe occupancy, while single bedroom can also contrast with double bedroom.

entries.definition: A room in a house where the washing machine and clothes dryer are located.
entries.example: The laundry room contains two washing machines and a dryer.

entries.definition: A corridor in a building that connects rooms.
entries.example: The hallway connects the kitchen to the bedrooms.

entries.definition: A room used for storing goods or equipment.
entries.example: Unused chairs are kept in the store room.
entries.usage: Storeroom is also commonly written as one word.

entries.definition: A building or room used to store goods or equipment.
entries.example: The tools are kept in the storehouse behind the workshop.
entries.usage: Storehouse is usually one word; storeroom may be intended for a room inside a building.

entries.definition: A small, usually uncultivated area adjoining or (now especially) within the precincts of a house or other building.
entries.example: 'Twas early June, the new grass was flourishing everywheres, the posies in the yard—peonies and such—in full bloom, the sun was shining, and the water of the bay was blue, with light green streaks where the shoal showed.

entries.definition: A machine that cools and controls the air in a room or building.
entries.example: The air-conditioner cooled the office during the heatwave.

entries.definition: Cooking appliances that use electricity to heat food.
entries.example: The accommodation has electric stoves in the shared kitchen.

entries.definition: Not furnished; having no furnishings.
entries.example: The unfurnished flat has no beds, chairs, or tables.

entries.definition: Supplied a room or building with furniture or equipment.
entries.example: The landlord furnished the flat with basic furniture.

entries.definition: A removable fabric cover for a pillow.
entries.example: She put a clean pillow case on the pillow.

entries.definition: To stretch out, open out (a material etc.) so that it more fully covers a given area of space.
entries.example: He spread his newspaper on the table.

entries.definition: Essential services supplied to homes and businesses, such as water and power.
entries.example: The rent excludes utilities such as electricity and water.
entries.usage: Plural of utility; the service sense is used here.

entries.definition: A temporary loss of consciousness.
entries.example: The patient experienced a brief blackout after standing up suddenly.

entries.definition: A short-haul minibus, typically privately owned, that shuttles passengers between set locations.
entries.example: A shuttle bus runs between the airport and the hotel.

entries.definition: A long car hired to carry passengers, especially between an airport and a hotel.
entries.example: The airport limousine collected us outside arrivals.

entries.definition: Chiefly in wide berth: a sufficient space in the water for a ship or other vessel to lie at anchor or manoeuvre without getting in the way of other vessels, or colliding into rocks or the shore.
entries.example: Tho' vve vvere again got near our harbour by three in the afternoon, yet it ſeemed to require a full hour or more, before vve could come to our former place of anchoring, or birth, as the captain called it.

entries.definition: A location where a stream is shallow and the bottom has good footing, making it possible to cross from one side to the other with no bridge, by walking, riding, or driving through the water; a crossing.
entries.example: He swam the Esk river where ford there was none.

entries.definition: The name of a luxury car marque founded by Rolls-Royce Limited.
entries.example: The museum displayed a classic Rolls-Royce automobile.
entries.usage: The conventional spelling is Rolls-Royce, with a hyphen; the source form RollsRoyce is corrupted.

entries.definition: A Mercedes-Benz vehicle.
entries.example: He parked his Benz beside the entrance.
entries.usage: Informal shortened name; selected the vehicle rather than a surname.

entries.definition: A manufacturer of motor vehicles (Bayerische Motoren-Werke (Bavarian Motor Works)).
entries.example: So BMW has conjured a tweener — a roomier hatchback on platform shoes, with standard all-wheel drive — to attract customers who crave the 3 Series’ performance but need more utility to close the deal.

entries.definition: A designated area, usually outdoors and divided into marked spaces, intended for the temporary parking of motor vehicles.
entries.example: Meronyms: parking space, parking spot, parking place

entries.definition: A designated place for parking vehicles.
entries.example: Leave your car in the marked parking area.

entries.definition: An outdoor area or a building where cars may be parked.
entries.example: It is important also that we improve car park security.

entries.definition: A device, located by a parking space, that collects payment in exchange for the right to park a vehicle for a specified time.
entries.example: The parking meter allows a maximum stay of two hours.

entries.definition: A pre-printed card, issued by several local authorities, that a resident (or his visitor) can display in his car when parking in a designated roadside place.
entries.example: Display the parking permit clearly on your windscreen.

entries.definition: A label placed on a vehicle to show permission to park.
entries.example: Display your parking sticker on the windscreen.

entries.definition: To pay money as a punishment for breaking a law or rule.
entries.example: You may have to pay a fine for parking here.

entries.definition: Remove a vehicle by towing it away, usually because it is illegally parked or obstructing traffic.
entries.example: The council may tow away cars left in the emergency lane.

entries.definition: To attach a locking device to a vehicle's wheel so it cannot move.
entries.example: Officials may clamp the wheel of a car parked without permission.

entries.definition: Transport owned or arranged for private use rather than public service.
entries.example: The conference venue is easier to reach by private transport.

entries.definition: A rapid transit rail transport system, or a train in such systems, generally underground and serving a metropolitan area.
entries.example: He is going to the stadium by metro.

entries.definition: Reserve or purchase a ticket.
entries.example: I need to book the ticket before the price increases.

entries.definition: To arrange in advance for something such as a table, seat, or room to be kept for you.
entries.example: We need to make a reservation for six people at the restaurant.

entries.definition: To verify that a booking or reservation is still wanted and valid.
entries.example: Please confirm your reservation by email.

entries.definition: Cancel a reservation made in your name.
entries.example: You can cancel your reservation online up to 24 hours before arrival.
entries.usage: One's is usually replaced by a possessive determiner such as your.

entries.definition: The arrangement in which people are served or accepted in the order they arrive.
entries.example: Places are allocated on a first come, first served basis.
entries.usage: First come, first served is the conventional form; first come first serve is nonstandard.

entries.definition: To arrange in advance to use a room.
entries.example: I would like to book a room for two nights.

entries.definition: To reserve a table at a restaurant.
entries.example: We booked a table for four at seven o'clock.

entries.definition: A ticket sold at a reduced price under conditions such as advance purchase or restricted travel times.
entries.example: We chose a saver ticket to keep the train fare low.

entries.definition: A travel ticket without a fixed travel date or with flexible arrangements.
entries.example: Ask whether the open ticket requires advance seat booking.
entries.usage: Conditions depend on the transport provider; an open ticket does not necessarily guarantee a seat.

entries.definition: A ticket allowing travel to a destination and back.
entries.example: A round-trip ticket includes the return journey.

entries.definition: A ticket granting permission to travel to a place and return.
entries.example: A return ticket covers both the journey there and the journey back.

entries.definition: Belonging to the best or top group in a system of classification.
entries.example: That was a first class restaurant.

entries.definition: A break between stages of a journey.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: stopover, stayover (both sometimes synonymous)

entries.definition: A short interruption in a journey or the place visited during such an interruption.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: stayover, layover, lie-over (all sometimes synonymous)

entries.definition: A flight taken after another flight, with a change between them.
entries.example: Our connecting flight leaves from terminal two.
entries.usage: Connecting flight is conventionally written as two words.

entries.definition: To remove.
entries.example: He took off his shoes.

entries.definition: A charge added to the price of an air ticket for using an airport.
entries.example: The airline displayed the airport tax separately from the base fare.

entries.definition: A shop selling eligible goods without certain local taxes or duties.
entries.example: She bought perfume at the airport duty-free shop.

entries.definition: An additional or excessive fee charged beyond the basic price.
entries.example: The airline applied an excess charge for the heavy suitcase.

entries.definition: A seat that has not been assigned or occupied.
entries.example: Ask the attendant whether a vacant seat is available.

entries.definition: An addition of extra charge on the agreed, stated, or baseline price. Sometimes portrayed by a buyer as excessive and rapacious; usually portrayed by a seller as justified and necessary.
entries.example: Our airline tickets cost twenty dollars more than we expected because we had to pay a fuel surcharge.

entries.definition: Having no available places or rooms because all have been reserved.
entries.example: The hotel is fully booked for the festival weekend.
entries.usage: Fulling-booked is a spelling error; use fully booked.

entries.definition: The way seats are positioned or organised.
entries.example: The theatre changed its seat arrangement for the lecture.

entries.definition: The process or position of allocating a particular seat to a passenger.
entries.example: Our seat assignment placed us together in row twelve.

entries.definition: The time when something (e.g., a ship, vehicle, aircraft, cargo, person, or emergency service) is expected to arrive at a certain place.
entries.example: The pilot announced the estimated time of arrival.

entries.definition: The time when something (e.g., a ship, vehicle, aircraft, cargo, person, or emergency service) is expected to depart a certain place.
entries.example: The screen shows the estimated time of departure for each flight.

entries.definition: To reserve a particular room in advance.
entries.example: Please book the room with the sea view for our anniversary.

entries.definition: Units of the currency used in Canada.
entries.example: The hotel charged two hundred Canadian dollars per night.

entries.definition: A unit of weight in various measurement systems.
entries.example: B-2 bombers are the only plane capable of carrying the Massive Ordinance Penetrator, which experts have highlighted as the only type of bomb potentially capable of destroying Iran’s underground Fordow nuclear facility. Each B-2 bomber is able to carry two of these “bunker buster” bombs, which weigh an impressive 30,000 pounds each.

entries.definition: The currency unit of the European Monetary Union. Symbol: €
entries.example: The ticket price is twenty euros.

entries.definition: The currency used in Japan.
entries.example: The museum ticket costs 1,200 Japanese yen.
entries.usage: Yen is usually lowercase when naming the currency; Japanese Yen may be a label or title.

entries.definition: A credit card issued by the credit card company Mastercard.
entries.example: And when they got to the funeral, well, Roger and Buddy were running around to various banks trying to raise ten thousand dollars from their Mastercards, and Jamie thought he might have to help them out, and nobody ever knew that Jamie was very poor, and Jamie always put up a good front, and Jamie would have helped them bury their mother too.

entries.definition: A brand and company known for charge cards and financial services.
entries.example: The hotel accepts American Express for payment.

entries.definition: Regions with many hills.
entries.example: Cycling is more demanding in hilly areas.

entries.definition: An area of land in a natural, uncultivated state; wilderness, open forest.
entries.example: The walking trail passes through native bushland.

entries.definition: Dense forests in tropical regions with high rainfall.
entries.example: Tropical rainforests support many kinds of plants and animals.

entries.definition: Areas of sand, pebbles or other material beside the sea or a lake.
entries.example: The island has several sandy beaches.

entries.definition: An area beside the sea or ocean.
entries.example: The coastal area attracts visitors in summer.

entries.definition: A natural spring producing water whose temperature is greater than about 20 °C (68 °F).
entries.example: Steam rose from the hot spring on the cold morning.

entries.definition: A guided visit that focuses attention on selected highlights.
entries.example: The museum's spotlight tour focuses on its newest paintings.
entries.usage: The term may be a venue-specific tour name; no particular program is identified.

entries.definition: The state or trait of having four drive wheels.
entries.example: The vehicle's four-wheel drive helps it move over muddy ground.

entries.definition: A leisure journey by boat along a river.
entries.example: The river cruise passes the old castle before returning to the quay.

entries.definition: To travel by getting lifts in passing vehicles.
entries.example: They decided to hitch-hike to the next town.

entries.definition: A traveler whose luggage consists of a backpack; especially, such a traveler who uses hostels, public transport, and other inexpensive services.
entries.example: Among the ah bengs and ah lians, the mats and the minahs, the young expats and the backpackers, he stood out like a dozen guys on a male-only dance floor singing Dancing Queen (I'll never forgive Blur for ruining my 21st birthday).

entries.definition: Jumping into water or moving below its surface.
entries.example: The children were diving into the pool from the low platform.

entries.definition: Underwater swimming using scuba equipment.
entries.example: She took a scuba diving course before exploring the reef.

entries.definition: Riding waves on a surfboard.
entries.example: She is surfing off the coast this morning.

entries.definition: The sport of flying in a hang glider.
entries.example: He tried hang gliding during his holiday in the mountains.
entries.usage: Common learner sense selected in place of a morphological source default.

entries.definition: A water sport consisting of two teams of swimmers who have to throw the ball into the opponent's goal.
entries.example: The swimmers passed the ball quickly during the water polo match.

entries.definition: Any of the suborder Serpentes of legless reptiles with long, thin bodies and fork-shaped tongues.
entries.example: The man writhed like a trampled snake, and a red foam bubbled from his lips.

entries.definition: A pointed portion of an insect or arachnid used for attack.
entries.example: The bee left its stinger in his skin.

entries.definition: Any predatory fish of the superorder Selachimorpha, with a cartilaginous skeleton and 5 to 7 gill slits on each side of its head.
entries.example: The straunge fishe is in length xvij. foote and iij. foote broad, and in compas about the bodie vj. foote; and is round snowted, short headdid, hauing iij. rankes of teeth on either iawe, …. Also it hath v. gills of eache side of the head, shoing white. Ther is no proper name for it that I know, but that sertayne men of Captayne Haukinses doth call it a sharke.

entries.definition: An almost transparent aquatic animal; any one of the acalephs, especially one of the larger species, having a jellylike appearance.
entries.example: A recent study focused on the enzymatic and cytotoxic functions of jellyfish metalloproteases and identified diverse proteolytic effects including gelatinolytic, caseinolytic, and fibrinolytic activities.

entries.definition: Some plants selected or referred to without specifying all of them.
entries.example: Certain plants grow only in acidic soil.

entries.definition: A towel for use at the beach, typically larger than a normal household towel so that a person can use it to lie on the sand.
entries.example: We spread a beach towel on the sand.

entries.definition: Close-fitting garments worn over the feet.
entries.example: Pack an extra pair of socks for the hike.

entries.definition: A topical substance formulated to protect the skin from the harmful effects of ultraviolet radiation by absorbing, reflecting or scattering ultraviolet rays.
entries.example:
Jill had Mark apply sunscreen to her back.
"Bet these river guides get a lot of skin cancer", he said. He had a slappy, unpleasant way of doing it, and she struggled to keep her balance.

entries.definition: trousers as opposed to shorts
entries.example: Wear long trousers for the walk through the rough grass.

entries.definition: A bank employee who receives and pays out money.
entries.example: The teller counted the notes before handing them to me.
entries.usage: Common learner sense selected in place of an unsuitable or less useful source default.

entries.definition: Withdraw cash from a bank account.
entries.example: I need to draw money before the shop closes.
entries.usage: Withdraw cash or take out money is more usual in general banking contexts.

entries.definition: To take money out of a bank account.
entries.example: You can withdraw money from the cash machine outside the library.

entries.definition: To give banknotes or coins in denominations of five.
entries.example: Could you give me the money in fives, please?
entries.usage: The wording is conversational; give me the money in five-pound notes is more explicit.

entries.definition: Hand over money in banknotes of ten units each.
entries.example: Please give the cashier the money in tens if you have exact notes.
entries.usage: The currency and whether coins or notes are intended are not specified.

entries.definition: A secret personal identification number used to authorize access or transactions.
entries.example: Never share your PIN number with another person.
entries.usage: PIN already includes number, so PIN number is redundant but common.

entries.definition: A bank account maintained by a financial institution in which a customer can deposit and withdraw money.
entries.example: Interest is paid monthly on the deposit account.

entries.definition: To set up a bank account intended for students.
entries.example: Bring proof of enrolment when you open a student account.

entries.term: check the present balance in your account
entries.definition: To look at how much money is currently in your bank account.
entries.example: You can check the present balance in your account online.
entries.usage: Current account balance is the more concise expression.

entries.definition: Request a loan for personal use.
entries.example: She plans to apply for a personal loan to replace the boiler.

entries.definition: To exchange money in pounds for money in dollars.
entries.example: I need to change pounds into dollars before my trip.

entries.definition: The exchange value or price that applies now.
entries.example: The current rate for euros is displayed on the screen.

entries.definition: Alternative form of labor market.
entries.example: She gets jobs that last only a few months, in the flexible labour market beloved of politicians, but which leaves her struggling to pay the bills.

entries.definition: An employment agency, a job centre.
entries.example: Isn't it taking candour unwisely far to anticipate clueless responses from some station staff and excuse them on the grounds that "some of the chaps you see in uniform have just arrived from the labour exchange"?

entries.definition: An office that helps people find jobs and employers find workers.
entries.example: The employment exchange helped him find temporary work.

entries.definition: Employment available only during a particular season.
entries.example: Students often take seasonal work during the summer holidays.

entries.definition: Work paid according to the number of items or units produced rather than time spent.
entries.example: The factory pays its workers for piecework according to the number of items they finish.

entries.definition: Work for which a certain rate is paid per unit of time.
entries.example: The workshop pays employees for timework at an hourly rate.

entries.definition: A legal authorization which allows a person to take employment in a country other than the one in which they hold citizenship.
entries.example: United hope to confirm Di María’s work permit in time for Saturday’s match at Burnley. If granted – and that should be a formality with his status as an Argentina international – he should be selected for the match-day squad at Turf Moor and could make a full debut.

entries.definition: To formally ask to be considered for employment.
entries.example: She decided to apply for a job at the museum.

entries.definition: Any ailment that occurs as a result of work or occupational activity.
entries.example: Prolonged exposure to dust can cause an occupational disease.

entries.definition: Advice that helps someone choose a career or occupation.
entries.example: The college offers vocational guidance to final-year students.

entries.definition: Education that prepares someone for a specific trade or occupation.
entries.example: Vocational training gave him the skills to become an electrician.

entries.definition: Someone who is still in the process of being formally trained in a workplace.
entries.example: The trainee practised serving customers under the supervisor's guidance.

entries.definition: An organization whose members belong to the same trade and that acts collectively to address common issues.
entries.example: When the first wave of postwar immigrants arrived in Britain in the 1950s and ’60s, it was a period of rising wages, full employment, an expanding welfare state and strong trade unions. Today, Britain’s manufacturing base has all but disappeared, working-class communities have disintegrated, unions have been neutered and the welfare state has begun to crumble.

entries.definition: To give money or other compensation to in exchange for goods or services.
entries.example: pay cash or pay in cash, pay by credit/debit card

entries.definition: Superior in quality; higher in price or value.
entries.example: The café charges more for its premium coffee.

entries.definition: Something extra that is good; an added benefit.
entries.example: Free breakfast was an unexpected bonus at the hotel.

entries.definition: Money received in addition to ordinary wages.
entries.example: Staff receive extra pay for working on public holidays.

entries.definition: The day of the week or month, or the specific day, on which an employee's wages or salary is paid.
entries.example: She pays her rent on payday.

entries.definition: A document showing an employee's earnings and deductions for a pay period.
entries.example: Check your pay slip to confirm the tax deduction.

entries.definition: An employee (such as a secretary) who works in reception (receiving visitors and/or calls) for a person or business, especially an office.
entries.example:
"At the moment, I think I'm working for the Central Intelligence Corporation, the Mafia, and Mr. Lee's Greater Hong Kong."
 "I see," the receptionist, making a note.

entries.definition: The act of inputting data into a computer, such as by typing out handwriting, capturing data from scanned documents, taking responses from telephone interviews, etc.
entries.example: The job involves data entry from paper application forms.

entries.definition: A person whose job involves entering information by pressing keys, historically on punched cards or a keyboard.
entries.example: The key puncher entered the figures into the old accounting system.
entries.usage: This is an old occupational term; data-entry clerk is more current.

entries.definition: Someone skilled in the writing of shorthand or the use of a stenotype machine, especially for the purpose of rapid transcription of speech. One employed in such a role: a professional transcriptionist who employs shorthand.
entries.example: The stenographer recorded the witness's testimony during the hearing.

entries.definition: A person who operates a telephone switchboard.
entries.example: Since the outbreak of war women have been recruited for many grades of railway work. The number of women clerks has been increased greatly, and women are performing invaluable work as porters, motor drivers, carriage cleaners, and telephone operators, as well as in a variety of other capacities.

entries.definition: A person skilled in shorthand and typing.
entries.example: The shorthand typist took notes during the hearing.

entries.definition: A male who is employed to deliver things to people.
entries.example: The delivery boy carried the parcel to the front door.

entries.definition: Alternative form of kitchenhand.
entries.example: At 16, he started work as a kitchen hand in a nearby restaurant.

entries.definition: Someone who delivers mail to, and/or collects mail from, residential or commercial addresses, or from public mailboxes.
entries.example: "What I'm thinking," she said, "is that I'll become a mailman. They're hiring women mailmen now, you know. […]"

entries.definition: A boy who delivers newspapers to customers.
entries.example: The newspaper boy left the morning paper by our door.
entries.usage: Newspaper delivery worker is more inclusive and often more current.

entries.definition: A man who delivers milk to households and sometimes businesses early in the morning.
entries.example: Our milkman is a jovial character, but not one given to yodelling at the customers on his round. Only the resounding "clonk" of bottles advises us that a couple of pints have been left on the doorstep.

entries.definition: A person who sells flowers.
entries.example: The florist arranged the roses in a glass vase.

entries.definition: A person who bakes and sells bread, cakes and similar items.
entries.example: But through the oligopoly, charcoal fuel proliferated throughout London's trades and industries. By the 1200s, brewers and bakers, tilemakers, glassblowers, pottery producers, and a range of other craftsmen all became hour-to-hour consumers of charcoal.

entries.definition: A person who shoplifts, one who steals from shops.
entries.example: Shoplifters will be prosecuted.

entries.definition: To monitor the supply of goods held for sale or use.
entries.example: Keep an eye on stock so we can reorder before the shelves are empty.

entries.definition: A doctor who specialises in diseases of the eyes.
entries.example: The oculist examined my vision and prescribed new glasses.
entries.usage: Oculist is an old-fashioned term; ophthalmologist or eye doctor is more current. Doctor is redundant in the original phrase.

entries.definition: Visit a doctor for medical advice or treatment.
entries.example: You should see a doctor if the fever continues.

entries.definition: To ask for a doctor to come and provide medical help.
entries.example: The hotel manager had to send for a doctor when a guest became ill.

entries.definition: To be ill with a common viral infection causing a blocked or runny nose.
entries.example: I have a cold, so I will stay home today.

entries.definition: To contract a cold.
entries.example: You can catch a cold after exposure to the viruses that cause it.

entries.definition: Experience pain or irritation in the throat.
entries.example: I have a sore throat, so I am drinking warm tea.

entries.definition: To have liquid mucus flowing from the nose.
entries.example: I have a runny nose and keep needing tissues.

entries.definition: To vomit.
entries.example: The dog vomited up the food it had just eaten.

entries.definition: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see throw, up.
entries.example:
Away to the window I flew like a flash,
Tore open the shutters and threw up the sash.

entries.definition: To feel slightly cold.
entries.example: I began to feel chilly when the sun went down.

entries.definition: An illness or other problem affecting the liver.
entries.example: The scan showed that her liver trouble needed specialist care.
entries.usage: Liver problem or liver disease may be more precise.

entries.definition: Inflammation of the lungs caused by viruses, bacteria or other infectious microorganisms.
entries.example: He had always been remarkably immune from such little ailments, and had only once in his life been ill, of a vicious pneumonia long ago at school.

entries.definition: Consisting of two or more threads, strands or the like intertwined; formed by twisting or twining.
entries.example: The twisted rope is made from several strands woven together.

entries.definition: A long-term respiratory condition, in which the airways may unexpectedly and suddenly narrow, often in response to an allergen, cold air, exercise, or emotional stress. Symptoms include wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, and coughing.
entries.example: ...but rheumatism is a vulgar complaint, and would sink even a ducal coronet—the very lowest people have it. I question if there is a workhouse in Great Britain exempt from it. Neither is there one free from asthma, and yet all the world knows a royal duke suffers from it as much as a coalheaver might do;...

entries.definition: Of or pertaining to diabetes, especially diabetes mellitus.
entries.example: diabetic complications

entries.definition: A painful contraction of a muscle which cannot be controlled; (sometimes) a similar pain even without noticeable contraction.
entries.example: He retired hurt at 31 due to a leg cramp.

entries.definition: A gastrointestinal disorder characterized by frequent and very soft or watery bowel movements.
entries.example: Diarrhea can cause dehydration if too much fluid is lost.

entries.definition: To have a nose blocked by congestion.
entries.example: I have a stuffed nose and cannot breathe comfortably through it.
entries.usage: Have a stuffy nose or have a blocked nose is more conventional.

entries.definition: An allergy to the pollen of grass or other plants that causes symptoms similar to those of a cold; pollinosis.
entries.example: Hay fever makes her sneeze when pollen levels are high.

entries.definition: Drops of liquid medicine placed in the eyes.
entries.example: The pharmacist showed her how to apply the prescribed eyedrops.

entries.definition: A medicine or treatment intended to relieve a cold.
entries.example: The pharmacist recommended a cold remedy for my sore throat.
entries.usage: Cold remedy is the conventional phrase; cold cure is understandable but less common.

entries.definition: Medicine intended to make a person sweat.
entries.example: The label described the product as a sweating medicine.
entries.usage: This is not a standard modern medical category; the intended treatment and evidence are uncertain.

entries.definition: Synonym of antipyretic (“a fever-reducing medication”).
entries.example: ...therein it differs not from the mode of operation, which we observe in the famous peruvian febrifuge.

entries.definition: A device used for injecting or drawing fluids through a membrane.
entries.example: In Kelly’s case, once the baby was admitted to the hospital, she began to use formula, fed through a syringe—she was told to avoid bottles because the baby would reject the breast.

entries.definition: A medical instrument used for listening to sounds produced within the body.
entries.example: The doctor listened to my chest through a stethoscope.

entries.definition: An injection given to help prevent an illness, often a vaccine.
entries.example: The clinic offers a preventive injection against influenza.
entries.usage: Vaccination is usually more precise when a vaccine is meant.

entries.definition: A thin fabric with a loose, open weave.
entries.example: The nurse covered the wound with sterile gauze.

entries.definition: The details of the history of some case (often medical).
entries.example: After consulting her case history, the doctor prescribed methotrexate.

entries.definition: To measure the pressure of blood flowing through the arteries.
