entries.definition: A space for using on-site computers, usually as part of an institution such as a school or library.
entries.example: The computer lab is open for students who need to print assignments.

entries.definition: A large, powerful computer able to manage very many simultaneous tasks and communicate with very many connected terminals; used by large, complex organizations (such as banks and supermarkets) where continuously sustained operation is vital.
entries.example: The bank's mainframe processes thousands of transactions each minute.

entries.definition: A modem that provides data communication via radio frequency channels over any of a variety of cable types to establish a cable internet connection.
entries.example: Restart the cable modem if the internet connection drops.

entries.definition: One of a series of parallel magnetic recording disks in a drive unit, used for the recording and retrieval of digital information; used especially in personal computers.
entries.example: Back up your files before replacing the hard disk.

entries.definition: A removable disk used for storing digital data, measuring between 2 and 8 inches diagonally and storing between 80 KB and 240 MB.
entries.example: A hacker starts with nothing but a dream and a floppy disk and presently finds himself in a business that's doubled and trebled.

entries.definition: The ability of the brain to record information or impressions with the facility of recalling them later, usually at will.
entries.example: Memory is a facility common to all animals.

entries.definition: One who makes prints.
entries.example: Old Japanese colour-prints are printed on a sheet of mulberry-bark paper, and are the product of three different craftsmen: the artist who drew the original design, the block-maker or engraver who transferred the design to the wood, and the printer.

entries.definition: One who scans.
entries.example: It is, perhaps, too much to assume that an elderly Melville read James, but he was an eager scanner of magazines and did read fiction in his later years.

entries.definition: A machine which reproduces documents by photographing the original over a glass plate and printing duplicates.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: (all broadly synonymous) xerox machine, xerographer, xerox, photostat, laser copier

entries.definition: A machine that copies graphical material; a duplicator.
entries.example: The copier has run out of paper.

entries.definition: A computer printer that uses a laser beam to produce an image on a rotating drum before transferring it to the paper.
entries.example: The laser printer produced the handouts in a few minutes.

entries.definition: A printer that forms characters and images using small pins that strike an inked ribbon.
entries.example: The old dot-matrix printer is still used for multi-part invoices.

entries.definition: A printer that applies coloured ink to paper.
entries.example: The office replaced its old colour inkjet printer.
entries.usage: The original has spelling errors: color inject printer is most reasonably colour inkjet printer. The exact device is inferred from the wording.

entries.definition: Applications that perform tasks on a computer or other device.
entries.example: The update fixed security problems in several software programs.

entries.definition: Legal rules governing rights over the copying and use of creative works.
entries.example: Copyright laws may limit how much of a textbook you can photocopy.

entries.definition: The act of observing, and the fact of being observed (see observance)
entries.example: But Miss Thorn relieved the situation by laughing aloud,[…]. We began to tell her about Mohair and the cotillon, and of our point of observation from the Florentine galleried porch, and she insisted she would join us there.

entries.definition: Questions requiring answers of only a few words or a short sentence.
entries.example: The test contains ten short-answer questions.
entries.usage: Short-answer is conventionally hyphenated before a noun.

entries.definition: A question format in which one answer is chosen from several alternatives.
entries.example: The test includes a multiple-choice section.
entries.usage: Usually hyphenated before a noun: multiple-choice question.

entries.definition: An exercise or task in which missing words or information are supplied.
entries.example: The listening test includes gap filling in a short summary.

entries.definition: Based on suitable data and statistical methods that justify the conclusions.
entries.example: A representative sample helps produce statistically valid survey results.

entries.definition: Something known or assumed as fact, and is made the basis of reasoning or inference which an intellectual system of any sort (such as knowledge or theoretical framework) is constructed.
entries.example: a datum of experience

entries.definition: The act of investigating; the process of inquiring into or following up; research, especially patient or thorough inquiry or examination
entries.example: The investigation into the crime has led to various leads as well as plenty of dead ends.

entries.definition: Of a measurements and data types: based on some quantity or number rather than on some quality.
entries.example: Near-synonyms: nonqualitative, unqualitative

entries.definition: Examine information systematically to discover patterns or draw conclusions.
entries.example: Researchers analyze data from thousands of survey responses.
entries.usage: Analyze is American spelling; analyse is British spelling.

entries.definition: An act of interpreting or explaining something unclear; a translation; a version.
entries.example: The interpretation of a dream, or of an enigma

entries.definition: A person's own view, especially one not expressed publicly.
entries.example: My private opinion differs from the statement issued by the committee.

entries.definition: The opinion of the public, the popular view.
entries.example: Her stock is high in terms of public opinion because of her aid work.

entries.definition: A meal of fish fried in batter and served with chips (fried potato pieces), popular throughout the Anglosphere, especially in coastal regions.
entries.example: Let's go to Sophie's by the sea; they have the most delicious fish and chips.

entries.definition: Having a slippery surface; having a surface covered with grease.
entries.example: a greasy mineral

entries.definition: A rule controlling where, when or how vehicles may be parked.
entries.example: The new parking regulation bans overnight parking on this street.

entries.definition: A building containing classrooms, laboratories, or offices for teaching.
entries.example: The new teaching building has accessible entrances on every floor.

entries.definition: An office that manages an organization's routine operations and records.
entries.example: Submit the completed form to the administration office.
entries.usage: Administration office or administrative office is more conventional than administrating office.

entries.definition: An office that handles administrative tasks.
entries.example: Submit the completed form to the admin office.
entries.usage: Administrative office is more formal; admin office is common in speech.

entries.definition: A long-standing group of people sharing cultural aspects such as language, dress, norms of behavior and artistic forms.
entries.example: This society has been known for centuries for its colorful clothing and tight-knit family structure.

entries.definition: For each person or animal in a group.
entries.example: The meal costs ten pounds a head.
entries.usage: A head is an informal counting unit for people or animals.

entries.definition: The amount of something contained in one jar.
entries.example: I bought a jar of honey at the market.

entries.definition: A large quantity or group of something.
entries.example: A mass of paperwork arrived before the deadline.

entries.definition: A combined amount obtained by adding all parts together.
entries.example: A total of 120 applications were received.

entries.definition: An unnecessary or unproductive use of something.
entries.example: Waiting for the wrong bus was a waste of time.

entries.definition: Many different kinds or varieties of something.
entries.example: The market sells all sorts of handmade soap.

entries.definition: Indicates that a list continues in a similar manner.
entries.example: Don't forget to pack weather items appropriate for the climate: sunscreen, rain gear, and so forth.

entries.definition: Begin or result from a particular cause.
entries.example: Many disputes arise from misunderstandings.

entries.definition: Used to relate to all the parts of something: altogether, on the whole
entries.example: The sets are being sold as a whole, which affects the trade as a whole.

entries.definition: Provided that, if, assuming (depending upon some condition or requirement).
entries.example: I don't mind if he stays there, as long as he cleans up after himself when he's done.

entries.definition: In a single, continuous period of time.
entries.example: He manages to abstain from smoking for weeks at a time, but then gives in and starts again.

entries.definition: A large amount of something.
entries.example: The repairs required a great deal of patience.
entries.usage: Normally followed by an uncountable noun.

entries.definition: A large number or group of people or things.
entries.example: A host of volunteers helped clean the beach.

entries.definition: A large amount or number of something.
entries.example: They brought a load of equipment to the campsite.
entries.usage: A load of is informal and can refer to people, things, or work.

entries.definition: Several different kinds or examples of something.
entries.example: The library offers a range of online resources.

entries.definition: A group of things that belong together or are used together.
entries.example: The kit contains a set of tools for basic repairs.

entries.definition: Set a goal of reaching or achieving something.
entries.example: We aim for a completion date in early June.

entries.definition: In addition to; coupled with.
entries.example: She fired all the journalists in the company, along with some of the administration workers.

entries.definition: Except for; besides.
entries.example: At Esher we were getting out into bright sunshine, and apart from another foggy patch between Farnborough and Winchfield, we had a clear run from then on.

entries.definition: Actually, in fact.
entries.example: The house of Ruthven was a small but ultra-modern limestone affair, between Madison and Fifth; a pocket-edition of the larger mansions of their friends, but with less excuse for the overelaboration since the dimensions were only twenty by a hundred. As a matter of fact its narrow ornate façade presented not a single quiet space the eyes might rest on[…]."

entries.definition: To the degree or extent that.
entries.example: as far as the eye can see

entries.definition: As is usually the case.
entries.example: “A tight little craft,” was Austin’s invariable comment on the matron;[…]. ¶ Near her wandered her husband, orientally bland, invariably affable, and from time to time squinting sideways, as usual, in the ever-renewed expectation that he might catch a glimpse of his stiff, retroussé moustache.

entries.definition: At an unspecified point in a process or period.
entries.example: At some stage, we will need to replace the old computers.

entries.definition: At this moment; right now.
entries.example: I'm really off horror movies at the moment.

entries.definition: At the point or phase currently being discussed.
entries.example: At this stage, we do not know the final cost.

entries.definition: Have someone or something with you or present alongside you.
entries.example: The certificate must be accompanied by a copy of your passport.

entries.definition: To be joined or fastened to something.
entries.example: The label is attached to the outside of the box.
entries.usage: The phrase can also describe emotional affection; the physical sense is used here.

entries.definition: To be changed from one form, state or use into another.
entries.example: The old warehouse was converted into apartments.

entries.definition: Have recognition or praise assigned to you as the source of something.
entries.example: The discovery is credited to a team of university researchers.

entries.definition: To know something through experience or previous contact.
entries.example: You should be familiar with the emergency procedures before using the lab.

entries.definition: To consist of particular parts or members.
entries.example: The committee is made up of representatives from six departments.

entries.definition: Be hit or affected suddenly by something.
entries.example: The village was struck by a severe storm.
entries.usage: Can also mean be impressed or surprised, depending on the object.

entries.definition: To be better in quality, ability, or performance than something else.
entries.example: This material is superior to the cheaper alternative in durability.

entries.definition: To be suddenly surprised or shocked.
entries.example: I was taken aback by the unexpected price increase.

entries.definition: Be someone's responsibility, decision, or choice.
entries.example: It is up to you whether we leave now or later.

entries.definition: To hold (something) in the memory; to remember; also, to be mindful of or pay attention to (something); to consider; to note.
entries.example: Bear in mind that I’m not as young as I was, so I can’t walk as fast as you.

entries.definition: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see blow, up.
entries.example: See if you can blow the bubbles up the staircase.

entries.definition: to purchase the entire stock or extent of something
entries.example: […] the present Earl had no colour or pretence of right to the estate; and yet the appellants had thought fit to buy him out, […]

entries.definition: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see come, across.
entries.example: He came across the street towards me.

entries.definition: To provide what a person or group needs.
entries.example: The cafeteria caters for students with different dietary requirements.

entries.definition: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see chop, down.
entries.example: chop down a tree

entries.definition: To reach by moving down or reducing.
entries.example: Wait for the temperature to come down to a reasonable level before touching the lid.

entries.definition: To emerge or become known, especially unexpectedly.
entries.example: Unless anything comes up, I'll be there every day this week.

entries.definition: When considered in relation to something else to identify similarities or differences.
entries.example: The new bus route is faster compared with the old one.

entries.definition: To make up for a loss, disadvantage or cost.
entries.example: The grant helps compensate for the reduced ticket income.

entries.definition: To be composed or made up of something.
entries.example: The body consists of cells.

entries.definition: To expel from the lungs, throat, stomach, etc. by coughing.
entries.example: He was coughing up blood.

entries.definition: Need or be determined by someone or something else.
entries.example: The final cost will depend on the materials we choose.

entries.definition: To study a course leading to a university degree.
entries.example: She wants to do a degree in environmental science.
entries.usage: Common in British English; study for a degree is another option.

entries.definition: To deliver or give a speech.
entries.example: She will give the speech at the closing ceremony.
entries.usage: Do the speech is nonstandard in this meaning; give or make a speech is conventional.

entries.definition: Be willing to do something without being annoyed or opposed.
entries.example: I do not mind waiting another ten minutes.
entries.usage: Usually followed by a gerund; expand don't in formal writing.

entries.definition: To compose (a document), especially following a standard form; prepare a plan.
entries.example: I asked my lawyer to draw up a new will.

entries.definition: In a state or condition marked by a level of risk or vulnerability.
entries.example: to put at risk

entries.definition: At stated rates of movement or operation.
entries.example: These trains travel at speeds of up to two hundred kilometres an hour.

entries.definition: At the beginning.
entries.example: At the outset, we agreed on the project's main goals.

entries.definition: Having something as a foundation, source, or reason.
entries.example: The film is based on a true story.

entries.definition: To feel fear of someone or something.
entries.example: Many children are afraid of thunder.

entries.definition: Feel uncertain or unable to understand something.
entries.example: I am confused about which form to submit.

entries.definition: To be combined or linked with something.
entries.example: Heavy rain was coupled with strong winds during the storm.

entries.definition: To be expected or required to do something.
entries.example: All applicants are expected to submit two references.

entries.definition: Feel afraid of doing something.
entries.example: She is frightened about driving on icy roads.
entries.usage: Frightened of doing is more idiomatic; frightened about can refer to worry concerning an event.

entries.definition: To have something else put in one's place.
entries.example: The broken chairs will be replaced with new ones.

entries.definition: To be exposed to or affected by something, often unpleasant.
entries.example: The material was subjected to high temperatures during testing.

entries.definition: Be expected or required to do something.
entries.example: All visitors are supposed to sign in at reception.

entries.definition: To be responsible for a problem or bad outcome.
entries.example: Poor maintenance was to blame for the equipment failure.

entries.definition: To be accustomed to something.
entries.example: I am used to working in a busy office.
entries.usage: Follow be used to with a noun or -ing form, not a bare verb.

entries.definition: Be owned by, or be a member of, a particular person or group.
entries.example: These keys belong to the caretaker.

entries.definition: To do something in a new way that departs from established patterns.
entries.example: The architect wanted to break the mould by designing an unusual circular house.
entries.usage: British spelling of break the mold.

entries.definition: By using (an object or an approach).
entries.example: "By means of the Golden Cap I shall command the Winged Monkeys to carry you to the gates of the Emerald City," said Glinda, "for it would be a shame to deprive the people of so wonderful a ruler."

entries.definition: To hold while moving it out.
entries.example: We’ll have to carry the piano out of the shop.

entries.definition: To follow up, so as to ensure completion.
entries.example: Could you chase up last month's invoices?

entries.definition: To accompany.
entries.example: I'd like you to come along with me to the opera.

entries.definition: To manage to produce, deliver, or present (something) by inventing, creating, thinking of, or obtaining it.
entries.example: How can you come up with such brilliant ideas?

entries.definition: To come to terms with; to overcome any difficulties presented by.
entries.example: She finds her mental illness very difficult to cope with.

entries.definition: To handle verbally or in some form of artistic expression; to address or discuss as a subject.
entries.example: This book deals with incest.

entries.definition: To eliminate; to dispose of.
entries.example: I wish he would dispense with the pleasantries and get to the point.

entries.definition: To spend time painting pictures or surfaces.
entries.example: We do some painting in the art room on Friday afternoons.
entries.usage: Do some painting or paint is usually more natural.

entries.definition: To make journeys, usually for a particular purpose.
entries.example: The engineer does regular trips to inspect remote sites.
entries.usage: Make trips or take trips is more natural than do trips.

entries.definition: To set a boundary, rule, or limit, especially on what one will tolerate.
entries.example: I don't mind if they have some fun, but I draw the line at anything that might harm others.

entries.definition: To leave (school, a race, etc.) prematurely and voluntarily.
entries.example: Nothing went well in high school, so he dropped out.

entries.definition: Caused by; resulting from; because of.
entries.example: Rising unemployment due to the economic downturn is spreading.

entries.definition: Used to present two alternatives, with one or the other applying.
entries.example: You can either call me or send an email.
entries.usage: The conventional construction is either ... or ...; the source omits the punctuation marks.

entries.definition: To register as a participant in a course.
entries.example: You can enrol on the evening course through the college website.
entries.usage: Enrol is British spelling; enroll is American spelling. Enrol in is also used.

entries.definition: By a much greater amount or degree.
entries.example: This model is far more efficient than the old one.

entries.definition: To fill; to replace material that is absent or has been removed.
entries.example: After you're done laying the pipe, fill in the trench.

entries.definition: Shoot a gun by causing it to fire.
entries.example: The officer warned everyone before he fired the gun.
entries.usage: Fire a gun is grammatical; fired the gun is used here to fit the past context.

entries.definition: Because of; out of consideration for; in the interest of.
entries.example: Release this man, for the sake of justice!

entries.definition: Starting at the earliest point of an event or process.
entries.example: The instructions were clear from the very beginning.

entries.definition: To move to the other side of (something, such as an obstruction) by deviating from a direct course or following a curved path.
entries.example: The tide was too high, and we couldn't get around the rocks.

entries.definition: To obtain.
entries.example: However, a Carlisle newspaper got hold of the story, and at the half-yearly meeting of the Caledonian Railway Company, held on March 17, 1863, a shareholder, Mr. Meiklem, questioned the Chairman, Lt.-Col. Salkeld, regarding a "Chase of Engines," described in the newspaper article. The Chairman admitted that the statements made in the article were perfectly true.

entries.definition: To board and leave a vehicle.
entries.example: Passengers may get on and off the bus at any marked stop.

entries.definition: To board or mount (something), especially a vehicle.
entries.example: Please get on the bus as quickly as possible.

entries.definition: To reach or arrive at (a physical or abstract destination, or state of doing a certain activity).
entries.example: I’ll call you when I get to the railway station.

entries.definition: Deliver a particular formal speech.
entries.example: The president will give the speech after the awards are announced.

entries.definition: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see go, for.
entries.example: I'll go for some milk.

entries.definition: To move or spread from person to person.
entries.example: The rumor is going around that Mr. X and Ms. Y are having an affair. There's a cough going around.

entries.definition: To get or drink a coffee, often quickly or informally.
entries.example: Let's grab a coffee before the next lecture.

entries.definition: To distribute; to give out, either by hand or as if so (figuratively).
entries.example: Near-synonyms: give out, pass out, send out

entries.definition: To experience difficulty with someone or something.
entries.example: I am having trouble with the online payment system.

entries.definition: To discover, pinpoint; to think up; to realize.
entries.example: He hit on a great idea for improving the design.

entries.definition: Very soon or after a short period of time.
entries.example: I will call you back in a moment.

entries.definition: To allow for the possibility that.
entries.example: I'll take an umbrella, in case it rains.

entries.definition: Fashionable, in style.
entries.example: Disco went out of style in the 1980s, but is now in fashion again.

entries.definition: Suitable or appropriate; keeping with expectations, norms, ideals, or rules.
entries.example: "[Plant] rescues are usually organized by local garden clubs, but before you grab your shovel and head for the door, check with local government agencies to make sure you're in line with regulations."

entries.definition: Especially, individually or specifically.
entries.example: Mr. Cooke at once began a tirade against the residents of Asquith for permitting a sandy and generally disgraceful condition of the roads. So roundly did he vituperate the inn management in particular, and with such a loud flow of words, that I trembled lest he should be heard on the veranda.

entries.definition: With one's own body and physical presence; not through media, a representative, or indirectly.
entries.example: Have you ever seen a celebrity in person?

entries.definition: Concerning; about.
entries.example: I am writing in regard to the advertisement that you placed in last week's Daily News.

entries.definition: [Of one variable or unit of measurement which has a known relationship to another] Using equivalent expressions that use one variable in place of expressions involving the other.
entries.example: If x=2y then 5x can be expressed in terms of y as 10y.

entries.definition: To dine at a restaurant or such public place.
entries.example: Jacky wanted Korean barbecue, but his mom didn't want to eat out.

entries.definition: To bring to a conclusion.
entries.example: The band usually ends up their concerts with their biggest hit song.

entries.definition: To go into something by falling.
entries.example: The cat might fall into the pool if you're not careful.

entries.definition: To come to understand; to discover or find a solution; to deduce.
entries.example: As soon as I figure out what is wrong with my car, I will fix it.

entries.definition: To complete a form or questionnaire with requested information.
entries.example: Please fill out this application if you are interested in the job.

entries.definition: To provide (someone) with something; to furnish.
entries.example: I need someone to fix me up with a tent and some camping gear.

entries.definition: From another country.
entries.example: Many of the conference speakers have travelled from abroad.

entries.definition: Synonym of in general; generally.
entries.example: Generally speaking, today's teenagers aren't much interested in hearing about historical details of typewriter design.

entries.definition: To contact or reach someone, especially after trying.
entries.example: I finally got hold of the landlord by phone.

entries.definition: To become physically fitter or better prepared for an activity.
entries.example: She joined the gym to get into shape.

entries.definition: To proceed with; to begin or continue, especially after an interruption.
entries.example: Turn off the television and get on with your homework.

entries.definition: Become unable to move or progress.
entries.example: The car got stuck in deep mud.

entries.definition: To treat something as more important or deal with it before other things.
entries.example: The council will give priority to urgent housing repairs.

entries.definition: To travel from one end of something to the other.
entries.example: The train went through the tunnel.

entries.definition: To worsen; to fail or go amiss; to have a bad outcome.
entries.example: Everything seems to be going very badly wrong today.

entries.definition: To talk briefly with someone, often about a serious or private matter.
entries.example: Could I have a word with you after the meeting?

entries.definition: Find an activity difficult to do.
entries.example: She has difficulty understanding fast speech.
entries.usage: Have difficulty doing is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.

entries.definition: To argue with someone or speak angrily to them.
entries.example: She had words with her neighbour about the loud music.
entries.usage: Sb. stands for somebody; have a word with someone usually means a brief conversation instead.

entries.definition: Of or pertaining to a type of bus tour that allows passengers to join and leave at a number of different stops.
entries.example: A hop-on hop-off bus tour lets you explore several stops at your own pace.

entries.definition: In general terms without giving many specific details.
entries.example: In broad terms, the plan aims to reduce waste.

entries.definition: When compared with another person or thing.
entries.example: In comparison with last year, sales are much higher.

entries.definition: Alternative spelling of in favor of.
entries.example: With financial losses emerging in 1957, the BTC abandoned the diesel pilot scheme in favour of wholesale orders for untried designs.

entries.definition: Working for a particular employer.
entries.example: He had three assistants in his employ.
entries.usage: A formal or somewhat old-fashioned expression.

entries.definition: During the busiest periods.
entries.example: Travel costs rise in peak times.
entries.usage: At peak times or during peak periods is more idiomatic than in peak times.

entries.definition: In an original position.
entries.example: The tiles are still in place after the renovation.

entries.definition: Despite, irrespective of, notwithstanding.
entries.example: No evening I had passed at Bly had the portentous quality of this one; in spite of which—and in spite also of the deeper depths of consternation that had opened beneath my feet—there was literally, in the ebbing actual, an extraordinarily sweet sadness.

entries.definition: In the fact that; in the sense that; for the cause or reason that; because; in its being the case that; inasmuch as.
entries.example: This essay is a good one in that it comprehensively outlines all the major arguments on this issue.

entries.definition: To give something to a responsible person.
entries.example: I found a wallet on the street, so I handed it in to the police.

entries.definition: Included among the items named in a list.
entries.example: Her name appears in the list of successful applicants.

entries.definition: approximately equivalent to; around; close to (a determinate figure or vale)
entries.example:
17 September 1980, Geoffrey Howe, Letter regarding Welsh Language TV
If we had to deduct the full net cost of the Welsh language service from the levy on the ITV companies, this would be an unwelcome addition to the PSBR, which I understand your officials put at somewhere in the region of £10 million a year.

entries.definition: One after the other; one at a time; in succession; successively.
entries.example: The teacher answered the students each in turn.

entries.definition: To plan or mean to do something.
entries.example: I intend to submit the application before Friday.

entries.definition: To exercise regularly to maintain physical fitness.
entries.example: She walks every day to keep fit.

entries.definition: To continue moving or working at a particular speed.
entries.example: The runners kept up the pace until the final kilometre.

entries.definition: To hit or collide with
entries.example: As I took the can off the shelf, I knocked down the one beside it.

entries.definition: A large amount or number of something.
entries.example: There were loads of people at the outdoor concert.
entries.usage: Informal; a lot of is neutral in tone.

entries.definition: To follow with the eyes; to look in the direction of (someone or something departing).
entries.example: The marshes were just a long black horizontal line then, as I stopped to look after him; and the river was just another horizontal line, not nearly so broad nor yet so black; and the sky was just a row of long angry red lines and dense black lines intermixed.

entries.definition: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see look, through.
entries.example: He looked through the binoculars at the bird.

entries.definition: To formally request money, compensation, or another entitlement.
entries.example: You can make a claim on your insurance after the theft.
entries.usage: The phrase can also mean asserting that something is true; the insurance sense is used here.

entries.definition: To write something down so it will be remembered.
entries.example: Make a note of the room number before you leave.

entries.definition: Try hard to do something.
entries.example: Please make an effort to arrive on time.

entries.definition: To decide; to reach a conclusion.
entries.example: I can't make up my mind whether to have ice cream or cake.

entries.definition: To achieve a specified goal or required level.
entries.example: The sales team worked together to meet its monthly target.

entries.definition: Not even a tiny bit; not in any way.
entries.example: He's not at all friendly towards his ex-wife.

entries.definition: Having a streak of good luck or good progress or success.
entries.example: He was on a roll with the answers that day and didn't want to stop.

entries.definition: Displayed or written on a board.
entries.example: The exam timetable is on the board outside the office.

entries.definition: Placed where people can see or examine it.
entries.example: The winning photographs are on display in the foyer.

entries.definition: When someone asks for something.
entries.example: Extra towels are available on request.

entries.definition: Punctual or according to schedule; at the planned time.
entries.example: Unless our train's not on time, we'll be home at three.

entries.definition: Unaided; without assistance or help from others.
entries.example: A seven-year-old can get dressed on his own, but it might take a long time.

entries.definition: Indicating duty or obligation.
entries.example: You ought to tell the tutor if you cannot attend the class.

entries.definition: A contract where one party pays money and supplies goods or services, and the other supplies goods or services in exchange.
